Rocio Concha, Which? director of policy and advocacy, said: “Fraud takes a serious toll on victims’ stress levels and mental health as well as their finances, and many were left too ashamed to tell the people closest to them.

“Despite the financial harm and human misery they cause, we believe that the tech giants who profit from scams on their platforms will not take enough action against fraudsters unless they are legally compelled to do so.”

Deltapoll carried out the survey of fraud victims in June.

A spokesperson for Meta told Which?: “Scammers are determined criminals who use increasingly sophisticated tactics to defraud people and evade detection on our platforms and across the internet.

“We fight scams on and off our platforms because they’re not good for us or the people and businesses that rely on our services.”

A spokesperson for Ofcom told the consumer group: “Combating online fraud is a priority for us, and we’re working at pace to implement new rules on paid-for fraudulent ads.”

The spokesperson said tech firms “don’t have to wait – they can start making improvements for their users now.

“Sites and apps that fail to meet their legal duties, once in force, can expect to face serious consequences.”

News.title: Man City survive tunnel clash and Porto fury thanks to Haaland double
News.content:
Enzo Maresca takes charge of his first Champions League game in charge of Manchester City as they have travelled to Portugal to take on Porto at the Estadio do Dragao. These sides last met during the Champions League group stages during the 2020/21 season. Manchester City won 3-1 at home before the two sides drew 0-0 in this stadium.

Manchester City were busy late on in the transfer window, bringing in both Iliman Ndiaye and Enzo Fernandez as they spent nearly £200m on deadline day alone. They come into tonight’s game off the back of three straight Premier League victories to kick off the Maresca era. Maresca has limited Champions League experience as a manager, which came with Chelsea last season. Manchester City have won their opening game of a Champions League campaign in six of the last seven seasons but this will be the first time since 2015/16 that Manchester City embark on a Champions League campaign without Pep Guardiola at the helm.

“It is a hard place to come [Porto],” said Maresca. “They have started really well. In the last 14/15 games in Europe they lost just one, that shows a difficult place to come, but we will try our best and try to win the game. It is a very, very good team. They have different players, but in terms of the team it is very clear in the way they play. They are aggressive without the ball and on the ball, they have a clear style. But we will try our best and try to win the game. The ambition is the same; try to be ourselves and to win games and then we will see.”

Porto, managed by Francesco Farioli, have won every league game so far this season and already sit four points clear at the summit of Liga Portugal. Farioli takes charge of his first game as a manger in the Champions League and the club make their return to the elite European competition after two seasons away.

“We are going to face one of the big favourites to win the competition,” Farioli said. “It will be a game that will demand that we be at our best, and we know that whenever we step onto the Dragão pitch, something special can happen. I am happy to be in the Champions League for the first time at 37 years old. This will be my first game, but we approach every game with the same attention to detail and the same focus. It is easy for the players to be motivated tomorrow [tonight]. But the key will be our strategy and our ability to execute it, individually and collectively.”

Porto were in the Europa League last season, making it to the quarter-finals, where they were knocked out by Nottingham Forest 2-1 on aggregate. The omens would not appear to be on Porto’s side tonight; they have only won two of their last 16 games against English opposition in major European competition.

Team news from Portugal to follow shortly.

News.title: Newcastle scrape past Millwall to extend Jaissle’s unbeaten start
News.content:
Joe Willock’s deft finish ensured Newcastle United survived a tough test against Millwall to keep their excellent run in the Carabao Cup intact.

This competition had been fruitful for Newcastle under former manager Eddie Howe and although this match was hard work – as well as hard to watch at times – his successor Matthias Jaissle guided them through a difficult trip to south-east London.

He called it “job done,” and that was pretty much all it was. “We needed patience on one hand, but also to be passionate and tough. We had the chance [to score] and took it,” he said.

Newcastle have reached the semi-finals of this competition three times in the last four years, but struggled to get any sort of tempo going against their Championship opponents.

You could argue the winning goal came against the run of play late in the second half, moments after Millwall substitute Taïryk Arconte had smashed a low shot against the post.

News.title: Villa end goal drought to finally give Emery’s new era lift-off
News.content:
Unai Emery is building Aston Villa 2.0 and this was a night when his new kids on the block produced clear signs of lift-off for the next chapter.

Emery always springs into life on European nights and his reconstructed team secured their first win and goals of the season to leave Villa’s 1,700 fans singing in the rain.

Ten summer signings have arrived during a summer of upheaval which included plenty of high-profile departures after the club’s Europa League triumph in May.

Yet this was an evening that will have further energised Emery on his return to the Champions League.

Nicolas Jackson, Zion Suzuki and João Gomes embody this new Villa team and all stood out here in Bruges.

Record £65m signing Jackson’s fine individual goal proved to be the winner to settle a chaotic, absorbing contest with the Belgian Pro League champions.

News.title: Bird flu threatens French foie gras amid new duck cull
News.content:
The latest cull - like previous ones - was undertaken to protect both animal and human health.

Ducks are killed to stop the spread of the disease between farms, as well as to protect the health of farmers and minimise the risk of the virus mutating.

It is thought foie gras itself does not pose a risk to human health, even if it came from a bird-flu-infected duck, because it is almost always heat-treated before it is sold, which effectively destroys the virus, according to Public Health France.

“The consumption of meat, foie gras and eggs – and more generally of any food product based on poultry – presents no risk to humans,” said a spokesman for the Maine-et-Loire prefecture.

Veterinary experts say ducks are especially problematic regarding H5N1 because they can carry the virus without showing symptoms and have been described as the Chevaux de Troie or “Trojan horses” of bird flu.

It is unclear how the birds in the latest outbreak, located on a farm in Longué-Jumelles, contracted the virus, although it is typically spread by wild birds which shed the virus through their droppings.

It is for this reason that British poultry were forced into lockdown or “flockdown” from late October to April of this year.

This included so-called “free-range” birds, which, as the Telegraph reported in November continued to be described as free-range despite never seeing the light of day under a dispensation given by the Department for Environment, Food, and Rural Affairs (DEFRA).

Ducks reared for foie gras typically spend the first 90 days of their lives being reared in their tens of thousands in barns with very little access to natural light.

Animal rights campaigners say most never see water.

They then are put through a rigorous 12-16 day “fattening up” period where they are force-fed through a tube to significantly enlarge their livers, before being slaughtered.

While France introduced a vaccination programme to protect its duck population from bird flu in 2023, the jabs do not entirely stop the virus from getting into a flock.

Data collected by the French Agency for Food, Environmental and Occupational Health & Safety suggested that between 50 and 55 per cent of the country’s ducks are unvaccinated at any given time, due to a 20-day gap between the first and second dose of the vaccine and waning immunity over time.

The ducks subject to the latest bird-flu cull in Western France had received their first dose of the H5N1 vaccine, but not the second, meaning they were not fully protected, according to the disease monitoring firm Airfinity.

The threat to France’s £2 billion foie gras industry comes amid increasing global competition.

Once the dominant producer, it is now being challenged by China, which has rapidly scaled up its output of the delicacy and now accounts for 45 per cent of global production.

A tin of Chinese foie gras costs roughly £3.70, while a typical tin of French foie gras made from duck liver costs between £10 and £15. French foie gras produced from Geese costs anywhere between £70 and £150.

China is also said to operate a more rigorous poultry vaccination programme, according to an analysis by DEFRA.

It applies to all farmed birds in the country, which has managed to keep outbreaks of bird flu on farms relatively low compared with European levels.

The H5N1 avian flu pandemic has now been running for six years and has decimated flocks of farmed chickens and turkeys across the globe.

In the UK alone, more than five million farmed birds have been culled since 2021, costing an estimated £48 million in farmers’ compensation alone.

Last week, the virus was detected on a mink farm in the US state of Utah.

Minks in captivity have previously been described as pandemic “time bombs”. The size and density of fur farms – where thousands of the animals are crammed together in tight proximity – give invading viruses a perfect environment in which to mutate.

The virus has also done huge damage to wild birds and other animals. In South America alone, more than 600,000 wild seabirds have died since 2022.

Dozens of other mammals have been infected and died across the globe, including foxes, otters, sea lions, bears, and seals.

In June, the virus was found in Australia for the first time – the last continent on earth to record a case – and the government has since launched a vaccination programme to protect the country’s rare species, including birds like orange-bellied parrots and black cockatoos.

Scientists have long warned that if H5N1 gains the mutations necessary to spread between people, it could trigger a human-pandemic, something that would be of “enormous concern”, according to the World Health Organization (WHO), given the virus’s 50 per cent case fatality rate.

News.title: The Chancellor’s speech, as it happened
News.content:
John Healey failed to rule out tax rises at next month’s Budget in his first major speech as Chancellor.

Mr Healey also sought to blame Liz Truss and her mini-Budget in 2022 for the high borrowing costs being paid by the Treasury.

During a speech in Coventry, the Chancellor said he would be “honest” about the need to control public spending during his time in Number 11.

He was speaking days after the cost of government borrowing hit its highest level since 2007.

It was also overshadowed by Jaguar Land Rover announcing plans to cut 4,000 jobs in the face of “intense competition and ongoing geopolitical uncertainty”.

Read our report on the Chancellor’s speech.

News.title: Maitland-Niles’ last-gasp debut goal salvages Everton’s miserable week
News.content:
At the final whistle, the first song the stadium DJ played was Spirit of the Blues and how those relieved Evertonians lapped it up after a week of angst.

Their team had been on the precipice of a defeat that would have exacerbated all the frustrations that bubbled away following the chaotic conclusion to the transfer window. Indeed, it was 10 seconds over the allotted five minutes of added time when the ball fell to Ainsley Maitland-Niles.

It had been three years since the former Arsenal full-back had played in the Premier League – his last goal in England was on October 30, 2019, in an EFL Cup tie with Liverpool at Anfield that ended 5-5 – and he would not have joined Everton if their attempt to sign Kenny Tete from Fulham had not failed.

But here he was 30 yards from goal, with no need to break his stride as Manchester United’s backtracking defenders presented him with an invitation to shoot. So that’s what he did. With one perfectly timed swish of his right foot, an unlikely hero transformed the mood of a club.

News.title: Arsenal teach Chelsea a lesson in how to be champions
News.content:
This is how champions are supposed to play and, although the Arsenal home support have not seen a team defend their place at the apex of English league football for two decades, they knew it when they saw it.

The chase was on for Mikel Arteta’s team within two minutes when Morgan Rogers, the man who might have moved to Arsenal this summer, put his new club Chelsea in the lead. So unfolded a thrilling 100 minutes of Premier League competition. Arsenal were the better team in terms of ambition and attack even if one could not discount Chelsea until the very last moment.

Others might have crumbled. That Chelsea did not will give Xabi Alonso hope for a team that did not feature the injured Moisés Caicedo and is now without the departed Enzo Fernández. Yet he will also recognise that his childhood friend from San Sebastián in the other dugout has created a side that treated the game, and their place in it, with an urgency that looks different. The first two minutes might have been ragged for Arsenal but after that they did not let the game happen to them.

Sports.title: ‘I can’t see him not scoring 1,000 goals’ – Jamie Carragher backs Erling Haaland to be greatest goalscorer of all time
Sports.content:
JAMIE CARRAGHER has backed Erling Haaland to become the greatest goalscorer of all time.

The Manchester City striker was on target yet again against Porto in the Champions League.



Haaland, 26, netted a brace during the 2-0 victory and became City’s third-highest scorer of all time.

He took his record for the club to 167 in just 203 appearances for the club since his move from Borussia Dortmund.



His two goals also meant that his record in the Champions League stands at 59 games and 59 goals.

In total, Haaland has already scored a staggering 366 goals in 445 appearances in his club and international career.

Haaland’s remarkable goalscoring feat has earned him huge praise from Carragher.

The Liverpool legend was discussing the Norwegian’s talents on CBS Sports after City’s win over Porto.

Carragher, 48, believes that Haaland is capable of going on to hit quadruple digits in goals before the end of his playing days.

He said: “I just can’t see Haaland not scoring 1,000 goals or being the best goalscorer of all time.

“It just feels like a normal night.

Sports.title: Glamorous Eva Murati stuns in little black dress as fans hail return of ‘the Queen of the Champions League’
Sports.content:
GLAMOROUS football presenter Eva Murati has stunned in a little black dress.

Fans have hailed the 31-year-old’s return as she presents on the Champions League.



The Albanian presenter has taken to Instagram to share a behind-the-scenes look at her football coverage.

Murati has shared a social media video of herself walking into the Tring Sport studio, starting with a close-up of her silver heels.



Wider shots then show the presenter wearing a short black dress to present the iconic tournament.

She paired the video with Tony Britten’s instantly-recognisable UEFA Champions League Anthem.



The Champions League host has been widely compared to Laura Woods, 39, for her Albanian coverage of the tournament.

Murati listed the Champions League opening night’s fixtures as she asked her 1.4million followers an important question.

The presenter captioned the post: “Six games. One very loud night in Europe. Which one are you watching?”

She previously wowed fans wearing a tiny lilac dress for her coverage of the Champions League qualifiers last month.



Murati first made her mark on football as a teenager when she was cast in a spot for Eagle Mobile during coverage of Euro 2012.

She then started hosting the Champions League in January 2017, after previous hosting duties on Albanian primetime television.

Her latest post has gained significant attention, with fans hailing “‘the Queen of the Champions League” returning for another season.



One fan said: “I’m very happy that you’re back in the Champions League again!”

Another shared: “This is gonna be amazing!!”

A third fan commented: “My favourite journalist.”

Sports.title: Entire stand of 81,000-seat stadium left virtually empty for Champions League clash after just 39 away fans buy tickets
Sports.content:
ONE section of Borussia Dortmund’s Signal Iduna Park was left completely empty after just 39 Villarreal supporters bought tickets in the away end.

The sides faced each other tonight to kick-off their Champions League campaigns.



Villarreal had next to no one cheering them on, while Dortmund had a huge 77,000 backing them.

And it would have been more if it wasn’t for Uefa’s rules regarding away allocations.



The visiting side must be given 5% of tickets.

Therefore the entire north-east corner of the stadium has remained empty tonight, after Dortmund relocated the 39 Villarreal faithfuls to the West Stand.

Considering they come from a city of just 54,000 people, it’s tough to blame Villarreal fans for not making the trip.

The lack of Spaniards in the ground points to the overall lack of away support culture in the Spanish game.

For years Spanish teams have brought noticeably less away fans than clubs from the rest of Europe.

Dortmund have been known for rocking atmospheres and the infamous Yellow Wall behind the goal at their huge home ground.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Their support, and the lack of away noise, helped spur their team on to a positive start in the Champions League, despite a worrying injury to one of their stars early on.

Despite being goalless at half-time, the clash finished 3-1 to the hosts.

An own-goal from former Chelsea defender Renato Veiga gave the home side the lead early in the second half, before Santiago Mourino equalised soon after.

Guinean striker Serhou Guirassy then found himself heavily involved in the closing stages of the clash.

He scored two in the space of four minutes to give his side a 3-1 lead late in the game.



The 30-year-old then thought he’d help out at the other end too, as he banged in an own-goal to send the 39 Villarreal fans wild.

Sports.title: Inside Arsenal star Riccardo Calafiori’s incredible summer backpacking trip to get over World Cup heartbreak
Sports.content:
RICCARDO CALAFIORI went backpacking this summer to get over the pain of missing out on the World Cup.

Italy failed to qualify for football’s biggest party for the third tournament in a row and the Arsenal defender couldn’t bear to watch.



Instead, he and his friends went travelling around South America, taking in the sights of Argentina, Rio de Janeiro and the waterfalls of the Iguazu River.

It was exactly the sort of holiday you would expect from Calafiori, who plays football with a youthful joy and freedom.



The Italian, 24, is Arsenal’s left-back, but that is his position in name only.

The reality is that he is far more than that and routinely pops up in attacking areas to cause chaos.

His touch map often resembles a Jackson Pollock painting and in four games this season, Calafiori already has two assists and a goal.

It is why Mikel Arteta will be tempted to start him on Wednesday in Naples as Arsenal kick off their Champions League campaign.

Piero Hincapie could easily come into the team in place of the Italian, but he does not offer the same attacking threat.

Former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher has hailed Calafiori as the best left-back in the Premier League right now and it is hard to argue with that.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

No one else is able to have such an influence at both ends of the pitch and Arteta stressed that after Calafiori’s goal against Manchester City in the Community Shield last month.

The Arsenal boss said: “He can be a total player. We can ask him to occupy certain areas of the pitch.

“And when he gets in and around the box he has this intuition, his timing to create goals and to score goals.

“But at the same time we ask him to do the defensive duties what he has to do, and we ask him because he’s capable of doing it.

“He knows how to do it, and if we keep him fit and available and with that physical condition, he’s a top player.”



Those in Italy will be intrigued to see Calafiori in action as he is very different from the player that left these shores two years ago.

The defender was viewed then as a centre-back and he still plays there for the national side when called upon.

But few would have predicted the 24-year-old transforming into a rampaging full-back who occupies a role no one else in world football really does.



Arteta has always placed great value on the left-back in his systems, and Oleksandr Zinchenko four years ago revolutionised the way Arsenal play.

The Ukrainian tucked into midfield so the Gunners could dominate possession and it very nearly led them to the title in the 2022-23 season.

Calafiori’s role is far more advanced than that and he is basically an additional No10 at times, or even an extra striker.



That was actually where he played as a youngster and clearly some of those traits are still with him.

The defender took his goal against City in the Community Shield with all the composure of a veteran striker and he has benefitted from a full break this summer.

Calafiori said: “Obviously from one side, I was sad because I couldn’t go to the World Cup.

“But from the other side, I so badly wanted to do this trip around South America and finally I’ve done it.

“It was unbelievable. You need to live it, to feel it, to be there and even in pictures it is not the same.”



After exploring South America, the hope for Calafiori is now that he has plenty of European trips with Arsenal this season.

The Gunners suffered agony in May as they lost the Champions League final to Paris Saint-Germain on penalties.

The squad is stronger now, though, and Arteta could make plenty of changes against Napoli.



Eberechi Eze and Bruno Guimaraes were unused substitutes in Sunday’s win over Chelsea, but could easily start tonight.

Viktor Gyokeres is another in need of minutes having played less than half an hour this season.

It sums up the embarrassment of riches that Arteta has at his disposal with Calafiori, perhaps, the crown jewel.

Sports.title: Porto 0 Man City 2: Haaland goes third on City’s all-time scoring list to seal three points in Champions League opener
Sports.content:
MAYBE head boy Erling Haaland should keep his hair short permanently now.

The Manchester City forward suggested this week he will grow his locks long again after getting it all chopped off at the start of the season.



But he certainly hasn’t been shorn of his powers. With his new buzz cut he has scored three headers in four matches at the start of the season.

Actually he could have scored a hat-trick with his bonce here and will probably be kicking himself that he didn’t.



However he got the one that mattered, nodding a cross by new boy Enzo Fernandez in off the post to finally beat inspired home keeper Diogo Costa.

And in stoppage time he slid in a second – this time with his feet – to settle any nerves.

It puts him third on City’s all-time goalscoring list – and also helped his boyhood favourites to lay a few ghosts to rest.

The Dragao does not hold happy memories for City fans – it was in this stadium that they lost their first ever Champions League final five years ago.

To make it worse, they went into that one as hot favourites against Thomas Tuchel’s Chelsea but a combination of Pep Guardiola selection and some below par performances proved their undoing.

That came in a period when City regularly reached the latter stages of this competition – and it proved to be the springboard for them to win it two years later.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

However in the last couple of years under Pep, their European campaigns tailed off as they failed to make it past the last 16 in either.

Their form on the road has been a particular concern as prior to this they had lost six of their last nine away games in Europe.

This was no easy take either against the newly crowned Portuguese champs who have started the current campaign with six straight domestic wins.



So the first task for City was to quieten the home crowd who were up for this one after a two year absence from Uefa biggest stage.

Francesco Farioli’s side had the first opportunity as Gabri Veiga shot turned behind at his near by Gianluigi Donnarumma – although the flag had gone up so it may not have counted.

Yet gradually City started to get a grip on the game with new midfielders Enzo Fernandez and Ayyoub Bouaddi showing their quality.

In truth the visitors – and star striker Erling Haaland in particular – should have put the game to bed and claimed the match ball by half time.

The first big chance came when Phil Foden linked up brilliantly with Antoine Semenyo down the left and chipped a perfect cross to the far post.



Haaland got a good connection on his header and looked certain to score but Diogo Costa got across to push it over the bar superbly.

A few minutes later Semenyo – who created Haaland’s winner against Coventry on Saturday – was at it again but this time the Norwegian flicked a header too high.

Foden – whose horse Wreck it Ronnie won at Goodwood earlier in the day – had the chance to make it a double celebration as he raced onto Rayan Cherki’s pass but Costa got down to save.



A low cross from the right found its way to Haaland whose volley was tipped away by Costa who then picked himself up to help smother the rebound from Cherki.

The Portugal number one – who has regularly been linked with a move to the Prem – is considered to be Porto’s star man.

And in this first half, it was easy to see why. He had kept his team in it almost single handedly kept his team in it.

Yet no doubt Costa – like every goalkeeper in Europe – knows you can’t keep giving Haaland chances and get away with it.



The first half ended in a storm as Porto were furious with Marc Guehi’s challenge on Gabri Veiga – that left the Porto man on the deck.

Players and staff from both teams were involved in a tunnel bust-up as they returned to the dressing room.

Yet City had regained their composure at the start of the second half and finally took the lead within a couple of minutes.

Cherki cleverly kept an attack alive and found Fernandez who hung up a cross to the back post.



This time Haaland got his header right – sending it back across Costa and in off the far post.

He revealed his love of chopping wood and burning it recently – and here he was cutting the Portuguese champions down to size.

Porto had their best spell of the game after falling behind with Donnarumma’s clearance hitting William Gomes but the deflection rolled agonisingly wide.

But for all their spirit there was no way back and Haaland sealed it when he got on the end of sub Rayan Ait Nouri’s cross and slid a low effort past Costa.

That’s four wins from four for new boss Enzo Maresca ahead of this weekend’s Manchester derby.



It was another landmark for the Norwegian – he goes third on City’s all-time list of goalscorers going past Tommy Johnson’s tally of 166.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

And to think he’s only been at the club for just over four years.

The Etihad faithful know he is head and shoulders above the rest no matter how long his hair is.

Sports.title: Erling Haaland in furious bust-up with Porto star as brawl breaks out for SECOND time in fiesty Champions League clash
Sports.content:
ERLING HAALAND has been caught in a furious bust-up during Manchester City’s Champions League clash.

A second brawl broke out in the game as Haaland scrapped with Porto‘s Pablo Rosario in the 92nd minute.



Play was stopped by the referee, withhime rushing to break the stars apart as City led 2-0 in their opening game of the Champions League.

Haaland appeared on top of Rosario as the pair pulled at each other’s jerseys on the grass.



Players from both sides then came rushing in to offer their support as referee Szymon Marciniak was bounced around by players.

It came just one minute after Haaland secured his second goal of the game.



Referee Marciniak then brandished yellow cards for both Haaland and Rosario before the final seconds of Manchester City‘s win played out.

Yellow cards had also been issued earlier in the game to the visitors’ Josko Gvardiol and Gianluigi Donnarumma.

This was the second scrappy incident of the game, with Porto midfielder Gabri Veiga left covered in blood just minutes before half-time.

Veiga had caught a wry elbow to the head from Marc Guehi, as the City and England defender escaped punishment after a VAR check.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

But the drama did not end there as a scuffle broke out between players as they walked down the tunnel for half-time.

Forward Haaland made a quick start to the second half as he handed Manchester City the lead after a well-placed cross from Enzo Fernandez.

He then secured the first-round victory by completing his brace in stoppage time.



Haaland is now City’s third-top all-time goalscorer following his latest Champions League efforts.

Manchester City will next head to Old Trafford to face Manchester United in the Premier League on Sunday.

Sports.title: Real Madrid 2 Inter Milan 1: Spanish giants edge swashbuckling clash to get Mourinho off to a flier in Champions League
Sports.content:
CLINICAL Real Madrid put on a Jose Mourinho masterclass to get their Champions League campaign off to a perfect start.

It was 2010 when Mourinho showed the world how compact defending and low possession could still win Europe’s biggest prizes as he lifted the Champions League as Inter Milan boss.



That was Mourinho’s final game as Inter chief, and 16 years later, he rolled back the years by showing his former club those old tricks still work.

Inter dominated the ball and the best of the chances, but it was Mourinho’s Madrid that showed their patience to pounce when it mattered most.



The Italian visitors should perhaps have known better, given manager Cristian Chivu played under Mourinho in that Champions League final all those years ago, but Madrid’s quality felt inevitable.

Real Madrid came into the game off the back of their first defeat of the new Mourinho era, a bruising 1-0 defeat to Real Betis last weekend.



And there was a new-look midfield for Los Blancos, as Trent Alexander-Arnold was given a run out in the middle of the park.

The opening exchanges saw Inter run riot over the hosts, notching four shots within 11 minutes.

Marcus Thuram saw his close-range effort parried away by Thibaut Courtois, while Lautaro Martinez also stung the former Belgian stopper’s gloves from inside the box.

It looked like the tide was well in Inter’s favour, that was, until a sloppy mistake at the back gifted Real Madrid an opening goal.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Brahim Diaz picked the pocket of Yann Bisseck after a hospital pass from Curtis Jones.

Diaz played in Kylian Mbappe to slide home the first goal completely against the run of play.

It felt as if it had come out of nowhere, but it was exactly what Jose Mourinho would expect – his patient side showing their class in the decisive moments.

And despite Inter testing Courtois twice more in the minutes that followed, Madrid doubled their lead through another costly mistake on 23 minutes.



Inter goalkeeper Josep Martinez inexplicably tried to pull off a Cruyff turn inside his own six-yard box when being pressed by Federico Valvarde.

The Uruguayan midfielder got his foot to the ball and essentially tackled the ball into the back of the net.

Madrid had managed just two shots and had maintained only 29 per cent of possession, yet they found themselves 2-0 up.

It is exactly the football Mourinho has made a name for himself by playing, and the same style that won him his Champions League as Inter boss.

The goals knocked the confidence of Chivu’s Inter side, who needed to bring John Stones on at half time to try and steady the ship.



After an outrageously clinical first half, Madrid became almost wasteful in the second.

Chances went begging for Jude Bellingham, Mbappe and Vinicius, and Carlos Augusto’s 77th minute goal certainly changed the mood inside the Bernabeu.

Lautaro Martinez drilled a cross into the box, which Augusto fired past Courtois.

It meant Mourinho was forced further into leaning into his defensive game, replacing Alexander Arnold with Aurelien Tchouameni to see out the result.



The managerial great was unable to deliver Europe’s top prize during his first stint in Madrid, crashing out in the semi-finals in three consecutive seasons.

But if he can lean into the quality of his star-studded squad, the 63-year-old may just be able to squeeze one last dance in this season.But Mourinho’s men held on to get three points on the board.

But Mourinho was happy to earn three points, even admitting the game was “crazy”.

He said: “I liked the result, three points against a very strong team. A spectacular match for those watching at home, but not for me or for Chivu.

“It was a crazy match, it could have been 5-0 for us or 5-5 or 6-5 or 7-6. Inter could have scored before us, after us. We could have closed it out several times. But crazy match.”



Inter Milan striker Lautaro Martinez said his team can leave the Bernabeu with their heads held high, despite losing the game.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The Argentine said: “This is a competition of details: when you make mistakes, you pay the price. The two errors at the start, after having approached the match well, made everything difficult because they are a top-level team.

“But we came here with personality, they want to win the Champions League just like us. The disappointment is that we didn’t take enough shots and we weren’t able to take all the chances we had, but we’re leaving with our heads held high because we played a top-level match against a very strong opponent.”

Sports.title: ‘Got away with murder’ – Marc  Guehi leaves Porto ace covered with blood after stray elbow leading to huge tunnel brawl
Sports.content:
FANS have been left stunned after Marc Guehi “got away with murder” in Manchester City’s clash with Porto.

The defender caught Porto midfielder Gabri Veiga with a wild elbow while challenging for the ball.



The two teams were meeting in Portugal during the Champions League league phase.

In the first half of the match, City star Guehi went up for a header and caught Veiga with his elbow.



The midfielder came off much the worse of the two and was covered in blood as he lay on the pitch.

Guehi, 26, escaped any punishment from referee Szymon Marciniak but fans think that was wrong.



Many took to social media to claim that the England international should have seen a card.

One posted: “Marc Guehi absolutely clattered Gabri Veiga.”

A second commented: “Guehi has gotten away with murder there.”

A third wrote: “Guehi getting away with murder. Never change Uefa.”

A fourth said: “Guehi is lucky there. That is a dangerous challenge.”

Another added: “How is Guehi not getting a red card for this rash tackle?”

After a couple of minutes of treatment, Viega was able to continue and play resumed.



There were some hard feelings between the two teams after the half-time whistle blew.

City players and staff clashed with the Porto team as they headed towards the tunnel.

Security was called upon to separate the arguing sides from the brawl at the mouth of the tunnel.

Amazon Prime reporter Gabriel Clarke offered an insight into what occurred.

He said: “That anger triggered by the Veiga-Guehi incident, the pushing and the shoving, the bad-tempered behaviour, continued down the tunnel as the players came off for half-time.

Reports in the stadium claimed that the tunnel could be seen “shaking” during the ruckus between the teams.

Sports.title: Lionel Messi splashes out on second football club as 'full takeover agreement reached'
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi splashes out on second football club as 'full takeover agreement reached'

Lionel Messi could become the owner of another football club with a deal reportedly on the verge of being announced

View 2 Images Lionel Messi could be about to complete a full takeover of another club (Image: Megan Briggs/Getty Images)

Lionel Messi has reportedly agreed to complete a full takeover of a Spanish second division club, just over a week after announcing his retirement from international football. Messi, 39, is currently in the middle of his fourth season in Major League Soccer with Inter Miami, and already appears to have an eye on the future.

‌



The Barcelona legend helped Argentina reach the final of the World Cup in the summer, before his country suffered a 1-0 defeat to Spain in the showpiece match in New Jersey.

‌



Messi signed a new contract with Miami earlier this year that will run until the end of the 2028 MLS season, at which point the former Paris Saint-Germain will be 41 years old.

‌



A fresh report from Spain, meanwhile, has claimed that Messi is now venturing further into the world of club ownership, with a deal appearing to be close to completion to oversee a full takeover.

Diego Simeone makes honest Julian Alvarez admission ahead of Liverpool clash READ MORE :

Spanish publication AS has claimed that Messi is on the verge of acquiring a 100 per cent stake in La Liga 2 club CD Eldense, who are currently sat in the relegation zone.

It has been reported that an agreement has been reached for Messi to become the majority owner of the Spanish second-tier club, with his lawyers said to be holding talks with TH, a Colombian investment group.

‌



The report goes on to claim that an official announcement confirming the full takeover from Messi could happen within the next few days.

Should a deal get over the line, it would be the second club under Messi’s ownership, with the other being Cornella, which plays in the fifth tier of Spanish football.

It was just last month that Messi announced his retirement from international football, with his final match for Argentina being the defeat to Spain in the World Cup final in July.

‌

Messi announced his retirement just a few weeks after his father, Jorge, passed away, and posted an emotional message confirming his plan to no longer represent his country.

"After all this time that has passed since the final, and after much thought, I want to announce to everyone that I am retiring from the National Team,” Messi posted on Instagram.”It was a decision that hurt, and still hurts, to my core, but I understand that it's the right time.

‌



"I swear that I always gave my all, not just in the last few years when we won everything, but before that too. I always fought and gave everything for this jersey, to bring you joy and make you proud to be Argentinian through football.

"There's not much time left, and chapters are closing, and this is one that hurts me deeply. I love, loved, and will always love being on the National Team. I've given everything I have; I have nothing more to give, and besides, there are some great young players coming up behind me who deserve to be there.

View 2 Images Lionel Messi announced his retirement from international football last month (Image: Leonardo Fernandez/Getty Images)

"Thank you for all the love and support over these 20 years. I'm going to miss hearing you all from the inside so much. Now I'm going to be just one of you, cheering and supporting you from the sidelines (in good times and bad, even more so).

"Thank you to my family for always being there, for accompanying me on this beautiful but difficult journey. Thank you to each and every one of the coaches, teammates, and managers I had the privilege of working with. I take with me unforgettable memories and moments.”

‌



Messi continued: "I leave with the peace and pride of having given you, along with my teammates, dreamlike moments. It was incredible to have experienced it with you all. I love you!

"Thank you, God, for making me Argentinian. Go Argentina! I wrote these words on July 21st, two days after the final. Today, after what happened to my dad, I'm even more convinced than before."

Sports.title: Erling Haaland delivers again to help Man City survive Porto scare - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Erling Haaland delivers again to help Man City survive Porto scare - 5 talking points

PORTO 0-2 MAN CITY: A brace from Erling Haaland decided the game for Manchester City once again, as they took maximum points from their awkward Champions League opener

View 5 Images Manchester City are up and running in the Champions League (Image: PATRICIA DE MELO MOREIRA/AFP via Getty Images)

Manchester City got their Champions League campaign off to a winning start with a hard-fought 2-0 victory over Porto. Erling Haaland netted both goals in Portugal to make it five for the season, having also decided Saturday's win against Coventry.

‌



City returned to the scene of their Champions League final defeat to Chelsea in 2021 with a new man in the dugout. Enzo Maresca didn't have easy time watching his team toil in the the pouring rain, but they earned their fourth successive win under him.

‌



They were left frustrated in the first half, much thanks to the heroics of Diogo Costa. The Porto goalkeeper made a string of impressive saves, including two from Haaland to keep the Premier League giants at bay.

‌



But it didn't take long for City to break through at the start of the second period - and third time was a charm for Haaland, whose header hit the post before nestling in the back of the net. It was then backs to the wall until full-time, as Porto pushed for an equaliser before City's goalscorer supreme struck again.

Here are five talking points from the Estadio do Dragao.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

1. Haaland starts despite Maresca hint

Erling Haaland's daddy issues was the main talking point from Enzo Maresca's pre-match press conference on Monday. The City boss explained how Haaland, now bearing the responsibilities of being a father, will need to be rested at some point this season following a busy 2025-26 campaign which ended in a deep run at the World Cup with Norway, who made it to the quarter-finals.

With deadline-day arrival Iliman Ndiaye now at his disposal, would Maresca rotate his striker? No. The 26-year-old was named in the starting XI alongside £86million signing Ayyoub Bouaddi, who was handed his full debut in midfield next to Enzo Fernandez after a cameo against Coventry.

‌



Will Man City win the Champions League? Give us your prediction in the comments section.

View 5 Images Erling Haaland isn't being rested yet (Image: PATRICIA DE MELO MOREIRA/AFP via Getty Images)

2. VAR looks past Guehi incident

With the first half meandering to a close, City were flexing their muscles and causing Porto some discomfort. Marc Guehi did that quite literally when challenging Gabri Veiga for a bouncing ball, drawing blood from the Porto star's head.

‌



Guehi's arm wasn't outstretched but the hosts became incensed after watching replays of the incident on the touchline. Francesco Farioli suggested that the City centre-back had elbowed his midfielder.

Veiga received treatment for a good few minutes, giving VAR plenty of time to assess the collision. But nothing was given, allowing referee Szymon Marciniak to signal for the restart without going to the monitor.

But when Marciniak blew his whistle for half-time, he was greeted by deafening whistles from the home crowd. The Polish official was also swarmed by Porto players as he attempted to get down the tunnel.

‌



View 5 Images Gabriel Veiga took a heavy blow from Marc Guehi (Image: Clive Brunskill/Getty Images)

3. Who else but Haaland?

Need someone to break the deadlock? Call Erling Haaland.

The Norwegian has now scored the first goal in City's last three games. This time he easily beat Jakub Kiwior in the air and headed Fernandez's cross back the way it came, leaving Costa wrong-footed.

‌



It seemed to take an age for the ball to go in, but there was relief when it eventually did. The header marked Haaland's 58th Champions League goal - in just 59 games - taking him clear of Bayern Munich legend Thomas Muller.

View 5 Images Erling Haaland rose highest to give Manchester City the lead (Image: Miguel RIOPA/AFP via Getty Images)

4. No messing from Maresca

After going 1-0 up, City suddenly became vulnerable and sloppiness seeped - or flooded more accurately - into their performance. Their tendency to give possession cheaply away left Maresca furious in his technical area and he made a double substitution shortly after a poor passage of play.

‌



Rayan Cherki, twice the source of his manager's frustration, came off alongside Antoine Semenyo, who had a difficult night. Ndiaye and Elliot Anderson were their replacements as Porto smelled blood.

View 5 Images Enzo Maresca saw the danger coming (Image: PATRICIA DE MELO MOREIRA/AFP via Getty Images)

5. Dodgy Donnarumma

Although Maresca wasn't happy with his outfielders, it was his goalkeeper who nearly made two fatal mistakes. Gianluigi Donnarumma flattened Pepe in the 49th minute, and while the offside flag saved him from giving away a penalty, he was still booked for his challenge.

‌



Shortly after the hour mark, Donnarumma misjudged a pass which was played back to him and got chased down by William Gomes as he hurriedly attempted to clear his lines. Luckily for the Italian, his blocked clearance flew back towards goal but whizzed past the post.

Porto never properly tested the City No.1 in the closing stages, getting caught offside on numerous occasions despite their pace. And when Haaland made it 2-0 with a cool finish inside the penalty area, Maresca could breathe a sigh of relief after two narrow victories in four days ahead of the Manchester derby at Old Trafford this Sunday.

Sports.title: Gabriel Jesus reveals brutal Mikel Arteta call days before Arsenal exit was confirmed
Sports.content:
Gabriel Jesus reveals brutal Mikel Arteta call days before Arsenal exit was confirmed

Gabriel Jesus completed a surprise move from Arsenal to Barcelona over the closing days of the summer transfer window and he has now revealed how the move came about

View 2 Images Jesus made the move from Arsenal to Barcelona over the closing days of the window (Image: Getty Images)

Gabriel Jesus has admitted that he was made to train alone at Arsenal in the days leading up to his exit. The Brazilian striker left the Emirates Stadium at the end of the window as he completed a surprise switch to Spanish giants Barcelona.

‌



His move brought to an end an ultimately frustrating period in North London where Jesus won the Premier League, albeit injuries limited him to just 123 appearances over four years.

‌



In discussing his switch, Jesus has admitted that he was forced to train away from his teammates in the build up. Speaking to SportyTV, Jesus said: "So, the truth is, I was training, I did all the pre-season with Arsenal as normal.

‌



“Obviously, I knew already that probably I would not play there or get many opportunities, but nobody told me nothing.

"Well, I am a professional. Obviously I was training with the group. Then, from nothing, they put me to train away from the group.

‌



"Well, I was training, I was doing my maximum to be ready if I have a chance to play at a high level again. Then, obviously, in the last week it was very quick.

"The work with Deco, the president of the club, and my agent was amazing. In one day, it was sure that I would have the opportunity to come (to Barcelona). I said yes, straight away, no matter what and I am so happy to be here."

In the aftermath of Jesus’ move to the Camp Nou, Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta had some kind words to say. He said: "Gabi’s gone to Barcelona, which I take the opportunity as well to give him a huge thank you.

‌



View 2 Images Jesus made his Barcelona debut over the weekend (Image: Getty Images)

"He was a massive contributor for us to change the dynamic and the energy in and around this club. I think when Gabi came in he brought this energy, this belief within, this aura, that’s really helped achieve what happened next.

"And now, yeah, he has an amazing opportunity to enjoy one of the biggest clubs in the world, and a beautiful place to live as well, and we are happy for him.”

‌



Jesus, 29, has already made his debut for his new employers, having made a brief cameo in the 5-0 win against Valencia over the weekend. He could potentially make his second appearance on Wednesday evening as Barcelona take on Feyenoord in the Champions League.

In the meantime, Arsenal kick off their latest European campaign against Italian giants Napoli. The Gunners will certainly be aiming to go one further this year, having lost out to Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League final last term.

Sports.content:
Eight players could miss Liverpool vs Atletico Madrid as Cody Gakpo absent from training

Liverpool will be without several key players when they take on Atletico Madrid in the Champions League on Wednesday night, with injuries and squad decisions set to limit both sides

View 2 Images Cody Gakpo has emerged as an injury concern for Liverpool (Image: Liverpool FC/Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

‌



Andoni Iraola oversaw his first win as Liverpool boss last week, with the Merseyside outfit securing a 2-0 victory away at Ipswich Town in the Premier League, with Alexander Isak scoring both goals at Portman Road.

‌



Iraola and Liverpool have seen several members of their squad be unavailable in the early weeks of the season, and that will still be the case when they face Atletico in Europe on Wednesday evening.

‌



Cody Gakpo is an doubt for Liverpool after the Netherlands international missed training on Tuesday, although his absence was understood to be as a precaution rather than something which will definitely rule him out.

Sports.title: Peter Schmeichel snubs Man Utd stars as he names signing of the season
Sports.content:
Peter Schmeichel snubs Man Utd stars as he names signing of the season

Manchester United splashed the cash this summer ahead of Michael Carrick’s first full season at the helm but it appears Peter Schmeichel is more impressed by another club’s business

View 2 Images Peter Schmeichel is a big fan of Emi Martinez's arrival at Chelsea (Image: Getty Images)

Peter Schmeichel says Emi Martinez could go on to become the signing of the season following his move to Chelsea. The Blues moved for the Argentine World Cup winner over the closing days of the summer transfer window.

‌



Chelsea agreed a £7.5m deal with Martinez’s former club Aston Villa. The 34-year-old has already made a couple of appearances for his new employers, having made his debut in the 4-3 thriller against Brighton.

‌



He was also selected in the 2-1 defeat against former side Arsenal. Despite having not kept a clean sheet yet, Schmeichel believes Martinez could be the signing of the season.

‌



“I have to say these are all crazy amounts of money, and I don’t understand how this is even possible for the clubs to maintain that level of investment,” Schmeichel told Viaplay.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

“I look at the list and the one name which I don’t see is Emi Martinez who is, for me, could turn out to be the signing of the season. He’s only costing them £7.5 million, top, top, world-class goalkeeper. Top, top, £7.5m.

‌



“If we’re confused about the transfer market, that I think is underlying of how it is. This has been the maddest window, I think.”

Martinez’s arrival was just one aspect of the reshuffle of the Blues’ goalkeeping department this summer. Robert Sanchez left the club to join Italian side Como on loan, while Filip Jorgensen signed for Strasbourg on loan. Mike Penders represents Martinez’s backup at Stamford Bridge.

Speaking about his new goalkeeper, Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso said: “Emi is a World Cup winner, is 33 years old, and is very experienced.

‌



View 2 Images Emi Martinez is already Chelsea's number one (Image: Getty Images)

“I spoke with him and we talked about the game and our team. He felt ready, and I don’t have to tell him many things for him to perform.

“Even today, while a goalkeeper wants to keep a clean sheet, I am happy with his impact. He has been in the building just 48 hours, so now we will have a whole week to prepare for the next one.

Article continues below

“Day by day, we will feel this presence because he has this charisma, this aura to influence and have a very positive connection with the rest of the team.”

Martinez and Chelsea will be back in action on Wednesday evening as they take on Premier League rivals Leeds United in the third round of the Carabao Cup. Their next league game pits them against newly promoted Hull City.

Kylian Mbappe, Harry Kane and Lamine Yamal are all among the Ballon d'Or nominees

The list of nominees for the 2026 Ballon d'Or have been announced. Harry Kane and Jude Bellingham are both among those on the 30-player shortlist this time around

The nominees for the 2026 Ballon d'Or have been announced.

England forward Harry Kane is the bookmakers' favourite to win the prestigious award following a prolific season for Bayern Munich. However, history suggests that football's biggest individual prize rarely gets decided by goals alone.

After the Ballon d'Or was first awarded in 1956, performances in the biggest competitions have shaped the outcome. World Cup years, in particular, have followed a clear pattern, and it has been shown just how difficult it is to win the award without lifting a major continental or global tournament.

With that in mind, Spain have several players featured among the 30 nominees after they triumphed at the World Cup in North America. Argentina ran them close, while England and France both reached the semi-final, and those three nations have many players in there, too.

Stay tuned here on Mirror Football for the latest on the Ballon d'Or nominees...

Sports.title: One week after the transfer window closes, Man Utd remind fans what they're really about
Sports.content:
One week after the transfer window closes, Man Utd remind fans what they're really about

Manchester United needed a new defender, but have got a shirt sleeve sponsor instead, reminding supporters what the priorities of the club's owners still are

View 2 Images Manchester United co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe (Image: Valery HACHE/AFP via Getty Images)

It has come a week after the transfer window slammed shut. So the news will mean little or nothing to long-suffering Manchester United supporters.

‌



But the club HAS made a signing.

‌



Not the left back the team continues to cry out for, or a central defender to ease the burden on Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez as United head back into the demands of Champions League football. Instead, United have landed a new shirt sleeve sponsor. The most lucrative one in the club's history, no less. The multi-million pound agreement is with financial tech giants SumUp.

‌



It follows in the footsteps of the record-breaking training kit sponsorship deal with 'Betway', said to be worth £20m-a-year.

SumUp's chief commercial officer and UK chief executive Luke Griffiths said: "Manchester United is one of the most iconic and followed clubs in the world, with a fanbase that continues to grow across generations and borders.

"That extraordinary reach and passion make this partnership a natural fit for SumUp. Football is about the moments people share. Watching the match with friends, travelling to see the team, wearing the shirt with pride and celebrating together, wherever you are. From fans using SumUp Personal Account to manage and spend their money simply, to the businesses that help make matchdays special, SumUp is part of the everyday moments that bring people together."

‌



Paul Ince recalls horrifying Glenn Hoddle incident as fans urged to back heart campaign READ MORE :

Man Utd strike deal to land Liverpool wonderkid in major transfer coup READ MORE :

View 2 Images The Glazers continue milk United like the cash cow it has served to be (Image: PA)

United might still be able to generate huge incomes from commercial deals, but it also remains a club created by the poor, and stolen by the rich.

Success on and off the pitch is supposed to go hand-in-hand. But where United are concerned, nothing could be further from the truth, because the fallen giants have not won a title since 2013, or conquered Europe since 2008. They haven't even come close.

‌



Along with the continued grip of the Glazer ownership, this is what infuriates supporters the most.

And while it is ever thus, the red half of Manchester will remain one very much divided - as opposed to United.
