World.title: Stop blaming spirits for disasters, PFN chairman tells C’River residents
World.content:
By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR

CALABAR — The Chairman of the Pentecostal Fellowship of Nigeria, PFN, in Cross River State, Apostle Trinity Ogar, has urged residents to stop attributing recent flood, landslide and fire incidents in the state to spiritual causes.

Ogar, who is also the Acting Chairman of the Christian Association of Nigeria, CAN, in the state, said the disasters should instead be viewed within the context of natural and environmental factors and existing early warning systems.

He spoke while responding to questions from journalists on the series of disasters recorded across the state in recent weeks.

His comments followed speculation among some residents linking the incidents to the alleged displeasure of an Efik marine deity, “Anansa,” said to be associated with traditional worshippers in the area.

The incidents include a fire outbreak at Spar Shopping Mall in Calabar, a landslide on Anansa Road which destroyed property, and another landslide at Ikot Awatim, which reportedly claimed four lives.

Several other deaths have also been reported in connection with flooding in parts of the state.

Some residents had called on the state government to engage the Efik traditional institution and the Obutung community, said to be associated with the deity’s shrine, to explore traditional measures to address what they believed was the cause of the disasters.

However, Ogar dismissed the attribution of the disasters to spiritual causes, saying government agencies had issued early warnings ahead of some of the incidents.

He expressed concern that residents often resorted to spiritual explanations for natural disasters instead of paying attention to scientific and environmental warnings.

According to him, greater attention should be paid to early warning systems and other preventive measures capable of reducing the impact of disasters on communities.

The PFN chairman also said sustained prayers had been offered across Calabar and other parts of Cross River State in response to the disasters.

He urged residents to take official warnings seriously and support measures aimed at preventing further loss of lives and property.

World.title: 2027: Sanwo-Olu, Hamzat urge peaceful elections
World.content:
— Lagos APC vows full mobilisation for Tinubu, Hamzat, candidates

By Olasunkanmi Akoni

LAGOS — Ahead of the 2027 general elections, Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu of Lagos State, his deputy, Dr Obafemi Hamzat, and leaders of the All Progressives Congress, APC, have urged residents to shun violence and ensure peaceful conduct before, during and after the polls.

They made the call on Tuesday at an interdenominational prayer session for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu, the election of Hamzat as Lagos State governor and other APC candidates, held at the Mobolaji Johnson Arena, Onikan, Lagos Island.

The prayer session, attended by party leaders, supporters and religious faithful, was organised to seek divine guidance, commit the party’s electoral aspirations to God and formally commence mobilisation for the 2027 elections.

Among those at the event were Senator Musiliu Obanikoro; Speaker of the Lagos State House of Assembly, Mudashiru Obasa; former Speaker of the House, Adeyemi Ikuforiji; Pa Tajudeen Olusi; Senator Ganiu Solomon; Jumoke Okoya-Thomas; Senator Idiat Adebule; Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Wale Edun; APC Lagos Chairman, Pastor Cornelius Ojelabi; Fouad Oki; members of the National Assembly and state House of Assembly; members of Conference 57 comprising 20 local government chairmen and 37 Local Council Development Area chairmen, as well as traditional rulers and religious leaders.

Speaking at the event, Sanwo-Olu stressed the importance of laying a spiritual foundation ahead of political activities.

He said the party would combine prayer with grassroots mobilisation and engagement with voters across the state.

Sanwo-Olu said although the party was relying on prayer, its members were also conscious that “faith without work is dead.”

He said the APC would not take any voter, community or stakeholder for granted, adding that the party planned to take its campaign to communities across the 20 local government areas and 37 LCDAs of the state.

According to him, the party’s objectives include securing the re-election of President Tinubu and victory for its National Assembly and state-level candidates.

Sanwo-Olu also pledged his support for Hamzat and his running mate, Damilola James-Sonayon, urging party members and residents to ensure that the electoral process remained peaceful and free from violence.

He further pledged to participate in the national presidential campaign to support the party’s efforts ahead of the election.

The governor prayed for a peaceful and prosperous Nigeria, stressing the need for unity and national development.

Also speaking, Hamzat said the prayer session provided an opportunity to commit the party’s candidates and the electoral process to God.

He prayed for peaceful elections without clashes, accidents or loss of lives, while expressing confidence in the prospects of APC candidates.

Hamzat also expressed confidence in the party’s candidates contesting the three senatorial seats, 24 House of Representatives seats and 40 Lagos State House of Assembly seats.

Earlier, the Director-General of the Kadiri Obafemi Hamzat, KOH, Campaign Council, Senator Musiliu Obanikoro, said the prayer was necessary because human efforts alone could not determine the outcome of every circumstance.

Obanikoro urged party members to place the interest of the APC above personal ambitions, warning that internal disagreements should not weaken the party ahead of the elections.

He called for dialogue, reconciliation, discipline and unity among candidates and supporters, urging them to campaign with respect and focus on their capacity to serve the people.

Obanikoro said the campaign organisation would take the APC’s message to communities across Lagos State and the wider South-West.

He expressed confidence that the APC would emerge victorious in the presidential, National Assembly and state elections, particularly projecting the emergence of Hamzat as governor and Damilola Sonayon James as deputy governor.

The event featured prayers by Christian, Muslim and traditional worshippers for Tinubu, Hamzat, other APC candidates and the peaceful conduct of the 2027 elections.

World.title: Zamfara assembly, agencies meet over 2027 -2029 budget framework
World.content:
The Zamfara State Government had validated the 2027–2029 Medium-Term Expenditure Framework (MTEF) with a view to enhancing budget credibility and planning.

The state Ministry of Budget and Planning, in collaboration with the State Action on Business Enabling Reforms (SABER) Programme, revealed this after a one-day Validation Workshop in Kaduna.

The workshop brought together members of the State House of Assembly, representatives of MDAs, and other key stakeholders to review and validate the draft framework.

The exercise demonstrated the commitment of the Zamfara State Government under the leadership of Governor Dauda Lawal to strengthening fiscal discipline, transparency, accountability, and prudent management of public resources.

The MTEF serves as a strategic framework for aligning medium-term revenue projections with expenditure priorities and ensuring efficient allocation of scarce resources.

Speaking at the workshop, the Commissioner for Budget and Planning, Prof. Y. A. Zakari, represented by the Permanent Secretary, Sani Abubakar Bukkuyum, emphasised the importance of ensuring that the 2027–2029 MTEF is credible, realistic, participatory, and aligned with the Administration’s Rescue Agenda.

The workshop reviewed key areas including revenue projections, expenditure ceilings, fiscal assumptions, sectoral priorities, fiscal sustainability, and the linkage between the MTEF and the annual budget process.

In his remarks, Speaker Bilyaminu Ismail Moriki highlighted that the participation of members of the State House of Assembly in the workshop provides an important opportunity to strengthen Executive–Legislative collaboration and ownership of the State’s fiscal and budgetary framework.

World.title: How Remi Tinubu’s N2bn lifeline could revive Akwete’s dying weaving heritage
World.content:
Remi Tinubu

By Steve Oko

For generations, the rhythmic clatter of wooden looms echoed through Akwete, a quiet riverine community in the Ukwa East Local Government Area of Abia State. Every woven thread told a story of ingenuity, resilience, and culture. The famous Akwete cloth was more than fabric; it was the people’s identity, painstakingly woven by women whose skills had been passed from one generation to the next.

Yet, behind the beauty of the colourful handwoven textile lay a painful reality. The women who kept the centuries-old tradition alive worked with little government support, obsolete equipment, limited access to finance and shrinking markets. Many younger people abandoned the craft in search of better opportunities, leaving fears that one of Nigeria’s oldest indigenous textile traditions could gradually fade into history.

That long season of neglect may now be drawing to a close. When Nigeria’s First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, arrived in Akwete on July 21, 2026, her visit was more than ceremonial. It was an acknowledgement that hidden within the modest weaving community is an economic asset capable of creating jobs, empowering women, and preserving Nigeria’s cultural identity.

The defining moment came when she announced a N2 billion intervention to establish and strengthen an Akwete production hub. For the women seated before her, it was more than a financial commitment. It was validation after decades of waiting for meaningful government intervention.

“I am donating N2 billion to the project,” the First Lady declared, while urging Nigerians, especially the South-East, to embrace Akwete cloth as a national fabric rather than merely a local cultural product.

Her words resonated deeply because they addressed one of the biggest challenges confronting the industry: visibility.

For decades, Akwete fabric has enjoyed admiration among cultural enthusiasts but has struggled to compete with more commercial indigenous textiles such as Aso Oke, despite possessing comparable historical and artistic value. The First Lady challenged Nigerians to change that narrative.

Her promise to wear Akwete fabric if President Bola Tinubu secures a second term was itself a powerful endorsement capable of projecting the fabric onto national and international fashion platforms.

However, Mrs Tinubu will not be the first high-profile Nigerian to proudly wear Akwete fabrics. In fact, Gov. Chukwuma Soludo of Anambra State is a brand Ambassador of Akwete textile. He has proudly adorned himself with different colours and designs of the prestigious local fabrics. Former Governor Okezie Ikpeazu of Abia State also did so well in promoting Akwete textile, just as the incumbent Gov. Otti is towing a similar line.

The diaspora Igbo community is scrambling for Akwete textile, as the women in the weaving industry confirmed to this Correspondent earlier that they were receiving orders for the Akwete fabric from different parts of the world. Beyond orders from the diaspora, some communities and women’s associations in Rivers, Bayelsa, and other neighbouring states have adopted Akwete textile as their uniform. The famous Arochukwu kingdom has been celebrating one of its traditional festivals with Akwete textile as the official attire. Some Government officials as well as patriotic individuals take pride in adorning themselves with Akwete fabrics.

Beyond symbolism, however, the N2 billion intervention has the potential to fundamentally transform the local economy. Experts have long argued that Akwete’s greatest challenge is not the absence of skilled artisans but the absence of investment. Most weavers still rely on manual production methods that limit output and income. Access to quality raw materials, modern finishing equipment, product packaging, branding, and organised marketing has remained poor.

A properly developed production hub could address many of these structural constraints. With adequate investment, hundreds of women could expand production, younger residents could acquire weaving skills as a viable means of livelihood, and the community could evolve into a major cultural and tourism destination.

For Abia State, which is increasingly positioning itself as Nigeria’s hub for small and medium-scale enterprises under Governor Alex Otti, the intervention fits neatly into the administration’s economic diversification agenda.

Governor Otti, while receiving the First Lady, acknowledged that his administration had recognised Akwete’s economic potential soon after assuming office in 2023 and pledged the state’s full cooperation in translating the intervention into tangible development.

He described the First Lady’s visit as timely and strategic, noting that the government was prepared to partner with her in building a modern production hub capable of unlocking the enormous commercial value embedded in the famous fabric.

The visit also demonstrated how development can transcend partisan politics. Although Governor Otti belongs to the Labour Party and the First Lady is a leading figure in the ruling APC, both emphasised collaboration rather than political differences. Their shared commitment underscored an important lesson: when livelihoods are at stake, governance should rise above party lines.

The significance of the visit was not lost on the people of Akwete. For perhaps the first time, they saw the First Lady of Nigeria walk through their weaving centre, inspect their looms, interact with the artisans and publicly commit substantial resources to their future.

The excitement reflected more than appreciation. It reflected renewed hope. If transparently implemented, the intervention could stimulate cottage industries supplying yarns, dyes and accessories, create employment across the value chain, attract fashion designers and textile entrepreneurs, encourage exports and improve household incomes across the community.

It could also inspire many young people to return to a profession their parents and grandparents once proudly practised but which declining returns had made unattractive. Perhaps the greatest significance of the intervention lies in its timing.

Across Nigeria, conversations about economic diversification increasingly focus on agriculture, technology and manufacturing. Yet, cultural industries remain one of the country’s least exploited economic frontiers.

Akwete represents what can happen when heritage becomes enterprise. Countries across Asia have transformed indigenous crafts into billion-dollar industries through strategic investments, branding and tourism. Nigeria possesses similar opportunities in communities like Akwete, where tradition and entrepreneurship naturally intersect.

The First Lady’s intervention therefore extends beyond charity. It represents an investment in culture, women, rural enterprise and economic inclusion.

Whether the N2 billion becomes a true game-changer will ultimately depend on transparent implementation, proper management and sustained institutional support from both the federal and Abia State governments. Some elder statesmen from the area, including former Senate President, Adolphus Wabara, and former Secretary General of Ohanaeze Ndigbo, Okey Emuchay, have, while lauding the gesture by the First Lady, called for transparency in the disbursement of the funds. It, therefore, becomes imperative that a corruption-free mechanism be put in place to checkmate abuse and the usual squandermania associated with ‘free money’.

For the women of Akwete, however, hope has returned to the looms. After decades of weaving history into every thread while waiting for government to notice them, they may finally be on the threshold of a new chapter—one in which their craft not only preserves the past but also secures the future. It is a challenge to the women and young girls in the area to double down and prove that, indeed, they can ‘do wonders’ with the necessary support.

Perhaps most importantly, the age-old myths that weaving in Akwete is exclusive of only the womenfold has to be broken. Similarly, there is a need for the trade to go beyond manual weaving and embrace technology for mass production. If the industry must break even and survive in this era of global competition, it must think about commercialisation and refuse to be limited by the ropes of tradition and myths.

World.title: Onitsha marks 500yrs unbroken monarchy with special logo for Ofala 2026
World.content:
By Vincent Ujumadu

The Ofala Onitsha Steering Committee has unveiled the official logo and theme for Ofala 2026 festival, which will mark 500 plus years of unbroken monarchy.

The festival is scheduled to hold on October 16 and 17 at Ime Obi, Ezechima Square, Onitsha, with the theme, Igba mbo, iga n’iru (Strive and Advance).

Chairman of the Ofala steering committee, Dr Mike Areh, said the 2026 logo is a royal, cultural, and premium visual statement developed to reflect the strength of an institution that has endured for over 500 years, yet remains relevant, progressive, and unifying.

“For 500 years, our forebears strove to build, protect, and sustain the Onitsha Kingdom. Today, we are called to advance that legacy through culture, enterprise, youth development, and unity. In this Ofala, we honour the past by building the future”, Areh said.

According to the Ofala steering committee chairman, the logo was conceptualized to show that Ofala is not only a celebration of tradition, but also a living system of identity, leadership, order, resilience, and advancement.

Areh added: “Ofala holds the people together while reminding them that heritage is not static; it is a foundation for movement.

“The swords represent royal authority, protection, and continuity. The beads speak to identity, honour, and cultural belonging.

“The central plate carries the message with the dignity of a royal proclamation. The line-up of Agbogidi, red-chiefs, and attendants captures the sacred moment of readiness before the monarch appears before his people.

“The white sculptural relief gives a refined heritage feel, while the purple accents reinforce royalty and the Ofala brand identity.

“Every element was intentionally placed to connect the throne, the people, the culture, and

the future. Ofala 2026 is heritage in motion;

rooted in royalty, built on resilience and moving toward progress.

“As the Onitsha Kingdom marks 500+ years of unbroken monarchy, the theme is a call for Ndi Onitsha and Ndi Igbo to strive and advance.”

The highlights of the two – day event include the Iru Ofala, Azu Ofala, Oreze International Art

Exhibition, Ofala Youth Carnival ,and initiatives aligned with the theme.

World.title: PDP denies collapse into APM, threatens legal action
World.content:
By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi

BAUCHI — THE Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Bauchi State has dismissed reports that its structure has collapsed into the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), describing the claim as false and alleging that it was being spread by individuals impersonating party officials.

The party’s Legal Adviser in the state, Yahaya Garkuwa, stated this on Tuesday at a press conference held at the PDP secretariat along Maiduguri Bypass, Bauchi.

Garkuwa said the PDP recognised by law in Bauchi State remained the faction led by Hon. Ibrahim Kashim Toro, while the national leadership was headed by Abdulrahman Mohammed.

He said the leadership dispute within the party had been the subject of several court cases, adding that successive judicial pronouncements had affirmed the leadership structure backed by the Bauchi PDP.

According to him, the Federal High Court affirmed the Abdulrahman Mohammed-led caretaker committee as the authentic national leadership of the party.

He said the faction led by Tanimu Turaki subsequently appealed the judgment, but the Court of Appeal upheld the leadership of Mohammed at the national level and that of Ibrahim Kashim Toro in Bauchi State.

“Dissatisfied with the decision, the Tanimu Turaki faction went to the Court of Appeal where the Appeal Court still confirmed the leadership of the PDP under Abdulrahman Mohammed, and in Bauchi State under Hon. Ibrahim’s leadership,” Garkuwa said.

He added that the matter was eventually taken to the Supreme Court, which, according to him, ruled in favour of the faction led by Mohammed.

“At the Supreme Court, judgment was given in our favour where the Supreme Court said the Tanimu Turaki faction is not known by law, that only the PDP under Abdulrahman Mohammed is known by law, while here in Bauchi State, the PDP known by law is the one under Honourable Ibrahim,” he said.

Garkuwa alleged that members of the rival faction had resorted to impersonation and the spread of what he described as false information after exhausting their legal options.

“Now that they don’t have anywhere to go by the judgment of the Supreme Court, they now started impersonating that they are leaders of the PDP. And as they don’t have where to stay, they decided to create confusion to tell the public that the PDP structure has collapsed into APM,” he said.

The legal adviser insisted that the PDP had neither joined the APM nor any other political party, saying the party remained intact.

“We, the authentic members of the PDP, are still in the PDP. We have not joined any other political party; we still remain in the PDP,” he added.

Garkuwa further disclosed that the Bauchi State PDP leadership was preparing to take legal action against individuals allegedly parading themselves as officials of the party.

He urged members of the public to disregard reports of the party’s alleged collapse, insisting that the PDP recognised by law remained under the current state leadership.

“You can see that we are the only PDP members whose candidates’ names were published by INEC ahead of the 2027 general elections,” he said.

He also challenged the rival faction to produce evidence of the candidates it intended to field under the PDP platform.

“If they are truly members of the PDP, let them name their candidates. They don’t have candidates,” Garkuwa said.

He assured party supporters that the PDP remained politically active in the state and was preparing for the 2027 general elections.

“PDP is not collapsing into any political party. PDP is still standing, PDP is still strong and is fully prepared for the 2027 general elections,” he said.

The press conference was attended by the state PDP chairman, other party officials, stakeholders and supporters.

World.title: AOG aircraft: NCAA demands cuts in airline operations
World.content:
By Dickson Omobola

NIGERIA Civil Aviation Authority, NCAA, has directed domestic airlines to cut down their flight operations whenever aircraft were grounded due to technical issues to avoid excessive disruption and hardship for passengers.

AOG simply means aircraft on ground.

Director of Public Affairs and Consumer Protection at NCAA, Michael Achimugu, who stated this on X, formerly Twitter, warned airlines against operating beyond their available capacity at the expense of passengers.

Achimugu said airlines with aircraft on ground were expected to reduce schedules to prevent avoidable delays and cancellations.

He stated: “If an airline has its machines AOG, it is instructed to cut down the size of its operations to avoid causing excessive, avoidable pain to passengers. It goes without saying.

“If a delay hits two hours, passengers nust be given light refreshment. On the six-hour mark, passengers are entitled to a proper meal. This is non-negotiable.

“If that delay lasts until 10pm, accommodation should be provided, except where the passenger resides in that city; even that is subject to certain factors.”

Meanwhile, Nigeria’s largest airline, Air Peace, has apologised to all passengers affected by the delays and cancellations recently experienced across its operations.

Chief Operating Officer, COO, of Air Peace, Oluwatoyin Olajide, said in a statement yesterday that the disruptions resulted from a combination of unforeseen circumstances, ‘including an inadvertent false fire alarm that grounded one of the aircraft; adverse weather conditions that resulted in diversions, delays and, in some cases, outright cancellations; and a bird strike that grounded another aircraft for days.

She also listed technical issues requiring necessary mandatory checks and maintenance, as well as a delay in the availability of aviation fuel in some cases as other factors responsible for the disruptions.

According to her, Air Peace will never compromise safety in an attempt to keep to a schedule.

“In Air Peace, safety remains our highest priority. We will never compromise the safety of our passengers, crew and aircraft. An aircraft will not be released for service until our technical teams and all relevant safety procedures are satisfied that it is safe to fly.

‘’Where weather, technical conditions, a bird strike or any other safety-related circumstance requires an aircraft to remain on the ground, that decision will always take precedence over operational convenience.

“We are taking immediate steps to stabilise our operations, strengthen our contingency measures and improve our communication and responsiveness when unforeseen challenges arise,’’ Olajide added.

World.title: FG moves to operationalise 112 national emergency number
World.content:
Vice President Shettima

—As VP Shettima directs relevant stakeholders, agencies to develop roadmap for NEC’s endorsement

By Johnbosco Agbakwuru

ABUJA— THE Federal Government on Tuesday, directed stakeholders and relevant agencies to design a comprehensive operational roadmap for the nationwide rollout of the 112 national emergency number.

Accordingly, it constituted a committee comprising the Nigeria Police Force (NPF), the Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC), the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA), the Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC), and other relevant agencies to finalise the roadmap and standard operating procedures for formal endorsement of the National Economic Council (NEC).

Recall that NEC had recently approved the 112 as Nigeria’s single universal toll-free emergency number to replace fragmented and slow response lines, with a view to eliminating bureaucratic red tape and allow citizens easy access to rapid help during fires, accidents, medical crises, or security breaches.

Speaking in Abuja during the National Emergency Number 112 Project stakeholders meeting, the Vice President who gave the directive, urged the committee to ensure their decisions are based on global best practises in order to have a clear roadmap.

Charging the committee to finalize the roadmap and standard operating procedures for formal NEC endorsement, Senator Shettima stressed the need to make significant progress, assuring that once it becomes visible, resources will be available to fund the process.

“Let’s make progress so that whatever time we have spent here is worth spending. And most importantly, the engine is finance. It is resources to drive the process. And I want to assure you that we will get the resources,” he stated.

On his part, the Inspector General of Police (IGP), Olatunji Rilwan Disu, said the Nigeria Police Force was fully in support of the adoption of 112 as Nigeria’s unified national emergency number.

From an operational perspective, he noted that it is “a significant step towards ensuring that citizens have a simple and reliable means of accessing emergency assistance.”

He explained that for a citizen facing an armed attack, accident, fire outbreak, medical emergency, kidnapping, or any other life-threatening situation, while the first challenge is to determine which agency to call, one number should provide access to the appropriate response.

Earlier in her presentation, the Personal Assistant to the President on e-Governance (Office of the Vice President), Mrs. Lydia Aina, noted that emergency response in Nigeria runs across many agencies, systems, and jurisdictions, creating fragmentation in how emergencies are received, coordinated, and responded to.

The goal, she said, is to move from the fragmented states through coordinated response to a fully integrated national framework, just as she explained that the meeting was about the system behind the process, including “the people, the agencies, the standards that make the number actually work when citizens dial it.

“Our job now is to turn it into an actual working programme with milestones. So, we have identified six immediate priorities. First, governance. We need a clear structure of who’s responsible for what,” she explained.

Other stakeholders who pledged the full support of their agencies at the meeting included the Director-General of NEMA, Mrs. Zubaida Umar; Corps Marshal of FRSC, Shehu Mohammed, and Director-General of the National Orientation Agency (NOA), Mallam Lanre Issa-Onilu, among others.

World.title: 150 Innovative University Academic Projects to Receive N20m Grooming Centre Research Grant
World.content:
Oluchi Chibuzor

About 150 innovative university academic projects at undergraduate and postgraduate levels will receive N20 million in the 2026 Grooming Centre University research grant.

Speaking at the opening of the call for applications in Lagos, Assistant Manager, Research and Development, CREM, Chimfurumnaya Chukwuekem, said there are no barriers of age, gender, religion, or ethnicity to the Grooming Centre University Grant Scheme.

He explained that this year’s grants would see 50 postgraduate and 100 undergraduate students receive N20m as beneficiaries of the programme.

He stated that since inception in 2019, the Grooming Centre University Grant scheme’s intervention in tertiary research has awarded prizes to 659 students.

The application, which opened on August 31, will close on October 23, 2026.

Chukwuekem said, “In addition to the designated focus areas for research proposals, the following criteria will serve as the basis for evaluating all submissions. The applicant must either be a final-year undergraduate student or a postgraduate student in a Nigerian tertiary institution whose research project covers any of such areas as financial inclusion, microfinance, rural development, social enterprise, MSMEs, technological development, digital innovation in finance, youth development, women’s empowerment or any other research that is aimed at lifting people out of poverty.

“The focus of the research study must be relevant to the Nigerian context, practical, innovative and should be capable of promoting any of the above areas of interest in the Nigerian space.”

The COO, CREM Consulting, Clifford Onyeike, said prospective research must “show a high level of originality, imaginative thought and be data-inclusive” and that the applicant must be a student of an approved Nigerian tertiary institution.

“Once selected, beneficiaries must submit their final project to the centre,” said Onyeike.

World.title: Retired BOUESTI Academics, Workers Lament Pension Ordeal, Appeal for Oyebanji’s Intervention
World.content:
Gbenga Sodeinde in Ado Ekiti

Retired academics and non-academic staff of the Bamidele Olumilua University of Education, Science and Technology, Ikere-Ekiti (BOUESTI), have appealed to Governor Biodun Oyebanji to intervene in what they described as a worsening pension ordeal, saying months of unpaid pensions and outstanding retirement benefits have pushed many into severe hardship.

The pensioners, under the aegis of the BOUESTI Pensioners Association, said many retired workers who devoted decades of service to the institution are now battling financial distress, ill health and uncertainty due to delayed pension payments and other outstanding entitlements.

The appeal was stated in a letter dated September 7, 2026, addressed to Governor Oyebanji as visitor to the university. The letter was jointly signed by the association’s Chairman, Dr Kola Ajaja, and its Public Relations Officer, Mr Alao Odeyemi.

The retirees said they have yet to receive their August 2026 pension, while only 50 per cent of their July pension had been paid, a development they said has compounded their suffering.

According to the association, the persistent delay in pension payments has made it difficult for many members to meet their healthcare needs and other basic responsibilities, adding that some pensioners have reportedly lost their lives amid the prolonged financial hardship.

The association further alleged that the university management owed pensioners outstanding gratuities and arrears arising from the implementation of the new minimum wage and the 20 to 28 per cent pension increment, and that it had also failed to implement the 2019 consequential pension adjustment for retired workers.

The pensioners urged the governor to use his office to facilitate the immediate payment of all outstanding entitlements, including the full August 2026 pension, the balance of the July pension, gratuities, arrears of the new minimum wage, the 20 to 28 per cent pension increase and the implementation of the 2019 consequential pension adjustment.

Explaining why it chose dialogue over public protests, the association said it was confident in the governor’s commitment to retirees’ welfare.

“We have chosen to send this appeal to you rather than embark on public protests because we believe that you will answer our prayers with utmost urgency,” the pensioners stated.

They expressed optimism that Oyebanji’s prompt intervention would bring relief to retired academics and other workers of the institution, enabling them to meet their medical and welfare needs while preventing further avoidable deaths among pensioners.

World.title: Governor Otti to Chair 2026 Fafunwa Educational Foundation Conference
World.content:
Governor Alex Otti of Abia State is expected to chair the 2026 Fafunwa Educational Foundation (FEF) conference.

The 24th annual FEF lecture/symposium will be held at Agip Recital Hall, Muson Centre, Onikan, Lagos, on September 23.

The foundation’s Executive Secretary, Muyiwa Obiyomi, disclosed that the theme of the 2026 symposium is ‘What Does the Research Say?: Mother Tongue Instruction and the Future of Early Education in Nigeria’.

The conference, open to scholars and the public, is scheduled to start at 11:00 a.m., but Obiyomi urged participants to be seated by 10:45 a.m.

He described this year’s conference as a special one, saying, “FEF is grateful that Dr Alex Otti agreed to be our esteemed chairman this year. Otti is widely admired in this country today. His presence honours the legacy of the late Professor Aliu Babatunde Fafunwa.”

Obiyomi said Fafunwa conceived the annual FEF conference more than 20 years ago.

“As Nigeria’s first indigenous Professor of Education and longtime researcher, Fafunwa trained several generations of teachers and educationists. As a former minister of education, he shaped Nigeria’s educational policy in positive and enduring ways. As a professor and researcher at the University of Ife (now Obafemi Awolowo University), he carried out a pioneering study in the use of mother tongue in early education. He became a lifelong advocate of mother tongue education,” Obiyomi said.

Fafunwa’s daughter, Prof Sheri Fafunwa Ndibe, also expressed delight in anticipation of Otti’s participation, and thanked the governor for accepting the foundation’s invitation to be chairman.

“Governor Otti is a visionary leader in many respects, including in the educational sector,” she said.

Jamiu Alli-Balogun, the Commissioner for Primary and Secondary Education in Lagos, would be the guest of honour. Obiyomi described the commissioner as a “capable and committed hand who is spearheading Governor Sanwo-Olu’s agenda for the transformation of primary and secondary education in Lagos State”.

The 2026 Fafunwa Educational Foundation conference will feature a keynote address by Prof Francis Egbokhare of the Linguistics and African Languages Department, University of Ibadan. Prof Angelina Kioko, a Kenyan scholar, will be the guest speaker. Kioko is a linguist and multilingual education expert who teaches at the United States International University-Africa (USIU-Africa) in Nairobi, Kenya.

The FEF programme will also feature a panel discussion on mother tongue education in Nigeria. The discussants include language experts such as Prof Adeyinka of the University of Ibadan, Dr Ebele Okafor of the University of Lagos, and Dr Hamisu Aliyu, who teaches at Federal College of Education, Abeokuta.

The event will also feature the presentation of postdoctoral awards to several recent graduates from a cross-section of Nigerian universities.

“Each year, scholars, policymakers and stakeholders look forward to the FEF conference because of the high intellectual quality. We have never disappointed. I expect this year’s conference to yield both intellectual stimulation and cogent policy pathways,” Obiyomi added.

Otti will also launch an illustrated biography of Fafunwa. The book, which is designed for young readers, is authored by Prof Okey Ndibe.

Ndibe said, “My late father-in-law lived an extraordinary life. He faced numerous challenges as a youngster. Even so, he persevered to triumph over adversity. From humble circumstances, he rose to become one of the world’s most respected scholars, researchers and policymakers. I’ve always been inspired by his story. I wrote a children’s version of his biography, my goal being to inspire youngsters in Nigeria, Africa, and the world.”

He expressed excitement that the Abia governor would formally unveil the book.

World.title: Senate Raises Alarm Over Declining TETFund Revenue, Warns of Impact on Infrastructure
World.content:
Funmi Ogundare

The Senate Committee on Tertiary Education and TETFund has expressed concern about the declining revenue available to the Tertiary Education Trust Fund (TETFund), saying it could slow infrastructure development in Nigerian tertiary institutions.

The committee chairman, Senator Mohammed Dandutshe, raised the concern during an oversight visit to Yaba College of Technology (YABATECH), Lagos, where the committee inspected TETFund-funded projects and interacted with the institution’s management, staff and students.

He said discussions with relevant stakeholders indicated that the amount available for distribution to TETFund this year could be significantly lower than the previous year’s allocation.

Dandutshe stated, “The development could affect the pace of infrastructure development in universities, polytechnics and colleges of education, particularly as the government continues to establish and expand tertiary institutions across the country.”

The senator highlighted the need for adequate education funding, saying Nigeria must accord the sector greater priority to achieve sustainable national development. He added that the committee’s visit was part of its constitutional responsibility to monitor project implementation and ensure transparency and accountability in the utilisation of public funds.

The chairman added, “The inspection was also designed to enable members of the committee to engage directly with tertiary institutions and understand the challenges affecting the delivery of quality education.”

Dandutshe said that the committee was particularly interested in assessing what YABATECH had achieved with TETFund interventions covering the 2023, 2024 and 2025 cycles, as well as identifying challenges requiring legislative intervention.

Speaking on the institution’s challenges, the Rector, Dr Ibraheem Abdul, noted that it is grappling with severe infrastructural pressure due to its large population and limited land space.

Dandutshe disclosed that the institution has about 35,400 students and more than 2,000 staff members operating within a relatively small land area, making conventional horizontal expansion difficult. He noted that the situation has forced the college to adopt vertical development by constructing multi-storey buildings to maximise its limited land space.

The rector said the college, which will mark its 80th anniversary next year, has several facilities that have become obsolete, some built during the colonial era. He said the college consequently embarked on a strategic redevelopment programme involving the demolition of some old structures and the construction of modern multi-storey facilities.

Abdul said, “YABATECH had also adopted the policy of merging TETFund interventions across different years to execute projects of substantial value and quality capable of addressing its peculiar infrastructural needs.”

He cited the conversion of spaces previously occupied by facilities such as the Rector’s Lodge for academic infrastructure as part of efforts to optimise the institution’s limited land.

Abdul further disclosed that the college is facing intense demand for admission because of its reputation, noting that hundreds of prospective students had protested in the past over their inability to secure admission. He, however, explained that despite the demand, the institution had to operate within the admission quota approved by the Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB).

Abdul said the college was gradually developing another campus and had begun directing some infrastructural interventions towards the new location. According to him, YABATECH is expanding its skills-development programmes to equip young Nigerians with practical competencies beyond conventional National Diploma and Higher National Diploma programmes.

A member of the committee, Senator Shuaibu Afolabi, commended the college for managing its large student population within limited physical space. Afolabi urged the institution to complement its vertical physical expansion with increased investment in digital learning. He advised the college to explore remote learning centres and technology-enabled teaching platforms that would allow students to participate in academic activities without necessarily being physically present on campus.

The senator also encouraged YABATECH to build stronger affiliations with reputable institutions worldwide to promote knowledge exchange and expose its students and staff to best practices.

Afolabi urged the college to seek additional interventions from federal agencies with mandates in technology and innovation to complement TETFund funding, particularly agencies involved in ICT, digital technology and innovation.

World.title: The Silent Return: How Diphtheria Killed 39 Children in Zamfara and UNICEF, Health Ministry’s Dash for Urgent Vaccination
World.content:
Onuminya Innocent

The ward at the Infectious Disease Centre in Damba is quiet in a way that feels wrong. Fluorescent lights hum above rows of iron beds. Mothers sit on plastic chairs, cloths pressed to fevered foreheads. Nurses move fast between patients, but their voices are low.

Last week, the Zamfara State Ministry of Health confirmed what many families here already feared: an outbreak of diphtheria has claimed 39 lives. The ministry also recorded another 261 suspected cases across 10 local government areas.

Most of the faces in these beds are small. Health workers say many of the children are between six and ten months old.

“Some of them came in too late,” a nurse at the WCWC Primary Healthcare Centre in Kwata, Gusau, said as she checked a child’s throat with a torchlight, adding, “By the time the parents realise it’s not just a cough, the breathing is already difficult.”

Diphtheria, caused by Corynebacterium, attacks the nose, throat, and sometimes the skin. The early signs look ordinary: fever, runny nose, sore throat, cough, red eyes. Then comes the neck swelling. Then the struggle to breathe. Without antitoxins and antibiotics, it kills.

What is new is how quickly it has moved this year.

A disease of missed chances

The numbers paint a worrying picture. Gusau Local Government Area alone accounts for 191 of the 261 suspected cases—the highest in the state. Laboratory tests have confirmed some cases, while surveillance teams continue to test and trace contacts across communities. The state government responded immediately. The Ministry of Health convened a rapid response team and deployed it to affected areas to identify new cases, provide emergency treatment, and prevent further spread.

Rilwan Musa, Permanent Secretary of the Zamfara State Ministry of Health, said that the response has full backing from Governor Dauda Lawal’s administration and development partners.

“We mobilised across the state the moment we saw the trend,” Musa told THISDAY. “But we need government at all levels to intensify efforts – more vaccines, more health workers, more sensitisation in every ward. This cannot be a one-state fight.”

But behind the mobilisation is a harder truth: most of the children who died had not been vaccinated. National data backs that up. According to UNICEF, only 22 per cent of confirmed diphtheria cases in Nigeria had received routine childhood immunisations. The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control (NCDC) reports that 68 per cent of confirmed cases nationwide involved unvaccinated people.

“It’s heartbreaking to note that only 22 per cent of the confirmed cases received their routine childhood immunisation vaccinations,” said Cristian Munduate, UNICEF Representative in Nigeria. “Many children did not receive their vaccines during the COVID-19 lockdown. We now urgently need to catch up. These zero-dose children, those who haven’t received a single dose of vaccine, are a primary concern.”

In Zamfara, that gap is visible. At Kwata PHC, health workers point to immunisation hesitancy and missed doses as major drivers of the spread.

“We are begging parents,” the nurse added. “Please bring your wards for vaccination. The vaccines are free at all PHCs. Waiting costs lives. If your child misses a dose, go to the clinic today. Don’t wait for symptoms.”

Ten LGAs, one fear

The outbreak is not confined to Gusau. Cases have been reported in nine other LGAs, stretching response teams thin. From Kwata PHC, the rapid response team proceeded to Damba to check on patients receiving care at the Infectious Disease Centre. Some were on oxygen. Some were stable. All were children.

Diphtheria thrives where routine vaccination drops. Nationwide, the outbreak has hit Kano, Yobe, Katsina, Lagos, FCT, Sokoto, and Zamfara hardest—those seven states account for 98 per cent of suspected cases. Children aged 2 to 14 make up about 71.5 per cent of confirmed cases. The case fatality rate sits at 8.7 per cent. For every 100 children infected, nearly nine do not make it. In the last three years, NCDC says diphtheria has claimed over 1,300 lives across Nigeria.

What happens next: A two-pronged responsibility

In Damba, the immediate work is clinical: identify, isolate, treat. Antitoxin and antibiotics are being administered. Contacts are being traced. Health education teams are moving through markets and schools with megaphones and pamphlets. But health officials insist that treatment alone will not end this. For government, the demand is clear: intensify efforts. That means deploying more vaccines to rural PHCs, funding mobile vaccination teams, paying community health workers promptly, and sustaining surveillance even after the outbreak slows.

For parents and caregivers, the responsibility is just as urgent: avail your wards for vaccination. The diphtheria vaccine is part of Nigeria’s routine immunisation and is provided free at primary healthcare centres. Children are to receive doses at six, 10, and 14 weeks, with boosters later. Catch-up campaigns are now being prioritised in Zamfara to reach “zero-dose” children.

Health officials are asking communities to do three things: bring any child with fever, sore throat, or breathing difficulty to a clinic immediately; complete the full vaccination schedule; and report suspected cases early. At Kwata, a mother rocked her eight-month-old and whispered prayers. She had missed the second vaccine dose during the pandemic.

“I thought we could wait,” she said. “I didn’t know it would come like this. I will take my other children tomorrow.”

The weight of 39

Thirty-nine funerals in a matter of weeks. Thirty-nine names that will be read at community meetings. Thirty-nine empty spaces at dinner tables across 10 LGAs. The rapid response team will keep working. The vaccines are available. The message from the health ministry and UNICEF is simple and urgent: this disease is preventable—but only if government intensifies efforts and parents step forward.

For now, Zamfara is in a race between the bacteria moving through unprotected children and the health workers trying to reach them first. In Damba ward, a nurse adjusts an IV and checks a chart. Outside, another ambulance pulls in. The fight is not over.

World.title: Elizabeth Musa wins Innovative Media Personality of the Year Awar
World.content:
Victoria Ojiako

Elizabeth Musa, Programme Lead and Anchor of Business Morning Live on BusinessDay Television, has won the Innovative Media Personality of the Year award.

Musa emerged winner of the category at the Golden Prestigious Icons Awards 2025, following a voting process that recognised her contributions to Nigeria’s media industry.

Speaking on the recognition, Musa said she was initially notified about the nomination through social media and was unfamiliar with the awards platform.

She said she subsequently conducted due diligence on the organisation and the awards before appreciating the nomination.

“I was genuinely honoured that someone had taken the time to nominate me,” she said.

Musa explained that she did not apply for the award, noting that the nomination-based process suggested that someone had been following her work and considered her deserving of the recognition.

According to her, consistency, persistence, resilience and versatility across different media platforms may have contributed to her nomination.

She said her career had exposed her to radio, television, print, content creation and podcasting, as well as media training and international and diplomatic discussions.

“For a category like Innovative Media Personality of the Year, I believe it was that combination of versatility, experience and my willingness to keep evolving that resonated with the organisers,” she said.

Musa described her emergence as winner as exciting and expressed gratitude to those who voted for her, particularly because it was a voting category.

She said the recognition validated her work but also represented the beginning of greater responsibilities and opportunities.

The journalist said she had been privileged to contribute to important projects at BusinessDay, including playing a pioneering role in the development of BusinessDay Television.

“Being part of a new project, helping to shape its direction and being at the forefront of building something from the ground up is certainly not easy,” she said.

On the evolving media landscape, she said artificial intelligence and changing audience behaviour had created new opportunities for media professionals.

She identified digital content, podcasts, online courses, video courses, educational content and new media products as areas with significant growth potential.

“I think the future really belongs to media professionals who can combine strong storytelling with technology and understand how to build communities around their content,” she said.

Looking ahead, Musa said she would continue creating, growing and using available platforms to make an impact.

She said her future plans included more storytelling, content, conversations and innovation, while trusting God with the bigger picture.

Musa is a broadcast journalist, business storyteller and professional events compere with close to a decade of experience in television, multimedia storytelling and live events across Africa.

She currently leads and anchors Business Morning Live on BusinessDay Television, where she engages business leaders, policymakers, entrepreneurs and industry experts on issues shaping Nigeria’s economy and business environment.

She previously worked as a producer and presenter on Breakfast Central, the pan-African morning programme on News Central Television.

Musa holds a Bachelor of Arts degree in International Studies and Diplomacy from the University of Benin, a Postgraduate Diploma in Mass Communications from the University of Lagos and a degree in Media Innovation from the School of Media and Communication, Pan-Atlantic University.

She also holds an additional certification from the University of Johannesburg.

World.title: Spotlight on Nigerian Army’s Operational Gains in Rescue, Counter-terrorism
World.content:
The Nigerian Army has recorded significant operational successes from July to the first week of September, with troops involved in rescue operations, arrests, patrols, ambushes and weapons recovery across multiple theatres. The period includes the rescue of 11 kidnapped persons and arrest of 21 suspects in July; 308 people rescued in a joint operation around Kainji Lake National Park; 21 abducted persons rescued in Kogi on August 31; and 25 more victims rescued in Katsina and Zamfara. Troops also recovered an RPG launcher, an AK-47 rifle, ammunition and 793 rounds of ammunition intercepted in Kaduna, as operations against terrorism, banditry and kidnapping continued nationwide. Chiemelie Ezeobi writes that this is in tandem with the Chief of Army Staff, Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu’s P.R.O.S.E operational framework

Since taking over as Chief of Army Staff in October 2025, Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu has made operational readiness, professionalism, innovation and joint operations central to his command philosophy.

Months down the line, these key derivatives on intelligence, surveillance, target acquisition and reconnaissance, as well as cooperation with other security agencies, has played central figures in responding to Nigeria’s changing security environment.

Which is why the operations carried out by the Nigerian Army, recorded specifically from July into the first week of September provide an early indication of how those priorities are being translated into activities by formations and units in the field.

Taken in a wider context, the NA, alongside other security agencies, conducted 7,062 operations nationwide in July and August, neutralised 1,487 terrorists and insurgents, arrested 354 suspects and rescued 777 kidnapped victims.

Rescue Operations Across Theatres

Across different theatres of operations, the NA troops carried out rescues with the most notable being the rescue of 21 abducted persons in Kogi State on August 31, including 15 National Youth Service Corps members who were abducted while travelling from Abuja to Bayelsa State.

The victims were rescued from the Egume and Ochaja forest areas of Dekina Local Government Area after troops of the Nigerian Army’s 12 Brigade joined other security agencies, hunters and vigilante groups in a search operation. In all, 21 victims, comprising eight males and 13 females, were rescued.

The Kogi operation was one of several rescue and security operations conducted by the Army and other security actors during the period. Between July 21 and 22, operations under Operation HADIN KAI, Operation FANSAN YAMMA and Operation MESA led to the rescue of 11 kidnapped persons and the arrest of 21 suspected terrorists, collaborators, logistics suppliers and drug peddlers.

Troops also discovered and destroyed improvised explosive devices during the operations, which covered Borno, Zamfara and Kogi states.

By August, the scale of some rescue operations had increased as a joint security operation in the Kainji Lake National Park area resulted in the rescue of 308 people. The operation involved multiple security actors and therefore cannot be attributed to the Nigerian Army alone.

The victims included 163 people abducted from Woro community in Kwara State and 145 others from Niger State. The operation highlighted the scale of kidnapping around forest and rural corridors linking parts of Kwara and Niger states, where security forces have had to conduct patrols over long distances and respond to intelligence on kidnapping gangs and other armed groups.

Notably, Kogi provided another test of rapid response as on September 2, two women were reportedly abducted from a farm in Ajodomodo Village in Dekina Local Government Area. Troops of the 21 Battalion Quick Reaction Force responded to a distress call and pursued the kidnappers towards Agbodakodo Forest. The pursuit forced the abductors to abandon the victims.

The women—a 15-year-old girl and a 30-year-old woman—were subsequently rescued and taken to the 21 Battalion Medical Reception Station for medical attention.

The two incidents within days of each other placed the response capabilities of troops in the area under pressure, with 12 Brigade and other Army units under 2 Division continuing to form part of the security response to kidnapping and other threats affecting Kogi and adjoining states.

Sustained Operations In The North-West.

The same operational priorities have been reflected in the North-West, where troops have continued operations against terrorists and bandits across Kaduna, Katsina and Zamfara states.

On September 4, troops of Operation FANSAN YAMMA rescued 25 kidnapped persons during separate operations in Katsina and Zamfara.

Two victims were rescued during a night patrol along the Kwanar Kura axis of Sabuwa Local Government Area in Katsina State after troops engaged fleeing terrorists.

In Zamfara, troops of Sector 2 rescued 23 civilians—three males and 20 females—during a fighting patrol on the outskirts of Wuya town in Anka Local Government Area.

Preliminary information indicated that the victims had been abducted from Gummi Local Government Area and had spent about three weeks in captivity. They were evacuated for medical attention and further debriefing.

The operations reflect the continued use of patrols, fighting patrols, engagements and intelligence-based responses against armed groups operating in the region.

Weapons Recovery and Disruption

The Nigerian Army’s recent operations have also focused on the weapons and logistics supporting terrorist and bandit activities.

During an ambush along the Kwanar Jolof axis of Shinkafi-Zurmi in Zamfara, troops engaged terrorists and recovered an RPG launcher, an AK-47 rifle, magazines and ammunition.

In another operation in Kaduna State, troops intercepted a vehicle carrying 793 rounds of ammunition concealed in a sack of grain. The operation was aimed at disrupting the movement of weapons to criminal elements.

Other recent operations in the North-West also resulted in the recovery of weapons, ammunition and motorcycles from terrorists. The seizures form part of efforts to restrict the movement of arms and ammunition to armed groups operating across the region.

The Wider Picture

Army formations remain engaged in several major security theatres. In the North-East, troops continue counter-insurgency operations against Boko Haram and ISWAP. In the North-West and North-Central, formations are conducting operations against banditry and kidnapping, while other Army units remain involved in security operations in the South-East and other parts of the country.

P.R.O.S.E and the Field Results

The pattern of operations from July into the first week of September provides a basis for examining the application of the COAS’ strategic framework.

From the rescue of 21 people in Kogi on August 31, to the recovery of an RPG launcher, AK-47 rifle and ammunition in Zamfara, the interception of 793 rounds of ammunition in Kaduna, and the rescue of 25 kidnapped persons in Katsina and Zamfara on September 4, the operations have continued into the first week of September.

In the North-West, Operation FANSAN YAMMA has combined patrols, ambushes, fighting patrols, intelligence-led operations and weapons recovery against terrorist and bandit groups.

Essentially, these activities correspond with key elements of Lieutenant General Shaibu’s P.R.O.S.E framework- Professional Excellence, Operational Readiness and Strategic Cooperation and Exemplary Leadership.

Taken together, the activities provide an early operational record against which the priorities set out in Shaibu’s command philosophy can be assessed, with troops continuing to conduct rescue operations, patrols, arrests, engagements and weapons recovery across multiple theatres.

World.title: AVM Suleh Charges NAF Personnel to Embrace Sportsmanship as Vital Ingredient of National Security
World.content:
Chiemelie Ezeobi

The Air Officer Commanding (AOC), Logistics Command, Air Vice Marshal Abubakar Suleh, has urged Nigerian Air Force personnel to embrace sportsmanship as part of their professional responsibility, describing it as a vital ingredient for strengthening the nation’s security architecture.

Air Vice Marshal Suleh made the call in Lagos at the closing ceremony of the 2026 Third Quarter Headquarters Intra-Command Sports Competition, organised for personnel of Logistics Command and co-located units in the Lagos area.

Air Vice Marshal Suleh said the competition showcased teamwork, endurance and tactical excellence across football, volleyball, basketball and handball, reflecting the qualities required of a combat-ready force.

According to him, the quarterly sporting event is more than a contest for medals and trophies; it is a true test of resilience, discipline and unity.

He noted that the initiative aligns with the Chief of the Air Staff’s command philosophy of promoting physical fitness, mental alertness and high morale among personnel.

Air Vice Marshal Suleh added that a capable fighting force is built not only in classrooms and operational theatres but also on the sports field, where esprit de corps is developed and strengthened.

The AOC congratulated all participating teams and athletes for their discipline, fair play and determination, while the captain of the winning Logistics football team, Sergeant Idoko Emmanuel, thanked God for the team’s victory. Senior officers from various arms of the Nigerian Armed Forces attended the event.

The week-long competition was held across three venues — the NAFOM Gym, AMAO Court and ATO Field — and featured four competing groups: Group A, comprising HQ Logistics Command, 641 Communications, AFSS Ikeja and 613 FPG; Group B, made up of 643 ESD, 661 NAFH, 081 PAG/DOP and AETSC; Group C, comprising 651 BSG, 057 PIG, 051 PMG and 015 SIG; and Group D, comprising 631 ACMD, NADC, 304 HAG and 355 RW.

At the close of the tournament, organisers released an official medal table showing results across all four disciplines. In basketball, Group D won Gold, Group B took Silver, and Group A settled for Bronze.

In volleyball, Group D again claimed Gold, with Group B taking Silver and Group A Bronze. In handball, Group B won Gold, Group A took Silver, and Group D settled for Bronze.

In football, Group A emerged Gold medallists, Group B took Silver, and Group C claimed Bronze.

Tallying medals across all four sports, Group D finished with 2 Gold and 1 Bronze to top the overall standings in 1st position. Group B followed in 2nd place with 1 Gold and 3 Silver medals.

Group A placed 3rd overall with 1 Gold, 1 Silver and 2 Bronze medals. Group C finished 4th, with a single Bronze medal from the football event.

World.title: Report: Arthur Zwane for Bafana Bafana assistant coaching job
World.content:
Arthur Zwane represents AmaZulu in the Betway Premiership. Image: Official PSL

Mosimane’s Bafana Bafana technical team is not yet complete. A new coach looks to add more hands to his backroom staff.

Arthur Zwane’s name has reportedly moved to the top of the list, According to iDiski Times‘ leading reporter Sinethemba Makonco.

The coach, affectionately known as “10111”, could now be handed a major opportunity with the national team.



BAFANA BAFANA’S NEW TECHNICAL TEAM IS TAKING SHAPE

Mosimane has moved quickly to assemble a high-performance backroom team at Bafana Bafana. At the heart of his setup are long-time assistants Musi Matlaba and Kabelo Rangoaga.

Matlaba serves as an assistant coach with a strong focus on match analysis, data interpretation and player-tracking metrics.

Rangoaga, meanwhile, combines his assistant coaching responsibilities with a focus on conditioning and fitness.



Although both have traditionally been associated with analysis and physical preparation, Mosimane has stressed that they have continued their coaching education.

They are therefore able to operate as fully qualified coaches within his technical structure.

The latest major addition came with the arrival of Morena Ramoreboli.



The highly regarded coach left his position as head coach of the Botswana national team, known as The Zebras, to return to the Bafana Bafana setup.

Ramoreboli brings extensive Southern African experience to the team.

He also has a reputation for tactical flexibility and has achieved success at both club and international level. His arrival sees him replace outgoing assistant Helman Mkhalele.



Meanwhile, Arthur Zwane is expected to finish the crew.

ARTHUR ZWANE’S LONG COACHING JOURNEY

Zwane made the transition from legendary player to coach after retiring in 2010.

He immediately joined Kaizer Chiefs‘ technical team as an assistant under Vladimir Vermezovic, remaining in that role until 2012.



He was then moved into the club’s academy. For almost a decade, Zwane worked across the U15, U17 and U19 structures before eventually taking charge of the Kaizer Chiefs reserve team.

His work with the youngsters earned him a return to the senior setup in 2020. Zwane served as an assistant to Gavin Hunt, Stuart Baxter and Molefi Ntseki.

He notably took temporary charge during the 2020/21 campaign, helping Kaizer Chiefs reach the CAF Champions League final.



In May 2022, Zwane was appointed permanent head coach on a three-year contract. However, after a difficult 2022/23 campaign, he was moved back into an assistant role before later returning to the academy.

A new chapter began in October 2024. Zwane left Kaizer Chiefs and joined AmaZulu FC as co-coach alongside Vusumuzi Vilakazi.

Following Vilakazi’s departure, Zwane became the club’s sole head coach.



He subsequently helped stabilise AmaZulu FC, guiding the Durban outfit to an impressive sixth-place finish in the 2024/25 Betway Premiership season.

That result secured Usuthu a place in the MTN8. Zwane’s work also earned him a contract extension.

World.title: SASSA grant helps Eastern Cape pensioner pay rent, but it is not enough
World.content:
Dwyer, in his sixties, has received the SASSA Older Person’s Grant for between one and three years, relying on the R2 400 monthly payment to cover his single biggest cost: rent.

Dwyer lives alone and rents privately, with no dependents drawing on his income. He told The South African that his grant “helps but it is not enough,” and said only a small amount typically remains once rent and essentials are paid. His biggest financial concern right now is the cost of living and rising food prices, a pressure echoed by pensioners nationwide as inflation continues to erode the value of fixed grant payments.

Additionally, despite the financial strain, Dwyer said he has never had anyone in his household go without food, a small relief in a system where many recipients report the opposite. He receives his grant directly into his Absa account and confirmed the process has been straightforward, with no payment issues to report. He rated SASSA’s communication with recipients as adequate.



No extra support sought due to lack of information

Dwyer said he has never applied for any additional government assistance beyond his Older Person’s Grant, explaining simply that he did not know what else was available. It’s a gap that experts say affects many elderly recipients, who often remain unaware of supplementary programmes that could ease pressure on their fixed incomes.

Asked what single change he would make to the system, his answer matched that of countless other pensioners: increase the grant amount.

A quiet struggle shared by many

Dwyer’s story carries none of the drama of a grant dispute or payment delay. Instead, it reflects a quieter concern facing South Africa’s elderly: doing everything right, receiving the support they’re entitled to, and still finding it falls short. Also, with rent, food and transport costs climbing steadily, pensioners on fixed incomes are increasingly forced into difficult trade-offs each month.

Dwyer’s experience adds to a growing body of testimony from Older Person’s Grant recipients calling for the payment to be reviewed. For now, he continues to manage on what he receives, prioritising a roof over his head above all else.

World.title: Viewers praise MaDlamini for standing up to her ‘bully’ husband
World.content:
In an episode that aired on 5 September 2026, fans of Umndeni Somnala on Moja Love absolutely loved how Sindisiwe MaDlamini, the second wife of popular polygamist and KZN Bishop Hamilton “Somnala” Nala, defended herself against her husband.

MADLAMINI APPLAUDED FOR BEING BRAVE

Following last week’s reprimanding spree on 29 August, Somnala turned his wrath towards MaDlamini. He accused her of being “disrespectful” towards the first wife, MaMbatha, as well as a guest at in their house.

However, in her diary session, MaMbatha clarified that it was actually MaNjomane who disrespected her, not MaDlamini, as their husband had stated.



Another bombshell from Somnala was his claim that MaDlamini had aborted their baby, which she vehemently denied, clarifying that she actually suffered a miscarriage, not an abortion as he believed.

Viewers perceived MaDlamini’s stance as a powerful moment, praising her for standing up to her husband, whom they view as a bully.

MaDlamini once again squared up with her husband after claiming that she had affairs with foreigners and didn’t reprimand male listeners who made advances during her church radio show.

Somnala also accused her of being “useless” in their family business, where she managed the IT department.

In her defense, MaDlamini emphasised that she worked hard for her education and was shocked by the “useless” label attached to her.

VIEWERS PRAISE MADLAMINI FOR STANDING UP FOR HERSELF

In a video posted by Ma Shinga on Facebook, she praised MaDlamini for mustering the strength to stand up to her husband. She wrote:



“Madlamini stood up to the bully, and she made me proud. I’m glad she left because WOW. Lendoda (this man) was not reprimanding her, he was destroying her dignity on camera, in front of all the wives. Some words can never be taken back.”

Ayanda KaMabaso Nzuza: MaDlamini, sisterhood is proud of you for standing up for yourself against that bully.

Nomthandazo Sibanyoni: MaDlamini for President. Love her.

MoMo Wa Banana Mafereka: Finally, he met his match MaDlamini for President.

Fortunate Ngwenya: I watched it twice this morning. She dealt with him nicely.

Tana Princess Mtolo: [I] am proud of you MaDlamini.

World.title: Durban teacher turns down R50k reward after finding missing pilot
World.content:
A Durban teacher turned down a R50 000 reward for helping to find missing pilot Slade Thomas on Monday, 7 September, after his disappearance over the weekend.

The woman claimed the discovery was down to divine intervention.

DURBAN TEACHER SAYS NO TO R50K REWARD

Speaking to Northglen News, Lezé van der Walt, a teacher at Northlands Primary School, shared how she tracked down missing pilot, Slade Thomas, on Monday morning.



She shared: “I had my five-year-old son with me, and that morning I had asked God to guide me and take me to find this man (Slade Thomas). I don’t always take Norrie Avenue on my route to school but [that] morning I did. It was like the holy spirit stopped me as I rounded the bend in the road.

“I saw a man fairly hidden, sitting in the bushes with his legs crossed. He matched the description I had seen on the missing poster on social media. I stopped next to the road and asked him what his name was. Initially, he gave me a false name but I think he wanted to be left alone. I then called the number listed for the people looking for him. I was so happy when they arrived to help reunite him,” she said.

The mother-of-one shared that divine intervention had led her to find Thomas, and as a result, turned down a R50 000 reward offered by his family.



The God-fearing woman is not the only one who turned down the cash. According to PI Brad Nathanson Investigations, a host of Durban volunteers, as well as emergency services, worked tirelessly together to look for the missing man.

MISSING PILOT’S MENTAL HEALTH ISSUES

In the past few years, Slade Thomas, a former Durban helicopter pilot in the South African Air Force (SAAF), had suffered from significant memory loss.

Family spokesperson Greg Parry told the media that said Thomas had also been living with mental illness and depression



Parry stated that Thomas’s disappearance was out of character, which had sparked concerns for his safety and well-being.

He told The Witness: “We are profoundly grateful to the many people, community members and security teams who have given up hours of their time to search for Slade and support our family.

“Their kindness, compassion and determination have meant more to us than we can express”.

World.title: Weather: Morning fog and cloudy spells to shape Wednesday’s conditions

World.title: Kaizer Chiefs news: The latest on Langelihle Phili’s injury
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs winger Langelihle Phili is set to begin his rehabilitation as he works his way back from an ankle injury.

The 21-year-old suffered the injury in training last month and is expected to be sidelined for at least another month.

Phili joined Chiefs from Stellenbosch at the start of the season and made an immediate impact after arriving at Naturena. His injury came at a time when he was beginning to find his rhythm with Amakhosi.



Chiefs coach Fernando Da Cruz has now provided an update on the winger’s condition.

Phili has enjoyed life at Kaizer Chiefs so far

“He’s an important player for us, for that we signed him,” Da Cruz said.

“For the moment he didn’t work during 10 days and now he’s starting his rehabilitation.

“Technically he’s a good player. He’s a player who is able to make a difference, a player who’s able to eliminate 1 vs 1.

“But also, we have other players we work, we are trusting them and we create chances, it’s not a problem. Our main issue is we are not enough killer inside the two box.”

While Phili remains sidelined, Chiefs can call on Faiz Abrahams, who also joined the club from Stellenbosch.



Phili’s return will be welcomed by Da Cruz, although Chiefs continue to deal with several injury concerns.

Paseka Mako, Bradley Cross, Nkhayiso Shinga and Khanyisa Mayo are among the other players currently sidelined. Despite the injuries, Amakhosi are third in the Betway Premiership behind Mamelodi Sundowns and Orlando Pirates.

Can Chiefs fight for the league?

World.title: Court day turned to war of words in Matlala' trial
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - What should have been a normal end to the court day turned into a war of words when chaos erupted in the trial within a trial in the attempted murder case against Vusimuzi 'Cat' Matlala and his co-accused.

A verbal altercation between police, the accused, and their counsel ensued.

Matlala and his co-accused wanted to consult their lawyers before being taken down to holding cells but were prevented by some members of the task force responsible for transporting them.

Matlala’s lawyer, Annelene van den Heever, lambasted the action, saying the aggression was unnecessary.

READ | From hospital threat to gunfire: Key evidence in Matlala trial

This resulted in Judge Cassim Moosa making an order.

He said the accused's legal representatives are entitled at all times to consult with their clients in court.

Earlier on, the state had requested a postponement after the defence submitted a document detailing the movement of 15 police cars that were involved in the arrest of alleged hitman Musa Kekana.

READ | Matlala trial: Court to hear police version of alleged hitman’s arrest

The prosecutor argued the sudden disclosure amounted to an ambush.

Judge Moosa sided with the prosecution, saying that the State is entitled to a reasonable opportunity to apply its mind to the document.

The trial within a trial resume on Thursday.

World.title: 354 arrested as government turns up heat on illegal activities
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - A total of 354 people has been arrested and 123 cases enrolled in court following multidisciplinary operations across the country.

These operations targeted fraudulent documentation, labour exploitation, human trafficking networks, illegal mining and other forms of organised crime linked to migration vulnerabilities.

This was revealed by Inter-Ministerial Committee chairperson Mmamoloko Kubayi, as she provided an update on the government's handling of the migration issue on Tuesday.

According to Kubayi, the operations have also seen more than 350,000 inspections carried out across the country.

READ | WATCH | Construction site and fast-food outlet in one, KZN cracks whip on

These inspections have, she said, targeted a range of industries, including factories, supermarkets, and spaza shops.

She said many of these were found to be non-compliant with labour- and health-related standards and legal prescripts, especially the employment of illegal immigrants.

“We are continuing with this important work and once again would like to warn employers to respect the laws of the country and desist from deliberately employing illegal immigrants in their firms and factories,”

Kubayi said they have redeployed experienced officials for these operations, adding to the department's commitment to what Kubayi called a ‘zero-tolerance approach to criminality irrespective of nationality’

World.title: Spring Day murder accused abandons bail
World.content:
PRETORIA -The man accused of murdering a 21-year-old boy following an altercation during Spring Day celebrations in Refilwe, Cullinan to remain behind bars.

This comes after he abandoned his bail application.

The 53-year-old man appeared before the Cullinan Magistrate's Court on charges of murder, where his matter was then postponed to 27 October for further investigations.

READ | Spring Day celebrations turn deadly in Tshwane

According to National Prosecution Authority (NPA) spokesperson Lumka Mahanjana on 1 September 2026, a group of young people in Refilwe Extension 3 were celebrating Spring Day by pouring water on one another and on people passing by.

Mahanjana said it is alleged that while the accused was walking past, the group attempted to pour water on him.

"He allegedly took out a knife and stabbed the deceased. The deceased was taken to a local clinic, where he later succumbed to his injuries," she said.

The accused was arrested on the same day after he was allegedly apprehended and assaulted by members of the community.
