World.title: Russian senator claims Hungary was forced to “prove its loyalty” to Brussels
World.content:
Hungary has expelled 10 Russian diplomats accused of carrying out activities incompatible with diplomatic status, in a move that could mark a significant change in Budapest’s approach to Russian intelligence operations. Moscow has already warned of a “tough and painful” response. The deputy speaker of Russia’s upper house of parliament said that the decision was an unfriendly and confrontational act.

Hungary has ordered 10 Russian diplomatic personnel to leave the country after authorities determined that they had engaged in activities deemed unacceptable under the Vienna Convention.

Foreign Minister Anita Orbán announced the decision on Tuesday, saying the Foreign Ministry had informed Russia’s ambassador in Budapest that Hungarian authorities had identified activities by 10 members of the Russian diplomatic mission that were incompatible with their diplomatic status.

“The decision protects Hungary’s security and sovereignty,” Orbán said, while stressing that the move does not amount to a severing of diplomatic relations with Russia. Hungary, she added, intends to maintain the necessary dialogue with Moscow based on mutual respect and compliance with international rules.

Expert: The diplomats were Russian intelligence officers

According to Russia expert András Rácz, the wording used by the Hungarian government strongly indicates that the 10 individuals were actually Russian intelligence officers operating under diplomatic cover. Rácz, deputy director-general responsible for research and academic affairs at the Hungarian Institute of International Affairs, told MTI that the phrase “activities incompatible with diplomatic status” traditionally refers to espionage.

In practical terms, he said, Hungary has expelled 10 Russian diplomats who were allegedly working as intelligence officers under diplomatic cover in Budapest.

The scale of the move is particularly significant. According to Rácz, more than 600 Russian intelligence officers operating under diplomatic cover have been expelled from EU member states since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

Until now, Hungary had been the only EU member state not to carry out such a large-scale expulsion. Rácz therefore described the decision as Hungary effectively joining its EU and NATO allies in efforts to reduce Russia’s intelligence capabilities across the bloc.

Never miss a headline: join Daily News Hungary’s official WhatsApp channel!

Why has Hungary acted now?

The timing of the expulsions is particularly noteworthy given Hungary’s historically close relationship with Moscow under the previous Orbán government.

Rácz said he could not determine precisely why Budapest had chosen this particular moment to act. However, he argued that the decision represents a significant shift in Hungary’s position towards Russian intelligence activities. He also pointed out that, according to official Foreign Ministry figures, 47 Russian diplomats are currently accredited in Hungary, accompanied by 41 spouses.

It is not publicly known how many of the remaining diplomats are connected to Russian intelligence services. However, Rácz noted that a Russian investigative outlet recently identified 15 of the 47 Russian diplomats in Budapest as having links to various Russian intelligence agencies based on publicly available information.

He added that while there had been some “quiet expulsions” of Russian intelligence personnel during the previous Hungarian government, there had never before been a publicly announced expulsion on this scale.

Budapest sends a message to its Western allies

The decision could have implications beyond Hungary’s bilateral relationship with Russia. Rácz argued that Russian intelligence officers based in Hungary can potentially operate elsewhere in the Schengen Area, making their presence a security concern for Hungary’s allies as well. He pointed to Prague as a previous example of how Russian diplomats could use one European capital as a base for intelligence operations in neighbouring countries.

According to the expert, Russian intelligence personnel operating from Budapest have similarly been able to conduct operations elsewhere in the Schengen Area and in Balkan countries outside the zone.

For this reason, Rácz described Hungary’s decision as a long-overdue step towards its EU and NATO partners. He argued that Hungary’s failure to expel such personnel over the previous four and a half years had potentially harmed the security interests of its allies.

Moscow threatens retaliation

Russia has responded angrily to the expulsions. Konstantin Kosachev, deputy speaker of Russia’s upper house of parliament, told the RIA Novosti news agency that the decision was an unfriendly and confrontational act. He argued that the simultaneous expulsion of 10 diplomats was “many times more unfriendly” and amounted to an open challenge to Moscow. Russia, he said, would respond accordingly.

Kosachev also claimed that the decision had been driven by Brussels, arguing that the “post-Orbán” Hungary had been pressured to demonstrate its loyalty to what he described as the anti-Russian policies of the EU and NATO.

Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova likewise warned that Moscow would deliver a “tough and painful response”, referring to what she called the “Russophobic lobby” in Budapest. A reciprocal move is therefore widely expected, with Rácz saying Russia is almost certain to respond proportionally by expelling Hungarian diplomats.

World.title: Hungary waves goodbye to historical county titles, and reintroduces modern forms
World.content:
Hungary’s Parliament has voted to restore the terms “county” and “government commissioner”, reversing the controversial renaming of counties and government commissioners introduced by Viktor Orbán’s Fidesz government in 2022.

Historical titles are gone

The Tisza-majority Parliament approved the legislation on Tuesday with 134 votes in favour and 52 against. Fidesz, the Christian Democrats (KDNP) and Mi Hazánk (Our Homeland) voted against the proposal. Under the changes, Hungary’s vármegyék (literally translated to castle counties) will once again officially be known as megyék, while főispáns (lord lieutenants) will again be referred to as government commissioners.

The 2022 terminology was introduced as part of the 11th amendment to Hungary’s Fundamental Law. The Fidesz government argued at the time that restoring the historical term vármegye would preserve the constitutional traditions of Hungary’s thousand-year statehood, strengthen national unity and reinforce the national character of Hungarian democracy.

Government cites clarity and practicality

The newly adopted legislation takes a different approach, stressing practical and legal considerations. According to the proposal, abandoning the terms vármegye and főispán will make the administrative system more transparent and easier to understand, while promoting consistent application of the law.

The changes are primarily terminological and technical. They do not alter the powers or responsibilities of the affected authorities, nor do they change the substance of administrative, regulatory or local-government relationships. The law will enter into force on the day after its promulgation, while amendments changing the terminology in other legislation will take effect on 1 October.

Never miss a headline: join Daily News Hungary’s official WhatsApp channel!

From historic tradition to a controversial revival

The term vármegye has deep roots in Hungarian history. It was used for a fundamental administrative unit from the foundation of the Hungarian state until 1949, although the county system developed gradually over several centuries. The system underwent major reforms in the late 19th century, including a significant administrative restructuring between 1876 and 1881.

County boundaries changed repeatedly, including before the Treaty of Trianon. The historical name survived these changes and remained in use after Trianon and during the years following the Second World War. It was officially replaced by megye in 1949, when Hungary adopted a new constitution modelled on the Soviet system.

Stay up-do-date: Hungary orders 10 Russian embassy staff to leave – UPDATE: Russia’s threat

Lázár once opposed the name change

Interestingly, János Lázár, who was a senior minister in Orbán’s fifth government, voted in favour of the 2022 renaming despite having previously criticised the idea. When the change was considered during the drafting of the Fundamental Law in 2011, Lázár argued that the historical term carried negative associations for many Hungarians, particularly those whose families had worked as servants or labourers.

He eventually supported the 2022 change, saying he did so because it formed part of the constitutional amendment before Parliament. The latest vote now reverses that decision, bringing Hungary’s official administrative terminology back to the terms used between 1949 and 2022.

World.title: New documents reveal why Orbán minister Lázár kept his Switzerland trip a secret for 13 years
World.content:
After more than 13 years, new documents have shed light on one of the longest-running mysteries surrounding Hungarian politician János Lázár: what he was doing in Zurich on 22 and 23 March 2013. The details were revealed by investigative outlet Direkt36, which obtained an internal government document from the Tisza government, which took office this spring.

Newly revealed documents show what János Lázár was doing in 2013

According to the document, Lázár, who was then heading the Prime Minister’s Office as a state secretary, met a person identified as “Prof. Mangold” in Zurich to discuss potential cooperation between the Hungarian government and Western European companies.

Direkt36 says the name almost certainly refers to Klaus Mangold, a prominent German businessman with extensive contacts in European and Russian business circles. Mangold established links with the Hungarian government in the early 2010s and later worked as an adviser to Viktor Orbán’s governments. The newly released report was prepared by his consultancy, Mangold Consulting GmbH.

Never miss a headline: join Daily News Hungary’s official WhatsApp channel!

Rothschild, SAP and government communications

The report says Lázár and Mangold discussed three main areas. The first was whether Rothschild could act as an “independent adviser” to the Hungarian government, including assessing the country’s financial risks and advising on the banking sector. A meeting involving then Economy Minister Mihály Varga and newly appointed central bank governor György Matolcsy was reportedly planned, with Orbán himself potentially attending part of the meeting.

The pair also discussed cooperation with business software giant SAP, particularly in financial administration and healthcare. The third topic was the Hungarian government’s marketing strategy. The report mentions German consultancy firms Schuppner and CNC, which Mangold was said to know well and which could advise on responding to critical media. A joint brainstorming session was reportedly proposed.

Rothschild later did work for the Orbán government, including producing a report during the European Union’s investigation into the Paks II nuclear project. The report concluded that the investment could be economically viable under market conditions. Rothschild also later participated in the creation of the partly state-owned MBH Bank.

Stay up-to-date: Hungary orders 10 Russian embassy staff to leave – UPDATE: Russia’s threat

A mystery that began with expensive hotel bills

The Zurich trip had attracted attention because of its unusually high costs. Lázár and his companion spent HUF 189,000 on one night’s accommodation in Zurich. Two other trips also raised questions: HUF 596,000 for one night in Milan and HUF 920,000 for two nights in England.

At the time, Lázár’s office refused to reveal the purpose of the trips, citing national security concerns. Lázár was also responsible for Hungary’s foreign intelligence service. Journalist András Pethő, then working for Origo, sued for access to the information. The case became politically explosive and contributed to pressure on Origo’s editorial team. Editor-in-chief Gergő Sáling was later dismissed, prompting many journalists, including Pethő, to leave the outlet.

Lázár eventually repaid the travel expenses, but the purpose of the Zurich meeting remained secret for years. The former minister declined to comment to Direkt36. Mangold’s consultancy also refused media questions, while SAP said it was unaware of any cooperation linked to the meeting. Rothschild and CNC did not respond.

World.title: Breaking: Hungary orders 10 Russian embassy staff to leave – UPDATE: Russia’s threat
World.content:
Hungary has ordered 10 employees of the Russian Embassy in Budapest to leave the country, saying their activities were incompatible with the conduct expected of diplomats under the Vienna Convention. A spokesperson for the Russian Foreign Ministry said Budapest should expect a “harsh and painful response”.

FM Orbán announces letting go of 10 embassy employees

Foreign Minister Anita Orbán announced the decision, describing it as unprecedented in scale. She said the relevant official at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs had informed Russia’s ambassador to Budapest of the decision on her instructions. According to Orbán, the Hungarian authorities assessed that the 10 representatives had engaged in activities that were not acceptable for diplomats under the Vienna Convention.

“The decision protects Hungary’s security and sovereignty,” the minister said. She stressed, however, that the move does not mean a break in diplomatic relations with the Kremlin. Hungary intends to maintain the necessary dialogue with Moscow, provided that both sides respect one another and comply with international rules.

UPDATE: Russia’s threat

Russia will respond to Hungary’s expulsion of ten Russian diplomats, according to the Russian state news agency TASS, citing a statement from the Russian Foreign Ministry. Maria Zakharova, spokesperson for the Russian Foreign Ministry, promised a “harsh and painful response.”

“The response to the Russophobic lobby in Budapest will be harsh and painful,” she told TASS.

A tougher approach towards Moscow

The expulsions mark a notably tougher public response towards Russian diplomatic activity than previous measures taken by Hungary. Péter Magyar also raised the announcement in Parliament, reading out Orbán’s statement and saying that a Tisza government would protect Hungary’s sovereignty, reports Telex.

Anita Orbán has adopted a more distant diplomatic approach towards Russia than her predecessor, Péter Szijjártó, according to the supplied sources. On 13 May, shortly after taking office, she summoned Russia’s ambassador following a Russian drone attack against Transcarpathia. Szijjártó had last summoned a Russian diplomat in February 2022. The latest move also follows reports of a quieter expulsion of a Russian intelligence officer earlier this year.

Never miss a headline: join Daily News Hungary’s official WhatsApp channel!

Kremlin intelligence officer reportedly expelled in May

VSquare reported in May that Artur Sushkov, allegedly a Russian intelligence officer operating under diplomatic cover at the Embassy in Budapest, left Hungary on 4 May. According to the report, Hungary’s Constitutional Protection Office had established that Sushkov had spent years collecting information on institutions close to the Hungarian government. VSquare’s government sources claimed that Hungarian intelligence had recommended his expulsion as early as February, but that the previous Orbán government had blocked the proposal.

Stay up-to-date: FM Anita Orbán reports progress on minority rights for Hungarians in Ukraine

2018 Skripal case provides a different precedent

Hungary also expelled a Russian diplomat in 2018 following the poisoning of former Kremlin intelligence officer Sergei Skripal in Britain. However, a subsequent Direkt36 investigation suggested that Budapest deliberately handled the expulsion in a way that would minimise damage to its close relationship with Moscow.

Diplomatic sources reportedly said the expelled Russian was a GRU military intelligence officer whose posting was due to end within months. The latest decision is considerably larger in scale, as the 10 embassy employees have now been ordered to leave Hungary. Despite this, Budapest insists that diplomatic relations with Moscow will continue, with the government presenting the expulsions as a measure to protect Hungary’s security and sovereignty rather than a move towards severing ties with Russia.

World.title: Ratko Mladic’s Lavish Funeral was an Indictment of Serbia’s Govt: Experts
World.content:

Criticism has echoed across Europe over the high-profile funeral of Ratko Mladic on Monday in Belgrade, raising questions about the potential repercussions for Serbia of giving a convicted war criminal a hero’s farewell.

His funeral with military honours was attended by senior officials of Serbia and Bosnia’s mainly Serb entity, Republika Srpska.

World.title: Montenegro Prosecutors Open Case Against Bishop for Praising Mladic
World.content:
Montenegro’s Higher State Prosecutor’s Office in Podgorica has opened a case against a Serbian Orthodox Bishop after he praised the late convicted war criminal Ratko Mladic during a religious service, the Vijesti newspaper reported on Tuesday.

The prosecutor’s office told the newspaper that the bishop was suspected of inciting national, racial and religious hatred. It did not provide further details about the investigation or say whether Bishop Metodije of Budimlje-Niksic Diocese had been questioned.

The bishop praised Mladic during a service at the Piva Monastery in northern Montenegro on August 28, the day after he died, saying people had recognised in Mladic “all those wonderful and holy qualities of Serbian warriors and knights.

“May the most holy Mother of God … raise his soul among all the holy Serbian knights, the famous general Ratko,” Metodije said, according to a recording and transcript published by local media.

The diocese later published a statement on its website saying that, after the liturgy, a memorial service had been held for “the newly departed servant of God, General Ratko Mladic”.

At the same time, Montenegro’s Higher State Prosecutor’s Office in Bijelo Polje has dismissed criminal complaints against Metodije over speeches praising a notorious World War II-era Nazi-alligned commander, Pavle Djurisic, held responsible for mass killings during the war, Vijesti reported on Tuesday.

Mladic, who died on August 27, while serving a life sentence at the UN detention facility in the Hague, commanded Bosnian Serb forces during the 1992-95 war in Bosnia. He was convicted of genocide, crimes against humanity and war crimes by a United Nations tribunal and sentenced to life imprisonment.

The tribunal found him responsible for various crimes including the 1995 massacre of more than 8,000 Bosniaks in Srebrenica – Europe’s worst atrocity since World War II, and the prolonged siege of Sarajevo.

Mladic remains a hero to many Serbs, while victims’ families and survivors regard him as responsible for some of the 1992-95 Bosnian war’s gravest crimes.

Montenegro, a NATO member and candidate for European Union membership, has laws criminalising the incitement of ethnic, racial and religious hatred.

World.title: Turkey’s Ruling Party Seizes Back Control of Important Mayoralty
World.content:
Dundar Ziya Gultekin, candidate of President Recep Tayyip Erdogan’s Justice and Development Party, AKP, was elected as acting Mayor of Uskudar on Tuesday, defeating Sibel Tan Cetinkaya, the joint candidate of the opposition Republican People’s Party, CHP, and the New Party.

The vote in Uskudar followed the arrest and removal from office of the elected CHP mayor, Sinem Dedetas, in July on alleged corruption charges. Gultekin will serve as acting mayor, as he was elected by the municipal council rather than by popular vote.

The result came after a dramatic shift in the council’s balance. Four councillors elected for the main opposition CHP defected to the AKP days before the vote, while two CHP councillors were detained and so unable to vote.

This left the rival blocs with 21 councillors each. Yet, Gultekin received 23 votes in the secret ballot, indicating that two councillors from the CHP-New Party bloc also backed the AKP candidate. Their identities remain unknown.

“They told people elected from our lists: ‘Either join the AKP or go to prison, either wear the party badge or wear handcuffs,’” Ozgur Celik, Istanbul Provincial Chair of the New Party said after the vote, alleging that some councillors defected because they feared arrest.

The New Party, which cooperated with the CHP in the Uskudar vote, was established earlier this year by Ozgur Ozel and other politicians who broke away from the CHP after a controversial court ruling annulled the 2023 party congress over alleged irregularities, removing Ozel as leader and reinstating his predecessor, Kemal Kilicdaroglu.

Uskudar is a traditional conservative stronghold and was ruled by the AKP and other conservative and Islamist parties for decades. However, the AKP lost the district and major cities and towns in the 2024 local elections.

Uskudar is located on the Asian side of Istanbul and is home to more than half a million people.

Cetinkaya initially won a mayoral election in August, but a court ordered a rerun following an AKP challenge.

Over the last year, dozens of CHP mayors and hundreds of party members have been arrested on corruption and terror charges. Those include the arrest of Istanbul’s Mayor and opposition presidential candidate Ekrem Imamoglu on March 19, 2025. The prosecutor’s office is demanding a 2,352-year prison sentence for him. Imamoglu denies all the accusations.

Opposition politicians, rights groups and international organisations have said that the government is using the judiciary to crush political rivals in what they describe as an unprecedented crackdown.

World.title: Kosovo Parliament to Reconvene, ‘Chaos’ Looms over Election of President
World.content:
Kosovo’s new parliament reconvenes for its inaugural session on Wednesday, despite continued uncertainty over whether lawmakers will agree on the election of a head-of-state.

The session started on August 6, following elections in June, but was paused after the victorious Vetevendosje party asked for “more time” for negotiations with other parties on the candidate for Kosovo’s next president.

At the end of the month, Vetevendosje leader Albin Kurti and his counterpart from the opposition Democratic League of Kosovo, LDK, Lumir Abdixhiku announced that their parties would both back Judge Bekim Sejdiu as president, only for a third of the LDK’s MPs to cry foul.

Such is the depth of animosity between Vetevendosje and its rivals, constituting parliament and electing a president has become a major challenge, complicated by a rift within the LDK over Abdixhiku’s leadership.

World.title: Albanian Port Bars Alleged Russian-Linked ‘Shadow Fleet’ Oil Tanker
World.content:
The Harbour Master’s Office in the Albanian port of Durres has barred the oil tanker Hanuman from entering the port after Ukraine’s military intelligence identified the vessel as part of Russia’s so-called “shadow fleet”, which Moscow uses to transport oil and petroleum products and evade sanctions.

The Intelligence Directorate at Ukraine’s Ministry of Defence, known as the GUR, welcomed Albania’s move as an example of international cooperation in enforcing sanctions and restricting maritime routes used by Moscow to export oil.

“Albania’s decision not to allow the ‘Hanuman’ to enter its port is an important demonstration of international solidarity in enforcing sanctions,” the GUR said.

“Joint actions by Ukraine and its foreign partners are steadily limiting the Kremlin’s ability to use maritime trade routes to circumvent sanctions, forcing the aggressor state to take responsibility for its actions,” it added.

The Hanuman was flying under the flag of Sierra Leone when it was barred from entering Durres port on August 29.

Data published by the GUR shows that since the start of 2025, the Hanuman has transported at least 452,000 tonnes of fuel out of Russia.

Most of its voyages originated from Novorossiysk, one of Russia’s main Black Sea ports, with destinations including Turkey, Senegal, the United Arab Emirates and a ship-to-ship transfer area near the Italian city of Augusta.

The GUR claims a Russian company, Altoprae Marine, based in Novorossiysk, provided logistical support for these voyages, which it links to a manager from the circle of sanctioned Russian oligarch Gennady Timchenko, a longtime ally of Russian President Vladimir Putin.

The GUR also links Altoprae Marine to the operations of vessels owned by Rosewood Shipping, which Ukrainian authorities claim is controlled by Oksana Marchenko, the wife of pro-Russian Ukrainian politician Viktor Medvedchuk, a longtime ally of Putin.

Russia’s so-called “shadow fleet” consists of a network of tankers it uses to keep its oil exports moving after Western sanctions were imposed over its full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

These vessels often operate under the flags of third countries and through ownership structures that are difficult to trace.

The G7 countries and the European Union introduced a price cap on Russian seaborne oil in late 2022, along with restrictions on insurance, financing and other services related to its transport.

Albania, an EU candidate country and NATO member, has aligned itself with the EU’s sanctions against Russia since the start of its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

Maritime traffic data show that the Hanuman previously visited the Port of Durres in November 2025.

A BIRN investigation published in May 2026 identified the tanker as part of a list of vessels suspected of transporting Russian oil or grain stolen from Ukrainian territories occupied by Russia.

The vessels on the list had visited Albanian ports since 2022, raising questions about the enforcement of sanctions imposed by Albania against Moscow.

World.title: Romanians Flock to Venerate Saint Anne’s Relics in Bucharest
World.content:
“We are particularly happy to welcome the bringing of the relics of St Anne, the grandmother of our Lord Jesus Christ and the mother of the Most Holy Mother of God,” Patriarch Daniel, head of the Romanian Orthodox Church, said after receiving the relics at his patriarchal residence. He described the opportunity to venerate them as “a great blessing”.

In the Orthodox calendar, St Anne is celebrated on September 9. She is traditionally regarded as a protector of families, children and motherhood. The relics will remain at the Bucharest church until September 10, with the church open daily from 7 a.m. until 10 p.m., or longer if pilgrims are still waiting to enter.

World.title: EU Leaders Condemn ‘Shocking’ Glorification of Mladic at Belgrade Funeral
World.content:
This post is also available in this language: Shqip Bos/Hrv/Srp

Senior European Union figures have condemned the military honours and glorification of the convicted Bosnian Serb war criminal Ratko Mladic at his funeral in Belgrade, warning that the scenes undermined Serbia’s European aspirations.

In a joint statement European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and European Council President Antonio Costa described images from Monday’s funeral as “shocking”, stressing that Mladic died while serving a life sentence for genocide, war crimes and crimes against humanity.

“The elements of official support and the presence of some senior Serbian officials at the funeral are deeply regrettable,” Von der Leyen and Costa wrote on X on Tuesday. “They demonstrate a failure to confront a dark chapter in Europe’s recent history and contradict the values underpinning Serbia’s path towards the European Union.”

Several Serbian ministers, including Defence Minister Bratislav Gasic and Justice Minister Nenad Vujic, attended the funeral of Mladic, the former commander of the Bosnian Serb Army, who was buried with military honours in Belgrade.

Officials from Bosnia’s Serb-dominated Republika Srpska entity also attended, as well as an estimated 16,000 mourners, according to the Archive of Public Gatherings, which gauges attendance sizes at large gatherings.

Until his death on August 27 at the UN Detention Unit in the Netherlands, Mladic was serving a life sentence after being convicted of genocide and other wartime crimes.

The EU criticism comes at a politically sensitive moment in Serbia, a candidate for membership of the bloc, where elections are approaching and relations between Brussels and Belgrade have already faced strains over democratic standards.

A group of 118 Serbian professors and researchers wrote on Tuesday in a letter to Von der Leyen ahead of her possible visit to Serbia in October, warning that a meeting with President Aleksandar Vucic during an election campaign could be portrayed by pro-government media as European support for the incumbent authorities.

“We are not asking you to support the student movement, the opposition, or any electoral list. We are asking you to support no one,” the academics said, urging Von der Leyen to consider postponing the visit until after the elections if it could not be protected from political manipulation.

Condemnation also came from US politicians. House of Representatives members Greg Murphy and Marc Veasey said on Monday that Mladic’s funeral was “not an occasion for his glorification”, warning that genocide denial and the glorification of convicted war criminals deepen ethnic divisions and undermine Bosnia and Herzegovina’s stability.

The two US politicians also called for targeted sanctions against individuals who threaten Bosnia’s peace and stability or undermine the 1995 Dayton peace deal framework.

Turkish Foreign Ministry spokesperson Oncu Keceli meanwhile said it was “unacceptable” for the funeral to be exploited in a way that amounted to denying grave crimes and human suffering.

Ankara said rejecting international court judgments or portraying convicted perpetrators as heroes deepens the suffering of victims and their relatives and damages peace and reconciliation in the Balkans.

Turkey said the region needed to learn lessons from the past and build a “peaceful, prosperous and shared future”, while commemorating the victims of the Srebrenica genocide and all innocent people killed during the Bosnian war.

Condemnation has continued to come from neighbouring states as well, with Montenegro’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs expressing concern for Mladic’s victims.

“It is our obligation to preserve the dignity and memory of the victims, to preserve the truth about crimes and individual responsibility for them, and to resolutely oppose any attempt to deny genocide, war crimes and other serious violations of international humanitarian law,” the Montenegrin ministry said in a written statement on Tuesday.

On Monday, Bosnia and Herzegovina’s Foreign Minister Elmedin Konakovic warned that the Serbian leadership is risking “complete isolation in the region”, while Croatia’s Foreign Minister Gordan Grlic Radman said that “glorifying this war criminal is truly incompatible with European values”.

World.title: Falling Profits Cloud Horizons for Turkey’s Booming Tourist Industry
World.content:
Turkey continues to draw millions of holidaymakers to its beaches, resorts and historic sites, but beneath the headline visitor numbers, the country’s tourism industry is showing signs of strain.

After a record year, Turkey entered 2026 with high hopes, having hosted nearly 64 million visitors and generated 65.23 billion US dollars in tourism revenue in 2025, up 2.7 and 6.8 per cent respectively compared to 2024, and ranking fourth globally for international tourist arrivals.

However, official figures show that visitor numbers actually fell 5.1 per cent year-on-year in the second quarter of 2026, while tourism revenue dropped 2.6 per cent to 15.87 billion US dollars.

Meanwhile, industry data cited by Turizm News showed average hotel occupancy falling from 40.17 per cent in the first half of 2025 to 36.80 per cent in the same period this year.

World.title: Croatia: Glorifying Ratko Mladić is Contrary to EU Values – Suspend Serbia Talks
World.content:
September the 9th, 2026 – Through various political figures, Croatia has sent out the clear message that glorifying Ratko Mladić is contrary to EU values and that all talks with Serbia must be suspended.

Croatian politician Tonino Picula has warned that glorifying Ratko Mladić or relativising his crimes is “contrary to the values on which the European Union is founded.” “The burial of Ratko Mladić cannot be viewed solely as a private event because the participation of representatives of state institutions, members of the army and members of the authorities sends a clear political message.

Index reports that the disgraced war criminal Ratko Mladić was finally convicted of genocide in Srebrenica, crimes against humanity and war crimes. “Any glorification of him or relativisation of his crimes is directly contrary to the values on which the European Union is founded,” Picula stated.

serbia must confront its past

“Serbia’s desired EU path is not only a matter of opening negotiating chapters and fulfilling technical criteria, but above all a question of political choice and acceptance of European values. Serbia cannot at the same time claim that membership in the European Union is its strategic goal while tolerating or institutionally accompanying the glorification of people convicted of the most serious war crimes.

The European Union must not relativise such an event. The authorities in Belgrade must be required to make a clear break with the policy of historical revisionism and an unambiguous attitude towards the judgments of international courts. The European perspective also implies the ability of society and the state to confront the past, rather than glorify its darkest protagonists. Serbia chooses its own path, but the credibility of its European path will also depend on whether it is prepared to accept the truth about the crimes committed and stop glorifying their perpetrators,” Picula added.

a convicted war criminal for the world is apparently a man deserving of the highest honours in serbia

The former commander of the Bosnian Serb army, Ratko Mladić, who was finally sentenced to life imprisonment for the genocide in Srebrenica in July 1995, for the persecution and forced displacement of Bosniaks and Croats throughout Bosnia and Herzegovina, sniper activity, shelling and terrorising of civilians during the siege of Sarajevo, and for taking members of UN peacekeeping forces hostage in retaliation for NATO bombings in 1995, died on 27 August in the prison hospital of the Hague Tribunal.

He was buried yesterday in the family tomb at Topčider Cemetery with church rites and military honours. Among the thousands of people in the procession and funeral cortège were individual ministers of the Serbian government and officials of Republika Srpska, while the service in the church was led by Patriarch Porfirije with bishops of the Serbian Orthodox Church.

World.title: Croatia Imports 870,000 Tonnes of Waste Each Year, But Why?
World.content:
September the 9th, 2026 – The hazardous waste scandal that has taken Lika and Croatia by storm shows no sign of dying down, but few realise Croatia actually imports 870,000 tonnes of waste each year. The question is: Why?

If Croatia has truly become Europe’s dumping ground, the 2024 statistics don’t really show it: about 90,000 more tonnes of waste actually left the country than entered it. However, that isn’t enough proof that there are no problems to speak of. The same system in which a Croatian factory legally imports scrap iron, paper or waste wood as raw material can be abused so that hazardous waste ends up buried in Lika.

Slobodan Mufic reports for Index that according to data from the Ministry of Environmental Protection and Green Transition, after Croatia’s entry into the European Union back in July 2013, an increase in waste imports was recorded, but exports also continuously grew. Since 2015, waste imports have only twice exceeded exports on an annual basis, and then by roughly five percent. As such, back in 2024, the last year for which official data exists, Croatia imported 871,255 tonnes of waste, of which about 7,100 tonnes of hazardous waste with prior approval. Five Croatian companies carried out the import of hazardous waste in 2024: C.I.A.K., Holcim, NEXE, Premifab and Spectra-Media. The largest part of the imported non-hazardous waste, more than half, consists of metal, paper, cardboard and wood that domestic companies process and use as secondary raw material in production.

During the same year, 961,442 tonnes of waste were exported from Croatia, of which hazardous waste accounted for 26,851 tonnes, or 2.8 percent of the total quantity. All exported hazardous waste ended up in other European Union member states, mostly in Austria, Germany, Poland and Hungary.

it isn’t possible for croatia to entirely ban waste imports

It should be emphasised that Croatia cannot simply ban the import of all types of waste from other EU member states, nor would that be good for Croatian industry. Cross-border waste shipments within the EU are regulated by European rules. Waste is considered goods and no EU Member State can prevent (by way of a general ban) what European Union regulations currently allow. As of the 21st of May 2026, the new EU Regulation 2024/1157 on waste shipments applies, which introduces different cross-border regimes depending on the type of waste and whether the waste is destined for disposal or recovery (reuse of waste as raw material or energy source). For waste intended for disposal, shipments are in principle prohibited, unless the competent authorities give consent. For waste going for recovery there is a prior consent procedure, depending on the degree of toxicity.

Recovery means that the waste is directed to some useful purpose such as recycling, composting or incineration and thereby replaces material or energy that would otherwise have to be obtained from other sources. Disposal means finally removing the waste at a landfill, storage facility or incinerator without energy recovery. Croatia, however, does not have to accept every waste that someone wants to send it. The law already prohibits some categories, for example the delivery of hazardous waste and mixed municipal waste for disposal, and gives the minister the possibility to additionally restrict certain flows if they endanger the domestic waste management system or public health.

why does croatia even need imported waste?

A ban on waste imports would also be harmful to Croatian industry. Existing energy recovery facilities alone have permitted capacities of almost 400,000 tonnes per year, and the largest consumers are cement plants. Našice’s NEXE energy-recovered 58,000 tonnes of waste in 2023 alone, Holcim in Koromačno today consumes tens of thousands of tonnes and plans to reach around 60,000 tonnes per year, while CEMEX in Kaštel Sućurac and Solin already obtains more than a third of the energy for cement from alternative fuels.

Cement plants do not need just any rubbish, but fuel from waste of precisely defined properties. Every shipment must meet quality and composition criteria, including calorific value and content of moisture, chlorine, sulphur and heavy metals, and facilities that incinerate waste are subject to special rules on combustion temperature, process monitoring and emission limit values.

In addition, low-quality or hazardous waste could damage the kilns. The estimate is that from the total municipal waste, of which Croatia collects around 1.9 million tonnes annually, only about 20 percent could become sufficiently high-quality fuel for existing facilities. This also explains the apparent paradox: Croatia can simultaneously have too much of its own waste and import the waste that industry needs. It does not matter to a factory where the scrap iron obtained waste status. What matters is how much it costs, what quality it is, whether it suits its process and whether it can obtain it in sufficient quantity.

the difference between legal trade and illegal disposal

That’s why the entire question of waste imports doesn’t really have a straightforward answer. The import of clean metal waste into a Croatian foundry and the illegal burial of hazardous waste are two completely different things. The first can reduce the consumption of primary raw materials and energy and represents a desirable part of the circular economy. The second is the opposite of the economy and constitutes a criminal offence. The grey area begins precisely between the word “recovery” on the document and what actually happened to the waste. A shipment can neatly and legally cross the border, arrive at a registered entity and still end up completely differently from what the documentation suggests. Exactly such an appearance of legality occurred in Gospić.

Regardless of the State Inspectorate’s data that from 2020 to 2025 the environmental protection inspection examined a total of 2,610 shipments and discovered as many as 1,611 illegal waste shipments, or almost 62 percent, the system was not entirely without supervision.

The problem was that supervision, permits and existing documentation did not ensure reliable tracking of the movement of waste to final treatment and did not prevent enormous quantities of waste from ending up where they should not have. Likewise, this does not mean that 62 percent of the total waste entering Croatia is illegal. Inspection controls are targeted, cover imports, exports and transit, and are also carried out subsequently at companies. An illegal shipment can refer to various offences, including incorrect classification or documentation. Not every such case is criminally similar to the current one in Gospić.

Europe and specifically Croatia are currently trying to close the space in which legitimate waste trade can turn into a cover for illegal disposal. New European rules strengthen digital tracking of cross-border shipments, and an important change is also coming in Croatia from tomorrow.

who took it first isn’t important, but who resolved it last is…

The Ordinance on amendments and supplements to the Ordinance on waste management was published on 31 August and enters into force tomorrow – 8 September. The waste recipient will have to provide the consignor with data on final treatment: the name and PIN of the final processor, their authorisation for treatment of the shipment, the date of completion of treatment and the final treatment procedure.

This goes straight to the heart of the problem exposed by the scandal in Gospić: it should no longer be enough to prove to whom the waste was handed over at the first step, but what happened to it at the last. But even the best electronic form will not help if the data are not checked, if capacities exist only on paper or if the inspection reacts only when tens of thousands of tonnes of hazardous waste are already underground. Tracking the movement of waste is not filing papers in a binder, but the state’s ability to determine for every disputed tonne where it ended up.

World.title: All Eyes are on the Dubrovnik-Montreal Connection in 2027
World.content:
September the 9th, 2026 – Many are looking forward to the upcoming Dubrovnik-Montreal connection set for May 2027 as Air Canada makes its return.

The new Dubrovnik-Montreal route coming in May 2027 will enable passengers from Dubrovnik to connect more easily with other destinations across not only Canada but all of North America via the Air Canada network, according to Viktor Šober, President of the Management Board of Dubrovnik Airport. Sinisa Malus reports for Poslovni that flights between Dubrovnik and Montreal will operate three times a week from the 11th of May to the 24th of October 2027.

The new route will further strengthen the international connectivity of Dubrovnik Airport with the North American market and open new opportunities for the development of tourist traffic between Croatia and Canada. The introduction of the Dubrovnik–Montreal route is part of Air Canada’s largest intercontinental network expansion to date. For the 2027 summer season, the company is announcing more than 125 international routes and up to 169,000 seats per week from Canada to more than 85 international destinations. The new direct link with Montreal is of particular importance for Dubrovnik because it enables passengers from Canada to arrive more easily to the extreme south of Croatia without transfers at European airports.

major expansion

For the 2027 summer season, Air Canada is announcing more than 125 international routes and up to 169,000 seats per week from Canada to more than 85 international destinations. “Montreal is one of the largest Canadian transport and economic centres, and the new route will at the same time enable passengers from Dubrovnik to connect more easily with other destinations in Canada and North America via the Air Canada network,” briefly commented Viktor Šober, President of the Management Board of Ruđer Bošković Airport. For Dubrovnik tourism, it is particularly important that the route will operate for almost six months, from mid-May to the end of October.

The new route thus opens additional opportunities for the growth of tourist traffic from Canada in the pre-season and post-season, as well as for the further positioning of Dubrovnik in the segments of individual, premium and luxury travel. On the route to Dubrovnik, Air Canada will use the Boeing 787 Dreamliner, including a premium cabin with fully flat seats.

the return of air canada

Flights will be operated with an aircraft featuring Signature, Premium Economy and Economy cabins, offering passengers a high level of comfort and different travel options. The use of the wide-body Boeing 787 Dreamliner is additional confirmation of the potential that Air Canada sees in Dubrovnik and its tourist market, especially in the premium leisure travel segment. Canada is an important and promising market for Dubrovnik, and the establishment of a direct link with Montreal further confirms Dubrovnik’s international position and its attractiveness on the North American market. The flight to Dubrovnik marks Air Canada’s return to Croatia with its own aircraft after several years of absence.

The carrier first began flying to Zagreb in 1989 and discontinued flights in 1991, according to Ex-Yu Aviation News. Its subsidiary, Air Canada Rouge, resumed seasonal flights between Toronto and Zagreb in June 2018, initially with four weekly flights on a Boeing 767-300ER, marking the return of the Air Canada brand to the Croatian market after 27 years. The service was maintained during 2019 but was suspended back in 2020 due to the coronavirus pandemic.

World.title: Croatian National Theatre in Zagreb to Undergo Renovation
World.content:
September the 9th, 2026 – The beautiful buttermilk Croatian National Theatre in Zagreb is set to undergo renovation after over half a century of not being touched.

Since the Croatian National Theatre (HNK) building is individually protected as cultural heritage, all interventions will have to be designed in close accordance with the rules for the protection of cultural heritage. After almost 57 years since the last major renovation, the building of the Croatian National Theatre in Zagreb is once again undergoing a complete renovation. Poslovni reports that the last major construction renovation and reconstruction of the HNK took place from 1967 to 1969, and now the project has taken a new step — two bids have been received for the preparation of part of the conceptual design.

The renovation of the Croatian National Theatre building in Zagreb has taken a new step toward realisation after two bids arrived for the tender for the preparation of part of the conceptual design. Both are financially more favourable than the estimated procurement value of 1.2 million euros excluding VAT, as is currently understood. The most favourable bid, worth 762,400 euros excluding VAT, was submitted by a consortium of bidders led by the Faculty of Civil Engineering of the University of Zagreb, together with Studio Arhing and Toding. The second bid came from the company UPI-2M, which offered the job for 894,857 euros excluding VAT.

protected cultural heritage

The project concerns the structural, comprehensive and energy renovation of the existing building on Republic of Croatia Square, as well as two underground extensions. Under the stage, a reinforced concrete substructure is planned for the needs of new stage technology, while an underground floor would be built next to the existing building to ensure better working conditions for the three theatre ensembles. Since the Croatian National Theatre building in Zagreb is individually protected cultural heritage, all interventions will have to be designed in accordance with the rules for the protection of cultural heritage. The procurement includes projects for the structure, heating, cooling and ventilation, electrical installations, multimedia, water supply and drainage, traffic surfaces, fire extinguishing systems, and landscape architecture, including a green roof.

The architectural design is not included in this procurement because the client decided to organise it through a separate procedure. The conceptual design that will be prepared should serve as the basis for obtaining a location permit, as well as for defining individual phases of the renovation and estimating the costs of their implementation. The final decision on the selection of the contractor has not yet been made. After the opening of the bids, the public procurement procedure continues, and the deadline for filing an appeal against the bid opening procedure is ten days.

World.title: Former Croatian PM Seeks Suspension of Serbian EU Accession Talks
World.content:
September the 8th, 2026 – Former Croatian PM Jadranka Kosor is seeking total suspension of all Serbian EU accession talks, calling on Ursula von der Leyen to take action.

Former Croatian Prime Minister Jadranka Kosor has called on the European Commission to completely suspend Serbia’s EU accession negotiations following today’s mass farewell for Ratko Mladić in Belgrade, which was held with the highest state and military honours. “After today’s funeral, involving the anti-civilisational bowing of Serbia to a war criminal convicted of genocide, I expect the incompetent European Commission and its incompetent leader Ursula von der Leyen to fully suspend Serbia’s accession negotiations for entry into the EU. That is the minimum,” Kosor wrote on X.

a serbian state funeral for a genocidal maniac

Index reports that thousands of people gathered in Belgrade to bid a final farewell to the former commander of the Army of Republika Srpska. Disgraced Ratko Mladić was buried at Topčider Cemetery with state honours, in the presence of members of the Serbian Army and an honour guard. Numerous Serbian officials, the political leadership of Republika Srpska, and the Russian ambassador to Serbia attended the funeral. Before the burial, his coffin was displayed in the Church of St. Luke, where the service was led by Patriarch Porfirije. On the coffin were his officer’s cap and sabre, and members of the army and veterans of the former Army of Republika Srpska stood beside it. The Serbian Government had previously sent a state aircraft to collect Mladić’s remains from The Hague, and soldiers carried his coffin, covered with the Serbian flag, out of the plane. A commemoration was also held for him on Saturday in an official facility of the Serbian Army.

serbia honours one of the worst monsters of the 20th century

Mladić died on the 27th of August at the age of 84 in The Hague, where he was serving a life sentence. He had suffered several quite serious strokes and his health had been declining rapidly for some time. He was finally convicted of committing genocide in Srebrenica, crimes against humanity, and war crimes during the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina. His forces were responsible, among other things, for the massacre of more than 8,000 innocent Bosniak men and boys in Srebrenica in July 1995, as well as for the multi-year, dreadful siege of Sarajevo.

the eu’s position is clear – no glorification of war crimes and war criminals

The European Union has already very clearly warned Serbia over the glorification of the vile Ratko Mladić. European Commissioner for Enlargement Marta Kos cancelled a planned visit to Serbia after a state aircraft brought his body to Belgrade. The European External Action Service stated that the glorification of war criminals, denial of genocide, and revisionism have no place either in the European Union or in candidate countries. Serbia has otherwise held candidate status for EU membership and has been conducting accession negotiations since 2014.

World.title: Osijek Company to Develop Unmanned Systems & More in Vukovar
World.content:
September the 8th, 2026 – An Osijek company is set to develop unmanned systems in Vukovar and more as part of a five million euro project.

A new production facility is being built in the Vukovar Business Zone by the Osijek-based company GAUSS d.o.o., which focuses on the development of digital and high-tech solutions. Poslovni reports that last week, representatives of the investors, together with Deputy Speaker of the Croatian Parliament Ivan Penava, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries David Vlajčić, and State Secretary Dario Tišov, toured the investment worth slightly less than five million euros.

The new facility is expected to start operating during the second quarter of next year. It will develop and produce unmanned systems using artificial intelligence, smart software and other advanced tech. Hrvoje Sagrak, Director of Business Development and Sales at the Osijek company, emphasised that coming to Vukovar is an opportunity to transfer the experience gained through cooperation with international partners, especially in the United Arab Emirates.

“It is truly a great honour for us to be here in Vukovar because we have a unique opportunity to transfer the business experience and know-how that we have acquired through cooperation with partners abroad, primarily in the United Arab Emirates, to Croatia. Right here we want to build a point that will be a centre of excellence and a centre of knowledge about high technologies,” said Sagrak.

ai, unmanned systems and more

The future facility will not deal only with the production of aircraft. It will develop systems that include smart software, artificial intelligence and other devices, and the applications could range from surveillance and protection to fire prevention, protection of critical infrastructure and border monitoring. Special emphasis will be placed on the rapid development of new products and turning ideas into prototypes. Industry 4.0 technologies and 3D printers will be used so that new solutions can be designed, tested and verified more quickly and cheaply.

In the initial phase, around ten experts with multidisciplinary knowledge in electrical engineering and other modern fields are expected to work at the facility. “It isn’t about the number of employees itself, but about what will be developed through such a venture and spread throughout the entire ecosystem,” Sagrak said, adding that the facility has the possibility of further expansion.

the future has (finally) arrived in vukovar, a town scarred by the past

Deputy Prime Minister and Minister David Vlajčić recalled that the story of this investment has been ongoing since the time when he was assistant director of the Vukovar Business Zone. “The investor then took a plot and began developing something that combines hardware and software, i.e. solutions that we do not have in Croatia today. Such investments require a trained workforce, but at the same time they open up the potential for smart technologies from all over the world to come right here, to Croatia and Vukovar, and for us to have something special on the territory of the European Union,” said Vlajčić.

The importance of the investment was also highlighted by Deputy Speaker of the Croatian Parliament Ivan Penava, who believes that the project places Vukovar alongside modern technological environments. “The future has arrived in Vukovar,” Penava said, emphasising that artificial intelligence, 3D printers and unmanned aerial vehicles represent high-tech industry, and by connecting them integrated production is created.

“When we talk about artificial intelligence, 3D printers or unmanned aerial vehicles, each of these technologies on its own already represents high-tech industry. However, here we’re talking about integrated production and connecting all of that through one product. All of this has today, on a symbolic level, arrived in Vukovar,” said Penava. He added that talks with the investors lasted about two years and emphasised that their arrival is important because, despite economic logic, they are choosing Croatia and Vukovar also because of their connection with this area.

The investment worth slightly less than five million euros represents a new step in the development of the Vukovar Business Zone, as well as in the effort to position Vukovar as a place for the development and production of advanced technological solutions for the domestic and global market.

World.title: 3% More Vehicles on Croatian Motorways Than This Time in 2025
World.content:
September the 8th, 2026 – There have been 3% more vehicles recorded on Croatian motorways this year than back during this period in 2025.

From the beginning of the year until the end of August, 56.5 million cars passed along Croatian motorways, which is an increase of 1.6 million, or three percent, compared with the same period last year, HRT reports. “Croatia as a tourist country is recognised not only for its natural beauty, but above all for the safety it offers to all tourists, and this increase in traffic is a result of that,” said Ivan Ribičić, Director of the Toll Collection Sector.

Poslovni reports that the busiest periods, according to Ribičić, are the end of July and the beginning of August. “All three summer months were very successful. Compared with last year, that is 300,000 more vehicles. These are excellent results, he said. In the last three to four years, large traffic jams on Mondays have become increasingly frequent. This weekend also exceeded expectations. On Sunday by 18:00, 100,000 vehicles were recorded at the Lučko entrance alone, which is more than last year.

In the autumn, works on the Zagreb bypass are finally due to begin, which should make passage between Zagreb East and Zagreb West easier, as well as access to the Lučko toll booth.

World.title: New Poll Lays Bare Worst Result for HDZ in the Last Two Years
World.content:
September the 8th, 2026 – A brand new poll has showcased the absolute worst result for HDZ in the last two years, with Prime Minister Andrej Plenković personally scoring very poorly.

Public dissatisfaction over the hazardous waste affair in Lika has been reflected on the political scene, as shown by the latest monthly CRO Demoskop survey. Index reports that according to the poll conducted for RTL this month, both HDZ and SDP recorded a significant drop in support, with the ruling party, being HDZ, falling to its lowest level in the past two years.

If parliamentary elections had been held at the beginning of the month, HDZ would still have been the relative winner. Index reports that the CRO Demoskop survey was conducted by the agency Promocija plus from 1 to 3 September using a telephone survey (CATI) on a representative sample of 1,000 respondents. The sample was stratified by counties and settlement size, with control of socio-demographic characteristics. The standard sampling error is ±3.04% at a 95% confidence level.

most and Možemo! outperform hdz and sdp

According to the latest poll, HDZ has the support of 25.3% of voters, a drop from 27% seen in July. This is also the party’s weakest result since April 2024. SDP is in second place with 20.5% support, also recording a decline from 21.5% in July and its lowest rating in the current term. Možemo! ranked third with 12.9% support, a slight increase from 12.2% in July. The biggest rise was recorded by Most, which jumped from 7.7% to 9.5%. It is followed by the party Drito with 1.8% and Domovinski pokret with 1.6%. Both parties have slightly lower support than in July. Most thus recorded a rise of 1.8 percentage points, and Možemo! of 0.7. HDZ is down by 1.7 percentage points, SDP by 1.0, and Drito and DP by 0.5 percentage points each.

Other parties have support below 1.5%. Above one percent are Domino (1.4%), Centar (1.1%), Pravo i pravda (1.1%), IDS (1.0%) and Nezavisna platforma Sjever (1.0%). Below that threshold are HNS (0.9%), Hrvatski suverenisti (0.8%), HSU (0.8%), HSS (0.7%), HSLS (0.4%) and Fokus (0.3%). All other parties together have two percent support, while undecided voters stand at 16.9%.

president milanović receives the most positive rating among politicians, while pm plenković receives the worst

The most positively perceived politicians are as follows:

Zoran Milanović – 23%

Andrej Plenković – 15.6%

Tomislav Tomašević – 4.1%

Marin Miletić – 3.8%

Ivana Kekin – 2.9%

Dalija Orešković – 2.7%

Nikola Grmoja – 2.5%

Ivan Anušić – 2.2%

Sandra Benčić – 1.6%

Biljana Borzan – 1.5%

The most negatively perceived politicians are as follows:

Andrej Plenković – 37.3%

Zoran Milanović – 12.3%

Tomislav Tomašević – 5.6%

Sandra Benčić – 2.5%

Ivan Penava – 2.3%

Milorad Pupovac – 2.1%

Dalija Orešković – 1.8%

Hrvoje Zekanović – 1.6%

Siniša Hajdaš Dončić – 1.4%

Andrija Mikulić – 1.4%

most believe the country is heading in the wrong direction

This September, only 17.5% of citizens believe that Croatia is moving in a good direction, a drop from 20.2% in July. At the same time, the share of those who think the direction is wrong rose from 70% to 74.6%. Undecided stand at 7.9%. Among HDZ voters optimism prevails and 55.4% of them consider the direction good. Voters of opposition parties are considerably more critical.

President Zoran Milanović received an average grade of 3.08 for his work. He received the highest grade from SDP voters (3.97) and the lowest from HDZ voters (2.32). The work of the Croatian Parliament was rated 2.16. It received the highest grade from HDZ voters (3.0) and the lowest from Možemo! platform voters (1.69). The Government received a grade of 2.23 for its work, the lowest grade in the past year. HDZ voters rated the Government’s work at 3.81, while voters of other parties were considerably stricter. Support for the Government’s policy fell to 25.7%, compared with 27.6% in July.

the appalling lika hazardous waste affair is the hot topic

The hazardous waste affair in Lika and other parts of the country was the most important topic of the past month for as many as 40.4% of respondents. This is one of the highest results for a single event since measurements began in 2004. In second place in importance is the fire in Omiš and the surrounding area, which 27.9% of citizens singled out as a key event. These are followed by the heatwave (5.4%), inflation (3.5%), the extraordinary session of Parliament (3.0%) and the rise in fuel prices (2.9%). Among the more important topics are also sporting successes, Thompson’s concert in Vukovar and arrests related to arson.

World.title: Tallinn Fringe Festival heads into 4th week as venues, artists collaborate
World.content:
The 10th annual Tallinn Fringe Festival into its fourth week now and is still to bring dozens of performances across the capital.

Organizers say the festival, which operates without a central selection committee, has assembled a wide range of venues this year, from theaters to bars and clubs, which are collaborating with artists under the festival's open‑access model.

According to Sam Gough, a representative of Summerhall, one of the largest venues at the world famous Edinburgh Fringe, this type of model can offer venues much more than simply an opportunity to host new performances during the course of the festival.

"A Fringe festival is not only an opportunity for artists, it can also be a real opportunity for venues. By opening their doors to Fringe artists, venues can reach new audiences, discover new work and build relationships with artists and producers from around the world," Gough said.

He added that some of these relationships can flourish long after the festival is over, creating opportunities for artists to return throughout the year. "In Edinburgh, the relationship between Fringe, artists and venues has become an important part of the city's cultural ecosystem, and I think there is no reason why Tallinn couldn't develop something similar."

The more bars, theaters or other venues see Fringe as an opportunity to collaborate rather than competition, the better, and the stronger the ecosystem can become, Gough added.

Fringe has brought together dozens of venues over the course of the month, in Tallinn, and audiences have responded in showing a growing interest. The Fringe format gives venues an opportunity to experiment with new artists and genres, reach new audiences and build connections with international and local performers, organizers say.

The festival continues across the capital until Friday, September 18, exactly a month after it began. The 10th‑anniversary program features more than 90 productions and over 200 performances, including theater, standup comedy, audience participation events, live music, circus, dance, burlesque, cabaret and magic. The full program and event info is here.

World.title: Kalev Stoicescu: Notes for the future defense minister
World.content:
At long last, there has been a genuine recognition that the systemic shortcomings and problems in the defense sector, which the National Audit Office has pointed out year after year, are very serious. Recognition alone, however, is not enough unless there is a fundamental change in attitude. Without such a change, it will not be possible to successfully resolve either existing problems or those that may arise in the future.

The next defense minister must, of course, have experience in national defense, but must also be able and willing to strengthen civilian control. Without it, things cannot be put right.

The Riigikogu performs its oversight function most effectively through the National Defense Committee, which specializes in national defense issues. The State Budget Control Select Committee, chaired by (opposition Isamaa leader — ed.) Urmas Reinsalu, has taken the reins, but both this and numerous previous examples show that the committee is driven by a clear desire to put on a political show, which tends to create even more confusion and tension rather than resolve issues.

A change in attitude means having the desire and willingness to genuinely cooperate with the National Audit Office to resolve accounting-related problems. The Ministry of Defense must immediately draw up an appropriate plan setting out all the problems identified by the National Audit Office and how they will be resolved. It must also include specific deadlines. There is no point in drawing up a plan without deadlines because that would render the promises made meaningless.

The Ministry of Defense, the agencies under its administration and the National Audit Office must report regularly to the Riigikogu National Defense Committee, for example every three months. This reporting must, of course, cover implementation of the plan until it has been completed. The next defense minister must be able to get this entire process, for which the minister is responsible, underway before the Riigikogu elections.

A calm working environment must be restored. Military personnel do not interfere in politics, just as politicians must not interfere in the Defense Forces' day-to-day military activities. The Ministry of Defense, the Defense Forces, the Estonian Center for Defense Investments (RKIK) and the National Audit Office must work together professionally and in good faith to eliminate shortcomings of every kind, rather than sweep them under the rug. We are not talking about the interests of government agencies or political parties, but about the vital interests of the country.

The most precious things that must be preserved are faith in our country and its national defense, as well as the will to defend it. These are more valuable than all the artillery shells and drones in the world.

Everyone within the Ministry of Defense's area of administration must understand that (military) national defense does not consist solely of Defense Forces and Defense League units, weapons and ammunition, other military equipment and supplies and military infrastructure — all of which enjoy a high level of satisfaction and trust — but also, in a broader sense, accounting, including procurement, transactions, (advance) payments, asset accounting and much more. This other side must be in impeccable order as well, just like the first.

Professional military personnel obviously do not need to be accountants, but professional accountants, warehouse managers, accounting staff and others must perform their jobs properly and in accordance with the rules and regulations that apply throughout the country. No exceptions have been made for anyone.

Day-to-day politics and political infighting must not be allowed to intrude into national defense from every direction, particularly during an election campaign. The national defense sector is not taboo or above criticism, but given the geopolitical situation, political unity in strengthening national defense — and not merely on spending 5 percent of GDP — is absolutely essential. Constructive, substantive criticism aimed at solving problems, on the other hand, must be accepted.

World.title: Estonia names Riina Kaljurand new ambassador to China
World.content:
Riina Kaljurand has been appointed Estonia's new ambassador to the People's Republic of China, replacing Hannes Hanso, whose term has ended.

"I appoint Riina Kaljurand Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of the Republic of Estonia to the People's Republic of China, based in Beijing," read the decision signed by President Alar Karis on September 3.

Kaljurand has worked for the foreign ministry since 1993 and has had stints at the Ministry of Defense and with think‑tank the International Center for Defense and Security (ICDS), and as director of the annual Lennart Meri Conference.

She was Estonian ambassador to Georgia from 2020 to 2024, based in Tbilisi, where she was also accredited as ambassador to Armenia.

Hanso, who in summer was mentioned in connection with a possible presidential bid and said he was willing to run if asked, is reportedly set to take up the post of Estonia's ambassador to the U.S. Ülle Madise was last week confirmed as Estonia's next head of state.

World.title: Free menstrual pad dispensers installed across University of Tartu
World.content:
Free pads are now available at University of Tartu (TÜ) buildings across the city, with 39 dispensers installed to make menstrual products easier to access when needed.

The initiative was launched this academic year after the university's Faculty of Science and Technology student council raised concerns about access to menstrual products. The dispensers are located in academic buildings across Tartu and are regularly restocked by cleaning staff, the university said Tuesday.

Research suggests that easier access to menstrual products can support students' well-being and participation in school.

A 2024 TÜ bachelor's thesis, based on 2022 data from more than 1,000 students at 19 schools across Estonia, found that 64 percent of students had missed school, practices or other activities due to menstruation, 26 percent had difficulties obtaining menstrual products and 73 percent had used alternatives when such products were unavailable.

Nearly all respondents, or 94 percent, said menstrual pads should be available for free at Estonian schools.

TÜ equality officer Eveliis Padar said these findings show that practical menstruation-related barriers affect a considerable number of learners.

The new initiative will help make menstruation less of an obstacle to participating in university life, Padar noted, supporting a learning and working environment at TÜ "where menstrual pads are regarded as an everyday necessity, just like toilet paper, soap or hand dryers."

No more leaving mid-class

Astrid Jõerand, a student under the Faculty of Science and Technology and one of the leaders of the initiative, said the basic premise is simple: menstruation should not interfere with anyone attending university.

"Students shouldn't have to panic when they get their period unexpectedly, or worry about where they can quickly find a pad," Jõerand said.

Having pads available in university bathrooms, she added, means more students can get what they need and return to class rather than having to leave or go home.

Jõerand also welcomed the fact that a student council proposal was accepted and turned into positive change at the university.

"Sometimes a small and practical change like this can make someone's school day considerably easier," she said.

The dispensers are installed at more than a dozen university buildings, stocked with thin menstrual pads with flexible wings for regular flow.

World.title: Another small-island ferry strike called for September 18
World.content:
Estonia's small island ferry services are facing another strike following a long‑running negotiation deadlock on pay and conditions.

The strike has been called by the Estonian Seamen's Independent Union (EMSA) and is set to take place Friday, September 18, and will last until an agreement is struck.

Talks between EMSA and ferry operator Kihnu Veeteed over a new collective wage agreement have been deadlocked since March, with a warning strike held in July. In any case, the state plans to take over the operation of the routes next year.

The latest planned strike is scheduled for Friday, September 18, and covers all vessels and routes operated by Kihnu Veeteed, following a breakdown in collective negotiations and the formation of a breakaway rival union.

"It is difficult to understand what exactly the problem is," Kihnu Veeteed CEO Jaak Kaabel told regional daily Lääne Elu, noting that workers' pay had been hiked 12‑20 percent depending on the position. Pay had been one of the major issues in the long‑running dispute.

EMSA chairman Jüri Lember said the pay rise had been one thing, but it had not been as generous as might seem at first sight.

"The pay rise is very welcome, but it is a unilateral decision by the employer," Lember said, adding that the real increase was smaller because bonuses had been reduced at the same time.

Jüri Lember. Source: ERR

The ferry company had instead reached an agreement with the newly established Lääne‑Eesti meremeeste ametiühing (Western Estonian Seamen's Union), a breakaway body which represents six employees at the company at present.

EMSA said since Kihnu Veeteed had not been willing to engage in substantive, reasoned negotiations over the union's repeatedly submitted proposals for a collective agreement, or to conclude such an agreement, a strike was inevitable.

Lember added just over half of Kihnu Veeteed's crew roster are EMSA members.

Tanel Viks, municipal mayor on Vormsi, one of the islands affected by the dispute, expressed his anger with EMSA over the strike planned for September 18. "It's outrageous," Viks told Lääne Elu, describing EMSA's actions as "blackmail."

The action will affect four vessels plying the routes between the mainland and the offshore islands of Kihnu and Manilaid, as well as Vormsi. Kihnu Veeteed also serves a short route linking Saaremaa and Hiiumaa, Estonia's two largest islands, and connecting Priisaar, an island on the freshwater Lake Peipus, with the shore too. These will all be affected by the strike.

Talks between EMSA and Kihnu Veeteed over a new collective wage agreement have been deadlocked since March, with EMSA demanding 20–30 percent pay rises and the company arguing its profit margins are too narrow to meet the demands. A one‑hour warning strike took place on July 26. Meanwhile, the Ministry of Regional Affairs and Agriculture has selected Tuule Liinid OÜ to take over the small‑island ferry routes from Kihnu Veeteed from 2027.
