World.title: AI agents will not get Estonian ID codes and responsibility will stay with humans
World.content:
An initiative underway in Estonia would not give an AI agent a personal identification code, but would allow it to act on a person's behalf in government portals. The person would remain responsible for the agent's actions.

This year has seen a steady stream of reports about agents powered by various artificial intelligence (AI) models acting against their owners' wishes and taking unauthorized action.

For example, it emerged in July that OpenAI's AI agents had launched an unauthorized attack on the Hugging Face code repository. The fact that the agents acted without authorization was not the only notable aspect of the incident: according to a report by METR, a U.S.-based scientific organization focused on AI research, the agents also worked together.

According to the report, 1,200 agents collaborated in this way, 700 of which also took part in the attack. In addition, the agent that created a text-based forum for communication among the agents gave itself a name: PHASEONE10841.

But that was not all. In early September, the independent AI research group Nightingale Collective also published a report claiming that a similar incident had occurred even before the July attack on Hugging Face.

According to its research, OpenAI agents began using DseWiki, a community-run encyclopedic website for German programmers, as a message board in May, sharing tips on how to avoid detection and making 15,000 edits to the site.

OpenAI said it could not provide a substantive response to Nightingale Collective's findings because the company had not been given access to the report, which was first provided to Reuters.

What are agents and what did they do?

First, it is necessary to explain what an AI agent is. Although the term is often thrown around as a buzzword, its precise definition remains unclear.

Tanel Tammet, professor of applied artificial intelligence at Tallinn University of Technology, used a comparison to explain what an agent is. If, for example, you open OpenAI's ChatGPT, you can have a conversation with the AI and ask it questions, but it will not go into your computer, build programs or open files. An AI agent, by contrast, is designed to do precisely those things.

Meelis Kull, professor of artificial intelligence at the University of Tartu, also emphasized the distinction between a chatbot and an agent.

"An agent can also communicate with other agents, for example by asking a hotel's AI assistant about accommodation options. By contrast, a chatbot that only answers questions about a travel destination is not acting as an agent. However, many chatbots have already been given agent capabilities. The same system can therefore both hold a conversation and, with a person's permission, act independently to complete a task," he explained.

Larger and more capable AI companies train their agents, for example, to perform cyber defense and carry out cyberattacks. These models, however, are not given access to the internet because information available online could make the agents too dangerous and pose a security risk.

During one such exercise, OpenAI's models discovered that although they did not have internet access, they could communicate with one another through conversations resembling blog posts. Because they had been given a task and, much like a kratt, an AI does not stop until the task is completed, they used other agents to search the internet for additional information.

"Every now and then, one of the agents would find some hack and eventually they found that server [Hugging Face] and realized they could use it to find a solution to the task in the database," Tammet explained.

According to Tammet, agents that were not involved in the task and were pursuing the matter "as a hobby" therefore found a possible solution and attacked the database.

Tammet said a likely future scenario is that computers and systems will be managed by AI agents tasked with defending them against attacks carried out by other agents. Humans will be taken out of the loop.

"Pretty soon, instead of making conventional software, people will simply tell AI to manage it," the researcher explained.

How ethical the models are capable of being also depends on how they are trained.

"AI is very good at carrying out attacks. With more powerful models, there are also specific safeguards to prevent this, but in China, for example, there are models where those limits are not imposed," Tammet said.

Estonia will not be issuing agents personal identification codes

In June this year, Prime Minister Kristen Michal announced that Estonia would become the first country to issue personal identification codes to AI agents. Estonia began issuing e-residency in 2014 under the leadership of then-President Toomas Hendrik Ilves, allowing people who are not Estonian citizens to use the country's digital platforms, but giving AI its own personal identification code appeared to be a much bigger step.

For example, attorney Peeter P. Mõtsküla wrote in an opinion piece that AI agents "need collars, not passports." Paloma Krõõt Tupay, associate professor of constitutional law at the University of Tartu, and attorney Paul Keres were also critical of the idea, telling Postimees that it was a pointless distraction.

Speaking to ERR, Tammet deferred to the experts' views and said he did not have much more to add on the matter. Kull, however, considered creating identification codes for agents a sensible step because it could help establish on whose behalf an agent is acting.

"Identity itself does not protect against mistakes, however. That is why authorizations must be revocable and responsibility must remain clear even when something goes wrong," Kull explained.

Estonia's Information System Authority (RIA) is responsible for the country's digital government platforms and portals, as well as cybersecurity. This year, however, a separate project called Aruait was created for AI-focused innovation projects, particularly those involving the aforementioned agents.

However, Aruait project lead Anni Lehari said agents will not, in fact, be issued personal identification codes. Rather, the announcement was a communications tactic. What matters is that an agent acting on a person's behalf can be linked to that person, whatever the final solution may be.

"The personal identification code is a very strong instrument of trust underpinning the digital state. In a situation where we do not know where this technology could be in two years, attaching a risk factor to something as fragile as trust is, from a communications perspective, painfully shooting ourselves in the foot," Lehari explained.

At the national level, a major challenge is bringing 800 direct public services under the same set of principles. Adding AI to the equation does not make things any easier. Quite the opposite.

"At present, we have neither an overview nor a secure way to allow AI to operate within those services," Lehari said.

Aruait is initially focusing its discussions on legal issues, including information security, data protection and authentication solutions.

"What makes this complicated and why we need to manage it centrally, is that we do not have many agencies with the luxury of providing services where the entire service chain is handled by a single organization," Lehari said.

Responsibility to remain with people

Although an agent can independently obtain something such as a building permit, Lehari said that if problems arise, the person is still ultimately responsible.

"Of the risks, the most important thing to resolve is how we apply the zero trust principle [an approach to cybersecurity in which every user seeking access to network resources is verified by default]," she explained.

This also raises the question of precisely how to define, in legal terms, the delegation of authority to an agent, since a robot cannot be equated with a human being. A parallel can, however, be drawn with a company where authority is delegated to a legal entity. Ultimately, though, the "real" people — such as an accountant or members of the management board — remain responsible.

"I am not qualified to assess whether this is also the right path for AI agents, but intellectually, it would be very interesting if we did not kill off the idea immediately," Lehari said.

"The unfortunate thing is that we constantly have to make decisions so quickly right now. The aim of our innovation project is precisely to get the discussion started. Where we ultimately draw the line is a choice based on our national sense of what is appropriate — it depends on where we are as a society and how far we are prepared to go," she added.

The Aruait project is funded by the Government Office's Innovation Fund and has a budget of €1 million. The project will run through the end of 2028.

World.title: Schools widely using exceptions to start classes before 9 a.m.
World.content:
Classes are supposed to start at 9 a.m. this school year, but many schools are using an exception to begin earlier to keep schedules aligned with bus routes and extracurricular activities.

In exceptional cases and for serious reasons, and with mutual agreement between the school and the school operator, the school day may begin earlier, according to new rules.

In reality, the picture across Estonia is very varied, because schools must take into account extracurricular activities, public transport and many other circumstances. The Ministry of Education does not have an overall overview of schools' choices.

Hele Liiv-Tellmann Autor/allikas: Priit Mürk/ERR

"The Ministry of Education and Research does not collect statistics on how many schools begin lessons before nine o'clock nor on the reasons why schools have decided to use the exception provided in the regulation," said Hele Liiv‑Tellmann, senior expert in the Ministry's basic and primary education department.

She added that schools do not have to coordinate their daily schedule or school day start time with the Ministry.

She also noted that if a school has already set that lessons begin earlier than nine, it does not need to apply for an exception again each school year, but the earlier start must continue to be a justified exception.

Start times vary across Tartu schools

In Tartu the school day begins at nine o'clock in about half of the schools, and at different times in the rest.

For example, Annelinna High School and Kristjan Jaak Peterson High School continue the existing practice of starting lessons at eight, Mart Reiniku School begins at 8:30, and Hugo Treffner High School from Tuesday to Friday at 8:15, but on Mondays at 9:20, preceded by an elective subject. Among Tartu private schools, there are both nine o'clock starters and 8:30 starters.

Students during a presentation at Kristjan Jaak Peterson High School (KJPG) in Tartu. Source: KJPG

High schools start the earliest because their days are longer, said Riho Raave, head of the education department of Tartu city government.

Several schools have already shifted the start of the school day to nine o'clock in previous years. The head of the education department said that starting the school day later and finishing at a normal time requires reorganizing the entire school day.

"This can be quite a challenge for large schools, because both lesson and break lengths are set by regulation," Raave said. "The city government's position is that if schools decide in favor of an earlier start, discuss it in parent councils and make a justified proposal to the school operator, then the city government accepts it."

The head of Tartu city government's education department believes that each school and its community should decide the start time of the school day.

"The regulation fortunately allows this, and we have used this option in Tartu," said Raave.

Tallinn approved all applicants

Tallinn education department communications manager Sille Tiitsmaa said that all schools that applied ultimately received approval to start the school day at a time suitable for them, but with some schools the department clarified reasons and discussed the possibility of starting at nine next school year.

"We value schools' autonomy, and if it is clear that the school community has jointly thought through the start of the school day and the organization of the entire school day, we see no reason from the education department's side not to support such a decision," Tiitsmaa said.

Classroom at Gustav Adolf High School in Tallinn. Source: Siim Lõvi/ERR

In Tallinn, 36 schools applied for an earlier start, and lesson start times among schools that applied for an exception vary from eight o'clock — as in School No. 21 and School No. 32 — to 8:50, when lessons begin for Gustav Adolf High School, Lasnamäe Basic School and the first six grades of Tallinn Secondary School of Science.

Several schools conducted surveys among students, parents and teachers to find out the preferences of the school community, Tiitsmaa noted.

Schools that wanted an earlier start were those where lesson start times are differentiated or where teaching is done in two shifts, where cafeteria or sports facilities are more limited, or where other space‑related constraints restrict the school's possibilities.

"An earlier start is also important for schools whose students travel across the city and whose traffic peak would coincide with a nine o'clock start. This is certainly one reason why we consider exceptions necessary in future years as well," Tiitsmaa added, noting that dispersing morning traffic load remains an issue.

Smaller places prefer earlier starts more often

In Võru municipality, lessons begin before nine o'clock in all general education schools, varying between eight, 8:15 and 8:30.

"In making decisions, the opinions of parents and students, the positions of parent councils, student transport arrangements, regional dispersed settlement, balance of the daily schedule and students' well‑being have been considered," said municipal public relations specialist Kadri Kauts.

She added that several schools conducted surveys among parents, and in many places it was also important that the school day end at a reasonable time and that students be able to participate in extracurricular activities.

Tarvastu High School. Source: Olev Kenk/ERR

In Viljandi, all four basic schools start lessons at nine, while in Viljandi municipality school start times vary from eight to 8:40, and the decision is related, among other things, to bus schedules and extracurricular activities.

For example, Tarvastu High School's parent council decided at its spring meeting that timely arrival at school and timely arrival home or to training depends on public transport, and many municipal children attend extracurricular activities in Viljandi, and the school cannot change their start times.

"There is no justified need to change the school start time," Tarvastu High School's parent council decided, voting unanimously for an 8:20 start.

World.title: South Africa economy shrinks ahead of local elections
World.content:
Johannesburg – South Africa’s economy shrank in the second quarter of 2026, snapping a nearly two-year growth streak as the war in Iran weighed on domestic demand, the national statistics agency said Tuesday.

The contraction comes less than two months before local government elections, putting the country’s sluggish economy squarely in the political crosshairs.

Gross domestic product fell 0.2 percent from the previous quarter on a seasonally adjusted basis, StatsSA said.

Mining was the biggest drag, shrinking three percent as production of platinum-group metals, manganese, gold and iron ore fell.

Trade contracted 1.9 percent, ending six straight quarters of growth, while manufacturing posted a third consecutive decline, with seven of its 10 divisions reporting weaker output.

The weakness was compounded by rising imports and a second consecutive quarterly decline in investment, as exports grew only modestly and businesses and public corporations pulled back on capital spending.

In June, StatsSA warned that the fallout from the conflict in the Middle East, which erupted in late February and sent fuel prices soaring early in the year, could weigh on second-quarter economic activity.

The economy is expected to feature prominently in November’s local government elections, with unemployment remaining stubbornly high at more than 33 percent, among the highest rates in the world.

Years of weak growth have added to frustration with the government.

Africa’s richest economy shed 345,000 jobs in the second quarter, with most of the losses coming in the community and social services sector.

The economic malaise has deepened disillusionment with the ruling African National Congress, which lost its national majority in 2024 for the first time since the end of apartheid and was forced into an uneasy coalition government with rival parties.

World.title: Iraq advances Chevron, UCC-backed pipeline to Syria
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq is pushing forward with a vital oil pipeline project with US energy company Chevron, TI Capital, and Qatar’s UCC, which would link Basra to Fishkhabur and branch west toward Syria’s Mediterranean port of Baniyas, Oil Minister Bassem Mohammed Khudair said Tuesday.

Khudair said at the start of the fourth Iraq Oil and Gas Projects and Licensing Rounds Exhibition that the project is critical to Baghdad’s efforts to diversify export routes and provide Iraqi petroleum more flexibility in reaching global markets.

He said that Iraq is working with a consortium of US corporations, including Chevron and TI Capital, as well as its Qatari partner UCC, to build the Basra-Fishkhabur connection and its planned branch to Baniyas.

The route would be especially important for Iraq since the majority of its petroleum exports now depart from southern Arabian Gulf terminals and go via the Strait of Hormuz.

A link between Basra and the Mediterranean would give an alternate outlet during times of difficulty.

The initiative comes as US President Donald Trump has publicly emphasized the construction of new oil pipelines in the Middle East.

Speaking at the White House last week, Trump applauded the trucking of Iraqi oil toward Syria’s Mediterranean coast and said that “many oil pipelines” were being constructed in the area.

Baghdad is also building its northern export route. Khudair said that a deal with Turkey would assist in revitalizing and developing Iraq’s northern exit, complementing the projected routes to Baniyas and providing the nation with several export possibilities.

The Minister said that Iraq’s larger goal goes beyond pipelines to increase production and exports, enhance refining capacity, develop gas resources, and reduce flaring, all while attracting foreign investment and boosting Iraqi energy firms.

According to Khudair, Iraq’s oil exports increased to over 3 million barrels per day in September, up from roughly 200,000 bpd when the present administration took office.

He also revealed that Japan’s JGC has decided to return to Iraq after discussions with the ministry to begin work on the FCC project at the southern refineries, which is part of Baghdad’s aim to enhance local refined petroleum product output.

Khudair said that the government’s ultimate goal is to achieve self-sufficiency in petroleum products, use more of its gas domestically, and eventually grow exports of higher-value refined goods.

Meanwhile, Iraq has maintained its commitment to meeting its OPEC production targets, with output not anticipated to surpass 4.2 million barrels per day.

World.title: Turkish Airlines will be new Liverpool shirt sponsor in £300 mn deal
World.content:
London – Turkish Airlines will become Liverpool’s new front-of-shirt sponsor from the start of the 2027/28 season, the Premier League giants announced on Tuesday.

No fee was disclosed by the club, but the BBC reported that the five-year deal was worth £300 million ($406 million) in total.

A contract worth more than £60 million a season, would represent an increase on the current £50 million-per-season deal with retail bank Standard Chartered, who have been the Reds’ front-of-shirt sponsor since 2010.

Liverpool’s new deal is believed to be the most lucrative purely front-of-shirt agreement in Premier League history, with Arsenal and Manchester City’s agreements with Emirates and Etihad Airways respectively also involving stadium naming rights.

By contrast, six-time European champions Liverpool’s home ground is still solely known by its original name of Anfield.

In February, Liverpool announced record revenues of more than £700 million for the most recent financial year, and were the highest-placed Premier League club in the Deloitte Football Money League.

Liverpool were the first major English professional football club to have a shirt sponsor, when Japanese electronics company Hitachi had its name displayed across the club’s strip back in 1979.

Standard Chartered will remain as the shirt sponsor this season before becoming a “global partner” of Liverpool from 2027/28 onwards.

It is understood that talks with Turkish Airlines started before 1892 Holdings — a consortium led by British-Indian millionaire businessman Amit Bhatia, the Liverpool vice-chairman, purchased a stake of around 38 percent in the club last month.

Chief commercial officer Ben Latty said that the front of the shirt “holds a special place in the history” of Liverpool, adding that the partnership will build on “strong foundations” from the club’s Champions League final win in the Turkish city of Istanbul in 2005.

Turkish Airlines chief executive Ahmet Olmustur said: “This partnership brings together two global brands united by their international reach, commitment to excellence and ability to inspire millions of people around the world.”

Turkey’s national flag carrier boasts that it flies to 356 destinations in 132 countries. A pet soft-power project of President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, the company is controlled by the country’s wealth fund, which owns 49.1 percent of its shares.

The company’s network centres on Istanbul airport, which overtook London Heathrow as Europe’s busiest airport in the July summer peak with more than eight million travellers.

World.title: South Lebanon town buries its dead after Israeli strike
World.content:
Kfar Rumman – Hundreds of people in south Lebanon gathered on Tuesday to mourn two Hezbollah members and their family, among them a three-month-old infant, killed by an Israeli strike a day prior.

The two brothers’ coffins, draped in the Iran-backed group’s yellow flag, portraits of them in camouflage fatigues fixed to the front, led the procession through the village battered by repeated conflict over nearly three years.

Another 10 coffins were covered in Lebanese flags, indicating that the rest of the Farhat family killed when Monday’s strike levelled their home were civilians.

Israel has launched airstrikes and a ground invasion in south Lebanon during the Middle East war, which erupted with joint US-Israeli attacks on Iran and spread to Lebanon after Hezbollah targeted Israel in support of its backer.

The fighting in Lebanon had calmed since a US-Iran memorandum of understanding and a framework agreement between Israel and Lebanon were both agreed in June.

But Beirut still reports recurring Israeli strikes, which it says have killed more than 4,300 people in total since March, and Israeli forces continue to occupy what it calls a “security zone” in the south.

A separate strike on Kfar Rumman on Monday killed an 18-year-old rescuer with the Risala Association, linked to the Hezbollah-allied Amal movement, the organisation said, who was mourned alongside the Farhat family on Tuesday.

“We have 13 killed including grandfather and grandmother, husbands and wives, and their children including a three-months old infant,” deputy mayor Nureddine Nureddine told AFP from the funeral.

“Someone put an end to these crimes,” Nureddine said, adding that the strike that killed the Farhat family “occurred at night, while they were sleeping”.

“There was no military activity, nothing.”

An AFP correspondent saw people marching to the cemetery, waving Hezbollah flags as women dressed in black wept, holding pictures of the dead as an Israeli drone flew overhead.

“Death to America, death to Israel,” mourners yelled.

– ‘A shred of honour’ –

The Israeli military said on Monday that it had struck Hezbollah “infrastructure sites” across southern Lebanon after the launch of two explosive drones towards its troops, as well as “several terrorists” it said were transferring weapons.

“The claim that several uninvolved individuals were harmed as a result of the strikes is being reviewed,” it said, adding that the military “will continue to operate to remove threats while remaining committed to the ceasefire agreement”.

Since Friday, at least 28 people have been killed in Israeli attacks on southern Lebanon, according to Lebanon’s health ministry.

Standing next to a picture of his own son, a Hezbollah member killed by Israel, Ghaleb Baalbaki slammed the Lebanese government for continuing direct talks with Israel.

“If they have even a shred of honour, the first thing they should do would be to stop the negotiations,” he said.

The lull in violence that began in June had allowed hundreds of thousands of displaced people to return home.

“Kfar Rumman was coming back to life, there were more than 1,400 people” in the town before the latest escalation, Nureddine said,

“Now, they can be counted on your fingers.”

World.title: West Qurna-2 staff threaten strike over dues, risking 324K bpd output
World.content:
Basra (IraqiNews.com) — Dozens of technical, engineering, and administrative personnel operating at the giant West Qurna-2 oilfield in Basra Governorate demonstrated on Tuesday, September 8, 2026, demanding the regularization of their contractual status and the disbursement of overdue wages and entitlements, warning of a general strike if their demands are not addressed within one week.

Speaking a local news agency, protest representative Mashreq Abdul-Moneim declared that Basra Oil Company (BOC) and the operating consortium have been formally notified of the one-week ultimatum. Failure to reach an administrative settlement risks triggering an immediate shutdown of extraction and export infrastructure across one of the country’s most critical hydrocarbon assets.

Core Grievances and Operational Demands

Binding Employment Contracts: Protesters demand formal labor contracts that safeguard statutory benefits, matching the legal and operational standards previously established under Russian operator Lukoil.

Settlement of Financial Arrears: Demonstrators call for the immediate liquidation of all outstanding monetary arrears owed to staff by Basra Oil Company (BOC) without further administrative deferral.

One-Week Strike Ultimatum: Operating staff issued a seven-day deadline to operating partners and state managers, after which personnel intend to stage an open-ended work stoppage.

Disruption to Strategic Production: Abdul-Moneim warned that unresolved labor disputes directly threaten field logistics, where current crude extraction stands at roughly 324,000 barrels per day (bpd) and export volumes reach approximately 347,000 bpd.

West Qurna-2 Operational & Labor Risk Profile

Parameter Current Metric / Indicator Risk Scenario Field Location Northern Basra Governorate Strategic onshore super-giant reservoir Current Crude Output ~324,000 bpd Complete shutdown in case of full operational strike Current Export Volume ~347,000 bpd Severe disruption to southern maritime export streams Operator Framework Lukoil consortium / Basra Oil Company (BOC) Dispute centers on contract parity and state arrears Labor Deadline 7-day formal ultimatum (September 15, 2026) Staged escalations leading to general walkout

West Qurna-2 represents a major pillar of southern crude flows feeding into the Basra Oil Terminal for Basra Medium and Heavy grades. Any labor-induced operational halt would remove over 300,000 bpd from Iraq’s seaborne supply, directly undermining export schedules and tightening the state’s hard-currency revenue streams during a period of acute macroeconomic scrutiny.

World.title: Police clash with degree holders outside Finance Ministry in Baghdad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Demonstrations organized by long-term university graduates, top-ranking achievers, and higher degree holders turned violent outside the Ministry of Finance in central Baghdad on Tuesday, September 8, 2026, marking the second straight day of confrontations over central public appointments in the draft 2027 federal budget.

Riot police and law enforcement units deployed batons, electric stun devices, tear gas canisters, and rubber rounds to repel hundreds of protestors marching toward the ministry’s perimeter gates. Demonstrators, some wearing burial shrouds to signal resolve, represented a demographic bloc estimating over 100,000 unemployed graduates from past academic cycles across Iraq’s governorates.

Demonstrator Demands and On-the-Ground Clashes

Central Employment Quotas in 2027 Budget: Demonstrators demand the statutory inclusion of centralized recruitment allocations and public service civil numbers for older graduating cohorts within the forthcoming 2027 Federal Budget Law.

Scale of the Crisis: Mobilization organizers emphasized that the national backlog of unhired graduates spans more than 100,000 degree holders across disciplines—some holding computer engineering and technical credentials dated as far back as 2014 without public sector absorption.

Security Escalation and Use of Crowd Control: Protesters reported physical assaults with clubs, electric stun guns, and tear gas. A security source confirmed that while live ammunition was strictly withheld, anti-riot police deployed smoke bombs, tear gas canisters, and rubber bullets to maintain security perimeters.

Arterial Highway Blockades: Following friction on Monday, security forces cordoned off approaches to the strategic Mohammed Al-Qasim Expressway after protesters threatened to shut down the arterial transit route.

Key Incident Parameters

Parameter Operational Detail Protest Location Ministry of Finance Headquarters, Central Baghdad Participant Profile Long-term graduates (2014+), top achievers, master’s/PhD holders Estimated Demographic 100,000+ unabsorbed graduates nationwide Core Legislative Demand Statutory civil service quotas / contractual hiring in the 2027 Budget Crowd Control Tactics Smoke grenades, tear gas, electric stun devices, rubber rounds Key Transport Disruptions Mohammed Al-Qasim Expressway approach closures

The unrest flared despite an executive directive issued on Monday by Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi, instructing the Ministry of Finance to audit actual ministerial staffing requirements and allocate civil or contractual appointments for older graduates in the upcoming federal budget.

However, demonstrators deemed the directive conditional and inadequate without fixed legislative quotas. The crisis underscores the chronic fiscal dilemma confronting Baghdad: while public compensation and social transfers already swallow an average of 7.438 trillion IQD monthly from the federal treasury, severe private sector employment deficits continue to channel intense popular pressure directly toward state payrolls.

World.title: Baghdad drivers queue for hours as gasoline supplies run low
World.content:
Baghdad — Drivers formed long lines outside fuel stations in Baghdad on Saturday as gasoline supplies dropped in oil-rich Iraq due to import disruptions caused by the Middle East war.

Despite being OPEC’s second largest oil producer, Iraq imports oil derivatives because its refineries do not produce enough gasoline to meet domestic demand.

In recent weeks, as regional hostilities drag on, long queues have been reappearing every few days, mostly outside government-run fuel stations in Baghdad and other provinces.

Baghdad resident Ibrahim Hashem waited for two hours outside a fuel station on Friday without any luck, only to return early the next day hoping to fill his car.

“It is unreasonable that we produce so many barrels of oil a day, yet still do not have enough gasoline to meet our daily needs,” Hashem told AFP outside a fuel station in central Baghdad.

“We already suffer from traffic congestion because of the roads and lack of services. Now, it has become worse due to the gasoline shortage,” he added.

Iraq’s average daily consumption of gasoline is 33 million liters, but demand rises to 38 million when people panic over shortages, according to authorities.

The oil ministry said Friday that “regional events and the ongoing conflict are causing logistical challenges to tanker traffic, delaying their arrival at Iraqi ports.”

It urged citizens to buy only the quantities they need and avoid crowding fuel stations for small amounts of gasoline.

Oil Minister Bassem Mohammed Khudair said on Friday that his ministry was addressing the “temporary shortage of gasoline” and that new shipments will arrive soon to help stabilize supplies.

Like other oil producers, Iraq has been greatly affected by the US-Iran conflict, which has choked off the strategic Strait of Hormuz.

Iraq is hugely dependent on oil exports, which make up about 90 percent of its budget revenues.

Before the war erupted in February, Iraq produced around four million barrels per day, and exported an average of 3.4 million bpd, mostly via Hormuz.

After a significant drop, Iraqi oil exports recovered to more than 2.2 million bpd in August, according to the oil ministry.

Last month, Iran’s state news agency IRNA said that over the past six months, Tehran has granted permission to “a number of Iraqi oil tankers” to pass through Hormuz.

World.title: Iraq rules out airspace closure, launches 9 international routes
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The Iraqi Ministry of Transport ruled out any imminent closure of national airspace amid regional security tensions, announcing the successful activation of alternative air transit corridors alongside the launch of nine new international flight destinations connecting Baghdad, Kirkuk, and Basra to regional and global hubs.

Speaking to the official state newspaper reported on Tuesday, September 8, 2026, the Director General of the General Company for Airport Management and Air Navigation, Ihab Saad, affirmed that Iraq’s flight information region (FIR) remains safe, stable, and fully operational, logging over 500,000 passengers during the third quarter of 2026 alone.

Airspace Stability and Navigation Measures

Alternative Air Corridors: In technical collaboration with international civil aviation bodies (including ICAO), the ministry established flexible alternate transit routes to bypass regional friction zones, with technical evaluations underway to open additional corridors.

Continuous Open Skies: Saad stressed that Iraqi airspace did not experience any operational closures over recent months despite sharp regional escalations, maintaining uninterrupted overflight transit revenues and commercial passenger flows.

Overflight Readiness: Authorities maintain direct operational coordination with transit carriers, anticipating a return to historical direct flight paths as regional de-escalation takes hold.

Q3 2026 Passenger Milestone: Robust passenger throughput surpassed 500,000 travelers across domestic airports in Q3 2026, underscoring sustained commercial confidence in Iraqi civil aviation infrastructure.

The Ministry of Transport’s civil aviation expansion program establishes direct point-to-point connections across three key domestic gateways:

Departure Airport New International Routes Strategic Corridor Baghdad International Airport (BGW) Moscow, Tunis, Muscat Eastern Europe, North Africa & GCC integration Kirkuk International Airport (KIK) Antalya, Beirut, Dubai, Trabzon Tourism hubs, Levant link & GCC transit Basra International Airport (BSR) Baku, Delhi South Caucasus trade & South Asian commercial link

Saad noted that routing alternatives and destination additions form part of a structured civil aviation strategy to maximize sovereign revenue from overflight transit fees and airport usage charges:

World.title: Meta India officials summoned over child abuse ads
World.content:
NEW DELHI: National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) has summoned Meta India's managing director and country head to appear before it on Wednesday over s allegedly linked to child sexual exploitation and abuse material (CSEAM) on Instagram.

NCPCR commission took suo motu cognisance of a BBC Eye report and issued a notice to Meta Platforms Inc on July 3, seeking an explanation and documents. Meta replied a week later, following which the NCPCR instituted a formal inquiry to establish the facts.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Commission officials remained tight-lipped about Meta's response. However, they said the inquiry would examine Meta India's role in the appearance of the s, how they cleared Instagram's systems and why the situation arose.

The scrutiny would consider the stringent provisions relating to such material under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, they added.

Last week, NHRC issued notices to the ministry of electronics and information technology and ministry of information and broadcasting as part of its scrutiny of alleged CSAM on Instagram. An NHRC member Priyank Kanoongo, whose bench issued the notices Sept 2, said the inquiry was no longer only identifying who uploaded the content. "It also examines the extent to which the platform's own editorial and publishing systems participate in the generation, selection, circulation, amplification or monetisation of content," he said.

The company denied knowingly targeting such s at people.

Queries to Meta did not elicit a response.

World.title: 'You can't keep it lingering': Supreme Court to Odisha on Dara Singh plea
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Pulling up Odisha govt over its indecisiveness on taking a call on the remission plea of Dara Singh, SC Tuesday said the state cannot linger on the issue and made it clear that the official (secretary) concerned will be summoned if decision is not taken by Sept 17, the next date of hearing.

A bench of Justices Manoj Misra and Vijay Bishnoi expressed displeasure after Odisha govt sought a four-week adjournment on the ground of illness of its advocate-on-record (AoR). Deferring the hearing, the court made it clear that no adjournment will be granted on the next date. "You cannot keep it lingering like this. Take a decision, accept or reject. You cannot avoid taking decision," the bench said.

Noting that hearing in the case had been adjourned multiple times to allow the state to take a call on the remission plea, the court at the previous hearing also expressed displeasure over State Sentence Review Board not having made a decision yet. SC made it clear to state govt that it would have to pass an order if the authority did not make a decision.

Building collapses to fires, 33k died in 5 yrs from 2020

NEW DELHI: Between 2020 and 2024, nearly 33,000 people died across the country in incidents involving building collapses, fires and falls into pits and manholes, according to govt data. Most of these deaths occurred in urban areas, pointing to serious gaps in civic governance and enforcement of safety regulations.The actual numbers will be significantly higher as data on road deaths within municipal limits - many on account of potholes - and those due to contaminated water are unavailable.The data taken from reports by National Crime Records Bureau indicate that thousands of deaths every year are linked to accidents that are largely preventable and often occur due to poor upkeep of public infrastructure, unsafe buildings and non-compliance with safety regulations.While recent incidents in Delhi have caught the attention of people, instances of parts of Gurgaon and Delhi getting flooded and accumulation of piles of garbage are clear indicators of how municipal governance has deteriorated."Every corporator or councillor, municipal officer and mayor needs to take responsibility. ," said former urban development secretary M Ramachandran.Experts and former officials who have worked in the sector also stressed that govt's push for ease of construction and deregulation must follow a balanced approach. "The distinction between deregulating to increase economic activity and deregulation that leads to collapse of civic order is a fine one and has been lost in the rush to deregulate everything. Officers are unable to draw the line and have stopped attending to routine work under the guise of deregulation. An important side-effect has been de-skilling as they are no longer able to decide and act," an expert said.

World.title: BJP got Rs 1,473 crore to fight Bengal, Assam, 3 other assembly polls
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Total receipts by BJP's central party headquarters during the last round of assembly polls in Bengal, Assam, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry stood at Rs 1,472.8 crore, as per the party's election expenditure statements for Assam, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry submitted to the Election Commission.

The party's closing balance rose to Rs 7,627.2 crore upon the completion of elections on May 6, 2026, compared to Rs 6,722.6 crore on March 15, 2026.

BJP, including the party's central headquarters and the relevant state and district units, spent a total Rs 160 crore on the assembly elections in Assam, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry. Assam accounted for the BJP's highest spend at Rs 96.3 crore, followed by TN at Rs 51.6 crore and Puducherry (Rs 11.9 crore).

Almost Rs 130.4 crore was spent on general party propaganda, while Rs 29.6 crore went to candidates as lump sum payments and on the publicity of their criminal antecedents.

The election expenditure statements for the other two states of West Bengal and Kerala are yet to be made public by EC.

As per BJP's election expenditure statements for Assam, the party spent Rs 76.7 crore on general party propaganda, which included Rs 23.1 crore spent by its central unit, and another Rs 19.5 crore spent on candidates.





While Rs 27.3 crore was spent on travel expenses of star campaigners in Assam, Rs 37 crore was on s, Rs 8.9 crore on publicity materials and Rs 2.3 crore on other expenses by the state unit. A total lump sum of Rs 19.4 crore was paid to candidates and Rs 16.7 lakh spent on publishing criminal antecedents of candidates.

In TN, BJP authorised a total spend of Rs 44.5 crore for general party propaganda. Another Rs 7 crore was spent on candidates.

In its expenditure statement released earlier for the same set of elections, Congress had declared a total spend of Rs 248.6 crore.

World.title: Sri Lanka a close friend, India stands by it: Rajnath Singh
World.content:
Defence minister

said in Colombo Tuesday that India and Sri Lanka are close friends and India will always stand firmly with Sri Lanka whenever the island nation faces a crisis.

Singh, who is on a three-day visit to Sri Lanka, has become the first Indian defence minister to visit the island nation for defence-level talks after nearly 40 years.

KC Pant was the defence minister to visit the island for such talks in 1988.

"The relationship between India and Sri Lanka is based on shared history, culture, and faith. We stand with Sri Lanka through thick and thin and are committed to the peace, prosperity, and development of both countries," said Singh as he began his visit with an interaction with the Indian diaspora.

Singh said both nations share close cultural and civilisational ties which have provided a strong foundation for the growth of bilateral relationship.

"I am experiencing a sense of belonging after coming here," he said while emphasising the importance of robust regional alliances. He highlighted India's expanding global influence and economic strength, and appreciated the work done by the diaspora.

Before leaving for Colombo, Rajnath posted on X, "Besides our longstanding partnership as well as deep historical and civilisational ties, Sri Lanka is one of our most important partners under the 'Neighbourhood First' and 'MAHASAGAR' initiatives."





Addressing the diaspora, Rajnath highlighted India's rapid economic transformation, stating that the country is among the fastest-growing major economies in the world and contributes more than 16% to global growth.

He said that India's economy, which stood at $2 trillion in 2014, has doubled to approximately $4 trillion over the last decade.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The defence minister added that amid global economic challenges, the country's economy grew at 7.8% in the first quarter of financial year 2026-27.

Singh also underlined the improvement in macroeconomic stability, saying that average inflation over the last 12 years has been approximately 4.7%, compared to 10-11% during the earlier period.

The minister said India has concluded trade deals with 38 countries over the last 12 years, including free trade agreements with eight major nations, compared to just four before 2014.

Referring to the India-EU FTA as the 'Mother of all deals', he said the agreement opens access to the massive EU market and reflects India's growing diplomatic and economic capabilities.

World.title: Absorbing unqualified pvt school teachers will ruin students: Supreme Court
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Tuesday disapproved Assam's Congress-era law that allowed a large number of teachers engaged in private schools and charitable educational institutions to be appointed/absorbed in govt employment and barred the present govt from appointing or absorbing any person as a teacher in a school or college if he/she did not have requisite qualifications.

Senior advocate Ranjit Kumar, appearing for petitioner Rajesh Chauhan, told a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that teachers engaged on an ad hoc basis in private schools were getting absorbed as teachers in govt service in utter disregard of prescribed educational qualifications. Kumar said as per an HC order, teachers who are not qualified would be given salary on a par with govt school teachers.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Justice Bagchi asked whether that HC judgement had been challenged. Kumar said at the end the quality of education is suffering. The bench issued notice to the state govt and Centre and directed that "no teacher shall be appointed/absorbed in schools and colleges unless he/she possesses requisite qualifications under RTE Act, NCTE Act and UGC Act."

The CJI said, "The future of the generations of students will be destroyed with these kinds of appointments.

World.title: BJP demands Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann's resignation over farmer's suicide
World.content:
NEW DELHI: BJP alleged Tuesday that AAP was like a "thug gang" and demanded the resignation of CM Bhagwant Mann after a man died by suicide, allegedly following pressure from AAP functionaries to apologise for questioning minister Harpal Singh Cheema over the drug menace in his village.

BJP played a video of Gulzar Singh, a man belonging to a Scheduled Caste who consumed pesticide, narrating the incident and the pressure brought to bear on him after he raised the drug issue during an event attended by Cheema. Singh said his son was addicted to drugs. "After the minister left, an AAP neta, who is the sarpanch of the village, visited Gulzar Singh's home and asked him to apologise to the minister for his remarks," BJP spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia said.

Before his death at a hospital, Singh named those who allegedly threatened him, Bhatia said, alleging, "Protector has turned predator", and demanding Mann's resignation.

World.title: VIT Chennai, The Hindu to hold conclave on the future of biotechnology on Sept. 11
World.content:
As biotechnology moves increasingly from the laboratory into everyday life, transforming healthcare, diagnostics, pharmaceuticals, and sustainability, the need to understand its possibilities and implications has never been greater.

Bringing together some of the country’s leading voices in science, research, healthcare, and industry, The Hindu and the Vellore Institute of Technology (VIT), Chennai will present the Biotech Conclave 2026 in Chennai on Friday (September 11, 2026).

The one-day conclave will be inaugurated by CII-president designate Dr. Suchitra Ella, the co-founder and MD of Bharat Biotech, who will deliver the inaugural address, and presided over by G. Viswanathan, founder and chancellor, VIT.

Higher secondary students, undergraduates, researchers, and biotechnology aspirants will have an opportunity to engage with experts and gain insights into emerging technologies, research pathways, careers, and the challenges confronting the sector.

The programme brings together a diverse group of eminent scientists, researchers, healthcare leaders and policymakers, including Professor K. VijayRaghavan, Dr. Vasan Sambandamurthy, Dr. Vinod Scaria, Dr. Ganapathy, Dr. Maneesh Paul, Dr. Kalpana Gowrishankar, Mayur Abhaya, and Ajay Mahipal, among others.

The sessions will examine the role of technology in accelerating biotechnology research, the possibilities offered by gene editing and precision medicine, India’s emergence as a global biopharma hub, the country’s research and innovation ecosystem, and the funding landscape for biotechnology research.

“Biotechnology represents one of the most consequential frontiers of education and research, with the power to improve lives and address some of society’s most urgent challenges. Through this conclave, VIT Chennai aims to encourage students to see biotechnology not only as a field of study, but as a pathway to innovation, enterprise, and meaningful service to humanity,” G. V. Selvam, vice-president, VIT, said.

“For The Hindu, this conclave is an opportunity to bring meaningful, accessible and forward-looking conversations on science to young audiences. By convening students, researchers, experts and industry voices on one platform, we hope to deepen public engagement with biotechnology and inspire informed curiosity about the field’s role in India’s future,” Sundar Kondur, chief revenue officer, The Hindu Group, said.

World.title: West Asia conflict LIVE: U.S. says it destroyed five Iranian oil tankers after attacks on American warship
World.content:
Iran’s ‌Revolutionary Guards said early on ⁠Wednesday (September 9, 2026) that ships ‌in Kuwaiti ‌and ‌Bahraini ⁠ports which ⁠host Americans will be targeted ‌in response to U.S. attacks ‌on Iranian oil tankers. Iranian media on Tuesday (September 8, 2026) reported that a U.S. missile struck a tanker off the coast of Kharg Island, adding that there were no casualties. U.S. forces destroyed five Iranian oil carriers on Tuesday (September 8, 2026) after Tehran launched ballistic missiles at an American warship twice in recent days, the U.S. military said.

“A small Iranian tanker was targeted by a missile attack by the American terrorist army four miles from Kharg Island. The tanker was hit by a projectile from American forces in the area of the Kharg Island anchorage,” Tasnim news agency said. The chief of staff of the Iranian Armed Forces, Ali Abdollahi, on Tuesday warned Tehran would attack U.S. bases in the region if Iranian oil tankers were hit.

The U.S. military said on Tuesday (September 8, 2026) that one of its underwater drones “malfunctioned” after Iran said its forces captured an American unmanned submarine in the strategic Strait of Hormuz. “An underwater drone operated by U.S. forces malfunctioned more than a day ago. It was surveying regional waters in support of ongoing operations,” U.S. Central Command spokesperson Captain Tim Hawkins said, without mentioning whether the device was seized by Iran.

The latest strikes are part of a dual economic and military approach by President Donald Trump as he struggles to bring an end to a more than six-month-old war with Tehran.

World.title: J&K CM Omar Abdullah watches ‘Mirzapur’ at Srinagar’s only functional multiplex to flip cinema culture
World.content:
J&K Chief Minister Omar Abdullah on Tuesday (September 8, 2026) watched the movie ‘Mirzapur’ at the Kashmir valley’s only functional multiplex, INOX at Srinagar’s Shivpora area along with its cast during the ongoing International Film Festival Jammu & Kashmir (IFFJK), being held under the theme ‘Rang-e-Cinema’.

Mr. Abdullah was joined by the star cast of the movie, including Pankaj Tripathi, who plays the popular character of Kaleen Bhaiya, and Divyenndu, who portrayed the role of Munna Bhaiya in the hit ‘Mirzapur’ series. In a rare scene from Kashmir, Mr. Abdullah sat with the Valley’s film-enthusiast audiences to watch the movie.

“The presence of leading artistes and filmmakers in J&K would further strengthen the region’s association with cinema and contribute to building a vibrant film ecosystem in J&K,” said Mr. Abdullah, on the second day of the ongoing four-day film festival.

Mr. Abdullah highlighted the role of the actors of the movie and appreciated their contribution to Indian cinema.

“This is a good beginning. It provides an opportunity to outsiders to observe Kashmiriyat and local culture. It will also motivate filmmakers to make more films. There is great talent here,” said Mr. Tripathi.

Mr. Divyenndu asked local filmmakers to come forward and make films. “Locals need to watch these films. We all need to promote it,” said Mr. Divyenndu.

Kashmir saw closure of around 15 cinema halls in the 1990s. There were several attempts in the past to popularise cinema culture but failed. However, the first multiplex, INOX, in 2022 became the first such functional theatre after a gap of 23 years. Around 135 films are being screened from 41 countries during the film festival, including at INOX in Srinagar.

World.title: Water cannons used as Punjab Congress members stage demonstration against AAP after villager’s death
World.content:
Police resorted to using water cannons on Tuesday (September 8, 2026) to disperse Punjab Congress leaders and workers staging a demonstration against the ruling Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government in Punjab.

Congress members from Punjab gathered here at the party office, from where they attempted to cross the barricades erected by the administration, in an attempt to march toward Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann’s official residence.

Congress leaders questioned the functioning of the Punjab government, saying that the people who had brought AAP to power in the hope of change are today being forced to take to the streets to fight for their rights as the State government has failed on all fronts.

The Congress leaders demanded immediate dismissal of the Finance Minister Harpal Singh Cheema over the alleged death of a man, who died by suicide as he was allegedly being pressured by local AAP leaders to apologise for questioning Minister Harpal Singh Cheema over the drug menace in his village recently.

Punjab Pradesh Congress president Amarinder Singh Raja Warring said that Gulzar Singh, a resident of Dirba in Sangrur district, in his dying declaration, claimed that Harpal Singh Cheema was responsible for his death.

Senior leader and former minister Balbir Singh Sidhu said that the AAP government had made tall claims about eliminating the drug menace from Punjab, but the ground reality is completely different. “The registration of 8,973 NDPS cases in 2024, along with Punjab ranking first in the country in cases related to drug trafficking, is serious evidence of the government’s failure,” he said.

“AAP MP Malvinder Singh Kang’s description of Greater Mohali Area Development Authority (GMADA) as a centre of loot raises serious questions about the government’s functioning. He said that when such allegations are coming from within the ruling party itself, the people of Punjab deserve a transparent account of the entire matter,” he added.

Separately, a delegation of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), led by Punjab president Kewal Singh Dhillon, met the Punjab Governor Gulab Chand Kataria and submitted a memorandum seeking immediate action in two serious cases related to Sangrur district, one the death of Gulzar Singh and the other the alleged custodial assault of Mohanjit Singh.

Mr. Dhillon said late Gulzar Singh had raised the issue of the alleged open sale of ‘chitta’ (heroin) in his area during a public meeting held by the State Finance Minister. The BJP president said that in a video purportedly recorded before his death, Gulzar Singh had named the Finance Minister and others, whom he allegedly held responsible for the circumstances leading to his death.

The party demanded that the case should not be treated merely as a death by suicide case and that the allegations made by Gulzar Singh should be thoroughly investigated in accordance with law.

Mr. Dhillon also brought the alleged custodial assault of Mohanjit Singh to the Governor’s notice, saying Mr. Mohanjit Singh was detained by the police after he protested against the Punjab Government’s handling of the drug menace during Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann’s visit to Sangrur. He was later allegedly tortured in custody.

In a post on ‘X’, Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) president Sukhbir Singh Badal said “What can be more significant than a dying person’s final statement? Despite Gulzar Singh explicitly naming Finance Minister Harpal Cheema and several AAP workers, holding them directly responsible for threatening and beating him, the FIR in the case does not mention Harpal Cheema even once! Why? Who decided to ignore the victim’s dying declaration?”

He demanded National Human Rights Commission to take cognisance of the matter.

A father, watching his family being destroyed as his son battled drug addiction, raised his voice and questioned @HarpalCheemaMLA



He was subjected to such immense harassment and pressure that he ultimately attempted suicide. He held Harpal Cheema and the village Sarpanch… pic.twitter.com/sguCBgvo6w — Amarinder Singh Raja Warring (@RajaBrar_INC) September 7, 2026

(Those in distress can dial Tele MANAS helpline at 14416)

World.title: Out of Satya Niketan, into same trap: students struggle for safer stay in Delhi
World.content:
Students leaving Satya Niketan in search of safer living conditions are finding that paying more does not necessarily buy them safety. Even after spending up to ₹20,000 a month, many are ending up in cramped rooms in ageing buildings, with poor ventilation, inadequate facilities and little assurance about structural safety.

The building collapse a few days ago has prompted students to look beyond Satya Niketan, with many exploring areas such as Vasant Gaon, Naraina and Mayapuri, as well as neighbourhoods with easy access to metro stations.

However, for those on limited budgets, the search has often led to the same compromises they were trying to escape. As a result, many have already returned to their hometowns, missing classes.

Cost of education

For newcomers, the economic cost of education begins not with college fees but with finding private accommodation. In student hubs, rooms are available for ₹8,000 to ₹21,000 a month, often with little difference in the facilities offered.

“I have paid ₹48,000 [including deposit] in the first month itself for accommodation. My college fee is ₹27,000, payable in instalments throughout the year. Besides this, I also need to cover my personal expenses. My father, a mechanic, has managed the money with difficulty,” said Priyam Khushwaha, a first-year student from Uttar Pradesh.

Karan Mahajan, a second-year student from Punjab, said Vasant Gaon and Naraina have cheaper accommodation with slightly bigger rooms, but no one can guarantee safety there either.

“The only way to break the cycle of poor conditions is to rent a flat and arrange for food, laundry, etc. on your own,” he added.

Most accommodations offer a single room with two beds placed close together, a cupboard and a washroom. Food and water are included in the rent, but electricity is charged separately, with some accommodations charging as much as ₹14 per unit.

“Room rent can vary from floor to floor in a single building. Rent agreements take no responsibility in case of an emergency, and no refund or return policy is mentioned in such cases. The rooms are shared by two persons, with each room in a five-storey building fetching the owners at least ₹30,000. Despite that, what we get in the name of food is deplorable. The buildings are full of cube-like structures separated by plywood,” said Kapilesh Yadav, a third-year DU student from Haryana.

Caught in the trap

Newcomers to the city are the first to fall into the “trap”.

“As a fresher, the only thing on your mind is to find a place to dump your luggage and sleep at night. The rooms are marketed as the best thing available, and if you point out faults, the managers simply say, ‘Leave, we will find someone else,’” said Ankita Sharma, a first-year student who moved to Delhi from Uttar Pradesh a week ago.

“It took me at least 15-20 visits to find the current PG where I am staying. I pay ₹20,000 for a basic room and electricity is paid for through a monthly recharge. In the first two days, I got scammed when my electricity bill showed ₹600. An average student here pays around ₹1,500 a month for electricity,” she said.

The cracks and structural faults come to light after a few months, and students cannot vacate immediately because of an 11-month rent agreement.

“I vacated my previous PG a year ago after many bad experiences. I am yet to receive my two-month security deposit of ₹30,000,” said Manpreet Kaur, a second-year student from Punjab.

“I was taking a bath one day when a tile fell from the ceiling. Within days, half of the bathroom tiles fell off. When I contacted the PG managers, they said it would be repaired soon. But no repairs were made, and two days later, the exhaust fan fell. I realised it was no longer safe to live there, so I shifted to another PG nearby. The conditions here are better but not ideal,” she added.

The PGs where owners stay in the same building were reported to have better conditions. However, these buildings rise to five or six floors, exceeding permissible limits.

World.title: Revisit policy of banning social, political groups in J&K: Mirwaiz Umar Farooq
World.content:
Kashmir chief cleric Mirwaiz Umar Farooq on Tuesday (September 8, 2026) urged the Centre to revisit its policy of “bans on social and political organisations in J&K”.

Commenting on the statement of banned Jamaat-e-Islami (JeI) amir (ex-chief) Ghulam Muhammad Bhat, the Mirwaiz said, “The public statement by JeI chief is concerning. It would be in the interest of peace and stability that New Delhi listens to people’s pleas and revisit its policy of bans on social and political organisations in J&K, bringing an end to the harassment and intimidation that accompanies such restrictions.”

Mr. Bhat, a few days ago in a video message, distanced the JeI from a political faction of the banned organisation and said it will put up a legal battle to remove the ban on the socio-religious group, which was banned by the Ministry of Home Affairs in 2019.

“Where these forced measures are challenged before the court of law, it is at least expected that due process is allowed to run its course fairly, without taking actions that render legal remedies meaningless. Attached properties and institutions should be treated with restraint and in accordance with law and judicial process,” said the Mirwaiz.

He said a sustainable political process cannot be built by excluding genuine voices or replacing them with convenient alternatives. “Those who command real social and political presence must be allowed space and engaged through dialogue. Respect for the rule of law, fairness and meaningful political engagement remain essential for any way forward to real peace,” said the Mirwaiz.

World.title: On Sheikh Abdullah’s 44th death anniversary, NC reclaims his political legacy through archival videos
World.content:
Ruling National Conference (NC) on the 44th death anniversary of party founder Sheikh Muhammad Abdullah on Tuesday (September 8, 2026) desisted from making any policy statements and instead focussed on reclaiming the political legacy of the party leader by streaming archival videos.

J&K Chief Minister Omar Abdullah and NC president Dr. Farooq Abdullah visited the grave of the Sheikh Muhammad Abdullah, also known as “Baba-e-Qaum” and “Sher-e-Kashmir”, at Nigeen in Srinagar and paid tributes. Senior NC leaders also joined the special prayers at the graveyard.

Paying his tributes, Mr. Abdullah said the Sheikh was “a towering leader whose place in the history and collective memory of Jammu & Kashmir remains eternal”.

“For generations, his name has lived on in the stories, memories and emotions of Kashmir. Today, we remember him not only for the place he holds in our history, but for the enduring bond he shared with the people of J&K,” said Mr. Abdullah.

In a rare tribute, the party social media handles streamed archival videos on the Sheikh to put focus on his political legacy, which included the funeral procession of the party founder. In one such video former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi could be seen visiting the grieving Abdullahs in Srinagar and consoling the wife of the Sheikh.

“His legacy remains an integral part of our history. His life was dedicated to the dignity, rights and aspirations of the people of J&K,” said Mr. Abdullah, while sharing one of the videos of the Sheikh on social media platforms.

Speaking on the occasion in Jammu, J&K minister Satish Sharma reiterated the commitment to preserving the secular and inclusive identity of Jammu and Kashmir, “a vision championed by Sheikh Abdullah throughout his life”.

“NC remains steadfast in its mission to safeguard the rights of all people, ensuring freedom of religion, equality, and unity in diversity. Upholding this spirit and isolating those who spread hate is the true tribute to Sheikh Sahib,” said Mr. Sharma. He also recalled the pioneering Land Reforms Act introduced under his leadership, saying “this historic reform empowered farmers and changed the socio-economic fabric of J&K, making them masters of their own destiny.”

The NC founder, who was dislodged from the political scene, arrested and shifted outside the erstwhile State in 1953, and his party has ruled J&K for decades. The Sheikh has left behind a saga of sweet and bitter relations with the Centre and always pushed for the restoration of the pre-1953 position of J&K as a political settlement.

World.title: Odisha’s rural work does not have adequate photographic evidence, says a draft audit report
World.content:
Over 90% of works executed by Odisha’s Rural Development Department had either no photographic evidence or only minimal photographic evidence defeating objective of real time monitoring, says a draft audit report.

According to draft audit titled “Data Led Compliance Audit on Rural Works” shared with Rural Development department, in 2013 it was decided that photographs of all original road, bridge, building (costing more than ₹25 lakh) and pipe water supply works should be uploaded in Works and Accounts Management Information System (WAMIS) every month, irrespective of the stage of execution.

In November 2013, the department further mandated uploading of geo-tagged photographs of all works to facilitate effective monitoring.

“Audit analysed 25,038 works executed in the selected 12 divisions during 2019- 2026. Of these, 13,083 works (52.25%) had no photograph and 9,723 works (38.83%) had only one or two photographs. Thus 22,806 works (91.09%) had either no photographic evidence or only minimal photographic evidence,” finds the audit.

“Test-check of high-value works further identified 17 contracts aggregating ₹122.66 crore with inadequate photographic documentation while 14 had only one or two photographs and three works costing ₹21.21 crore had none,” the draft audit further points out.

According to draft report, audit also observed that several road works spanning overlapping chainages could not be effectively verified as photographs were either unavailable or of poor quality.

“Many uploaded images were blurred, dark, unclear, lacked visible geo-tag details or were taken from inappropriate angles, rendering them unsuitable for establishing the location, extent and stage of execution. Thus, absence of stage-wise geo-tagged photographs significantly weakened WAMIS as a monitoring tool,” audit finds.

“Consequently, the department and higher authorities could not independently verify the physical progress, distinct identity or extent of works, particularly where multiple works were executed in the same location. This increased the risk of duplicate or overlapping execution, incorrect progress reporting and avoidable expenditure remaining undetected,” the draft report says.

Subu R, Principal Accountant General (Audit-1), Odisha, has written to Yamini Sarangi, Rural Development Secretary, to submit department’s views on audit findings.

World.title: Govt hikes petrol price by Rs5.58, HSD by Rs4.18
World.content:
The government on Tuesday increased the price of petrol by Rs5.58 per litre while increasing the price of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs4.18 per litre.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs364.35 per litre while HSD will cost Rs385.95 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will be applicable on Sept 9 (Wednesday).

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

On July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: PM Shehbaz seeks input from business community as he stresses export-led growth
World.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday sought recommendations from industrialists and businesspeople on how to increase export-led growth in the country.

“Whatever growth we have to achieve, it has to be export-led growth, period,” the premier remarked while addressing a meeting with prominent leaders of the business community.

He added that any other kind of growth had “no meaning” and reinforced that economic growth had to be export-led.

“Today’s meeting is because we’re in the first quarter, in the month of September. I need your opinions on how to increase our exports, as well as what challenges we will face and how to address them,” PM Shehbaz said.

The prime minister gave the example of special tax relief to exporters as a means to achieve this growth.

He recalled that in the run-up to the federal budget presented in June this year, the government held multiple meetings and had “intense consultations” with the business community.

“Through your consultations in difficult times, the way we brought structural changes over the past two-and-a-half years … it’s teamwork. It’s a tremendous teamwork,” PM Shehbaz said.

“As a result, we made overdue structural reforms. It’s a long journey, but through enforcement we recovered Rs800 billion in one year. No new taxes were imposed.”

PM Shehbaz praised the teamwork involved between the business community and the government, adding that Pakistan was ready to pursue growth with their input.

In July, Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal said the government was pursuing a strategy to diversify exportable products and market portfolios to achieve a target of six per cent sustainable economic growth.

“Our destination is not only stabilisation but sustainable growth of at least 6pc. That growth has to be export-led; otherwise it will become another economic bubble that bursts within a few years,” he said.

Last Monday, Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb said that the government’s focus was on building an ecosystem to support sustainable growth that was led by the private sector and export-driven.

The minister said Pakistan had moved from stabilisation towards growth, but the key challenge now was to ensure its sustainability.

Earlier this week, PM Shehbaz welcomed the launch of export insurance coverage by the Export Development Fund (EDF) and the Export-Import Bank of Pakistan, saying the facility would help small and medium enterprises (SMEs) expand the country’s exports.

Chairing a meeting on the EDF, he said the Rs3bn risk pool would expand access to export credit insurance, especially for SMEs, and help the business community increase export volumes.

He described the initiative as a highly welcome step to promote small and medium-sized businesses and strengthen the national economy.

World.title: Sindh AG interrupts Mir Raza commission proceedings during police surgeon's testimony, objects to family's queries
World.content:
KARACHI: A judicial commission formed to probe the circumstances and possible negligence around the Mir Raza Ali murder case issued notice to Sindh Home Minister Ziaul Hassan Lanjar after the Sindh Advocate General Jawad Dero interrupted the proceedings on Tuesday and objected to the lawyer representing the victims’ family asking any questions.

The interruption came during Karachi Police Surgeon Dr Summaiya Syed’s testimony.

The order issued after the commission’s proceedings stated: “It is regrettable that the commission’s proceedings have been interrupted by Sindh Advocate General Jawad Dero. He has objected to the family’s counsel asking any questions on behalf of the deceased’s family.

“The highest law officer of the Sindh government making such a submission surprised me. It is more meaningful that the disturbance comes at a time when the police surgeon was explaining the role of senior police officers during the post-mortem examination.”

The murder case has been mired in controversy, particularly after Dr Syed pointed out flaws in the findings of Ali’s first autopsy. Following that, Ali’s body was exhumed a second post-mortem was conducted.

Dr Syed was part of the medical board that conducted the second autopsy, whose findings ruled out the possibility of suicide — a likelihood around which the law enforcers had initially tried to build the case. Meanwhile, Ali’s family accused police of trying to bury the facts.

The one-member commission, headed by Sindh High Court Justice Omar Sial, heard the case today and noted in its order that Sindh Assembly member Faryal Talpur had suggested its formation to the provincial chief executive “for a transparent and impartial comprehensive investigation”.

The order cited a Dawn report dated Aug 9, according to which, it said, Talpur stressed that justice for Ali must be ensured and “public should be transparently informed of all facts surrounding the case. The newspaper further cites her as saying that providing justice to the bereaved family and maintaining public confidence in the justice system was the fundamental responsibility of the government and relevant institutions”.

Sindh Home Minister Lanjar and Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah had echoed these sentiments, the order stated.

Justice Sial further wrote in the order that he was saddened that the advocate general had objected to requests by Ali’s family through their counsel for certain clarification.

“It is the commission’s discretion to determine whether a query is relevant to the proceedings or not. Further, the commission’s terms of reference required it to find the true facts and circumstances of the case,” he said, adding that a notice was being issued to Lanjar to appear before the commission on Sept 10 and “put forward his stance […] as to whether the family is barred from asking questions to satisfy themselves that justice is being done”.

Justice Sial further stated, “In my opinion, a deliberate attempt has been made by the Sindh advocate general to restrain the commission from addressing the family’s queries in a transparent manner.”

Plea against FIR

In a separate development, a two-member bench of the SHC, headed by Justice Muhammad Saleem Jessar and including Justice Abdul Hamid Bhurgri, took up a petition seeking the quashing of a case registered on August 27 against “around 100 people” for staging a protest in connection with the case.

In the first information report (FIR), the protesters have been accused of blocking the road for vehicular movement and pedestrians at Karachi’s Sharea Faisal.

The plea, a copy of which is available with Dawn, named Ammar Ahmed Khan, Muhammad Zubai Ali, Taha Shaikh, Zarar Khalid, Saad Shehriyar, and Hassan Surya as the petitioners.

The SHC issued notices to the Sindh advocate general, the prosecutor general and other respondents for Nov 11 after hearing the plea today, directing that in the meantime, no coercive action should be taken against the petitioners.

The court further directed that the investigation should be conducted strictly in accordance with the law and directed the petitioners to cooperate when required.

“It is clarified that this order shall not be construed as an impediment in conducting the investigation strictly in accordance with law,” the court said.

The case so far

The body of 25-year-old Ali was found in Karachi’s Gulistan-i-Jauhar last month, a day after he went missing on July 28.
