World.title: Police raids in Victoria, Queensland in cross-border CFMEU operation
World.content:
Updated NationalCFMEU Police raids in Victoria, Queensland in cross-border CFMEU operation Nick McKenzie and Dominique Tassell Updated September 9, 2026 — 10:58am ,first published September 9, 2026 — 8:19am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Police have launched raids in two states as part of a cross-border operation involving Queensland and Victorian detectives and allegations that union officials were corrupted. The surprise operation was led by Victoria’s Taskforce Hawk and included Queensland detectives linked to the state’s commission of inquiry into the CFMEU. Vehicles parked outside the Queensland CFMEU offices in Bowen Hills, Brisbane, as the premises are raided on Wednesday. Brisbane Times / Dominique Tassell According to information detailed in search warrants, authorities allege that CFMEU officials are involved in the federal crime of seeking to corrupt a member of a registered trade union. In a statement, Victoria Police said Taskforce Hawk detectives had also executed a number of warrants in Victoria as part of its investigation alleged corrupting benefits offences.



Three people were arrested in Victoria and would be interviewed by police, the statement said. The co-operation between Queensland and Victorian police is a significant development and reveals attempts to uncover suspected crime and corruption in the building industry has become a borderless effort. About 10 plain-clothed officers were seen at the CFMEU premises in Bowen Hills, in Brisbane’s inner north, on Wednesday morning, with a security guard stationed inside. Four unmarked police cars were parked outside the building, and the door was manually opened to let each officer inside.



A CFMEU spokesperson told this masthead: “CFMEU has been made aware of a police investigation this morning and will co-operate fully.” Four officers left the building about 8.50am, driving away in two vehicles. No one was seen carrying any items out of the offices. The last significant corrupting benefits case involved the jailing of former NSW CFMEU official Darren Greenfield and his son Michael. The suspected offending that led to the Brisbane raid on Wednesday allegedly took place in Queensland and NSW.



Regardless of whether the raids lead to charges, they will almost certainly inform the coming Victorian royal commission and the ongoing Queensland commission of inquiry into the CFMEU. The police activity comes a fortnight after the taskforce oversaw raids targeting officials in Victoria and former members of an outlaw bikie gang in connection to allegations of bribery and criminal activity. The royal commission in Victoria into the construction industry was announced after organised crime infiltration of the CFMEU and the government’s Big Build program was uncovered by this masthead and 60 Minutes. The Building Bad investigation revealed allegations of sexual exploitation of women, drug trafficking, systemic corruption and bribery that cost taxpayers billions of dollars.

World.title: Elon Musk offered his ex $40m to not take part in a new doco about him. She did it anyway
World.content:
CultureMoviesCinema Elon Musk offered his ex $40m to not take part in a new doco about him. She did it anyway Stephanie Bunbury September 9, 2026 — 10:56am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Venice: A four-hour documentary tracing the life and work of Elon Musk – maker of electric cars, rockets, Starlink satellites, right-wing propaganda and “a legion of children” from his own loins – has proved the pivotal talking point of the Venice Film Festival. Alex Gibney, the prolific director of documentaries about subjects including Enron, Edward Snowden and Scientology, tells the story of his rise to dizzying power – and phenomenal riches – in Musk, which confronts the question of how and why anyone has been allowed so much influence. Gibney usually interviews his subjects, but Musk refused to participate. Filmmaker Alex Gibney (middle) with tech journalist Zoë Schiffer (left) and Musk’s former girlfriend Ashley St Clair, at the Venice Film Festival this week. AP Photo/Scott A Garfitt It wasn’t easy to find other willing interviewees. “There was a fear of talking. Among his critics, his business colleagues and his friends, very few agreed to speak,” Gibney said at a festival press conference. One exception was the film’s trump card, a former MAGA influencer and Musk’s ex-girlfriend Ashley St Clair, who gave birth to one of Musk’s 14 children in 2024.



St Clair was close to Musk during the heady few months when he was head of President Donald Trump’s newly minted Department of Government Efficiency, striking out entire project budgets and sacking thousands of government employees. Loading “Elon is a nuke,” St Clair told the cameras. St Clair, who was in Venice with the film, alleged he had offered her $US40 million not to participate in the documentary. “When you’re offered something like that it really causes a debate in your head about what your speech means,” she says. “How valuable that is – and why do they want to offer me that much money not to speak?” She has her own answers. “It has to do with his sense of unreality, Elon’s relationships are complicated in general but, especially, he has a complicated relationship with the truth.” Gibney put his own spin on this by putting Musk’s extreme pronouncements into the mouth of a graphic avatar in a space suit. He says he was picking up on Musk’s obsession with video games.



“But also, so much of what Elon Musk says has an air of unreality to it.” He soon realised that what looked like a story about new technology and its overlords was “the story of old wine in a new bottle, the story of the confidence man. His wealth and power come from inflated stock.” Elon Musk was appointed head of the Department of Government Efficiency and took to the task with gusto. AP It was Enron all over again. He maintains a measured tone, however, as he covers the tech lord’s troubled South African childhood, his command over the satellites crucial to many countries’ military operations, his acquisition and manipulation of Twitter, now called X, his alliance – and fall-out – with President Trump and his $158 billion Tesla remuneration package. We see his beginnings, devising and then selling an online business directory, then taking and selling a slice of Peter Thiel’s Paypal, which provided him with working capital. Gibney spends a good deal of time debunking Musk’s promise of an imminent life on Mars. The research is meticulous, even if nothing is new. “I think it’s bearing witness and reaching out to witnesses,” says Gibney. “And also trying to understand. Particularly in this bewildering world of inputs from social media and 24-hour news access. There are so many trees that I think it’s worth stitching together a narrative that shows the forest. The film attempts to reframe the story.”



There were mutterings before the press screenings about the prospect of having to watch a four-hour documentary half-way through an exhausting festival, but the film proved a literal eye-opener that drew an energetic critical response. Editor's pick Film Festivals Hidden cameras, no script: Oasis documentary goes inside the Gallagher brothers’ split “A chillingly forensic hatchet job,” said the Telegraph; “a poleaxing portrait of the tech titan as a con man,” read the Hollywood Reporter’s headline; “an epic study of the world’s richest and dullest man … excellent”, according to the Guardian. It is Musk’s involvement in political influence, especially on the eve of the mid-term elections in the United States, that feels least transparent and thus the most troubling aspect of his influence. “We know during DOGE, the boys (Musk’s team of very young men who carried out mass sackings from government departments) had super administrative status at all agencies,” says Gibney. “That meant they had access to an extraordinary amount of data on American citizens - and moving that data would be as easy, as I understand it, as copying a file into a folder.



“Would that folder be at Space X and might he be using that information for an AI (tool) to influence the election? Yes. I don’t know that it will happen but it might happen. It was a warning.” So, asks one journalist at the press conference, one short answer: is Elon Musk dangerous to democracy? “Extremely,” says Gibney. “There’s your short answer. He’s very dangerous.” Must-see movies, interviews and all the latest from the world of film delivered to your inbox.

World.title: Almost half of Victoria’s roads in poor condition, as decline outpaces repairs
World.content:
Remove items from your saved list to add more.

Almost half of the state’s government-managed roads are in poor or very poor condition, with decline outpacing repairs, according to a new report from the Victorian Auditor-General’s Office (VAGO).

Tracking the deterioration of Victoria’s “state roads” – major arterials owned and operated by the Department of Transport and Planning which span 23,000 kilometres – the report released on Wednesday found current government funding to maintain or improve state roads was insufficient.

A report by the Victorian auditor-general has found state roads are deteriorating faster than repairs are made. Joe Armao

“This has meant it [funding] focuses more on reactive and safety-critical repairs rather than preventative works,” the report found.

The vast majority of state roads are in regional Victoria, and carry most of the state’s traffic and freight vehicles. About 48 per cent of state roads were considered in poor or very poor condition in 2024 – jumping by almost a quarter from 39 per cent in 2021.

World.title: ‘Wants to be stuck with me’: Ellidy Pullin announces engagement
World.content:
LifestyleLife & relationshipsSex & relationships ‘Wants to be stuck with me’: Ellidy Pullin announces engagement Abby Seaman September 9, 2026 — 10:37am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Ellidy Pullin has shared the news of her engagement to Brock Wadsworth. Pullin, 38, confirmed the development via an Instagram post captioned, “HE WANTS TO BE STUCK WITH ME FOREVER” while holidaying in Europe with Wadsworth. The internet personality and podcast co-host of Darling, Shine! went public with the relationship in late 2025. Just hours after announcing the news, the couple’s post was flooded with well-wishes for the happy couple.



Related Article Sunday Life 36 hours after losing her partner, Ellidy Pullin made a life-changing decision The engagement comes six years after the sudden death of Pullin’s partner, Olympic snowboarder Alex “Chumpy” Pullin. Pullin met Wadsworth through mutual friends and knew each other for years before it is believed they began dating, about February last year. In November, they made the relationship Instagram-official while on holiday in Bali. Pullin later confirmed the details of their courtship in a December podcast episode, where she also spoke about navigating feelings of grief while falling in love.



“Of course, I love Chumpy, I still love him so much. I’ll never not love him,” she confessed. “Grief is absolutely f---ed.” Pullin admitted that she felt guilty about how happy she felt: “I was making things up in my head, now I’m just like all of those things were in my head ... I was just scared of my feelings.” Just days after her partner’s sudden death, Ellidy Pullin made the decision to retrieve his sperm. Hannah Sugarman In 2021, 15-months after Alex’s death, Pullin gave birth to their daughter, Minnie, who was conceived via IVF after she chose to undergo a post-mortem sperm retrieval. “The idea of having a baby on my own, a constant reminder of what I’d lost, was hard enough without having to deal with other people’s judgment,” Pullin wrote in her 2022 memoir, Heartstrong.



“Until someone has been in my shoes, I don’t think they’d ever be able to understand what I went through.” Make the most of your health, relationships, fitness and nutrition with our Live Well newsletter. Get it in your inbox every Monday.

World.title: Creamy, silky and, err, fibrous: The saucy social media trend making tinned beans sexy
World.content:
Tips & adviceBeans Creamy, silky and, err, fibrous: The saucy social media trend making tinned beans sexy Beans are budget-friendly and high in fibre but can be a bit of a hard sell. However, have you ever tried drowning them in satay sauce? Now we’re cooking! Jane de Graaff September 9, 2026 Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

In case you missed it, it’s the year of “maxxing” everything. Protein-maxxing, looks-maxxing, Nanna-maxxing – we’re not just leaning in to the things we love any more, we’re maxxing out on them. And that includes fibre-maxxing – or the practice of consciously increasing fibre in the diet, with a focus on potential health benefits, including gut health and blood sugar management. Enter an unlikely poster-child for the fibre-maxxing trend: beans. Now, I personally love beans (tinned, dried, refried, souped), but I’d hesitate to call them sexy. And yet, the latest social media trend for dressing them up in creamy, silky and downright decadent-looking sauces – that still aim to support health goals – is making humble beans look, well, decidedly sexier than they did before. Welcome to the world of sexy bean recipes that are flooding social media and might just get you serving some up tonight. Katrina Meynink’s creamy marry-me chickpeas recipe has the big flavours of the original, minus the meat. Katrina Meynink The sexy-creamy-beany trend The trend itself is simple: sauces that you might usually see on pasta or noodles are being drizzled over or simmered with beans as a way of introducing more fibre-rich ingredients into the diet, without compromising on flavour. The beans are, essentially, a sauce delivery system.



Variations include cacio e pepe beans (pepper and cheese), green goddess or pesto, velvety french onion and creamy curry beans – and that’s just the tip of the beanstalk. The best recipes from Australia's leading chefs straight to your inbox. Sign up Championed by content creators such as Ohio-based @dietitiandebbie Deborah Murphy (with her social media recipe series “No Boring Beans”), one clear favourite has bubbled to the top: satay-style beans. This creamy, dreamy recipe is sliding into feeds everywhere, with iterations running from super spiced and topped with fresh herbs, to mild, mellow and sweet. Is it really better for us? It’s easy to see why this dish has caught on. It relies on flavours that we already know – such as peanutty, spiced and sweet satay-style sauce – and it’s made with just a handful of pantry-staple budget-friendly ingredients. It also promises to edge us closer to potential health goals, ticking off the golden quartet: quick, budget-friendly, healthier and tasty.



But, as always, we take health-related social media claims with a grain of (ahem) salt. “The fibre-maxxing trend and rising interest in gut health has a lot to do with the popularity of these recipes,” says food and nutrition scientist Dr Emma Beckett. “But I also think it comes back to cost. People are looking for ways to make things healthier without it costing the earth.” ‘These kinds of dishes – that you already like – will be better for you if you do them with beans. There’s not much of a downside to that.’ Dr Emma Beckett, food and nutrition scientist Beckett notes that younger generations are moving away from health foods that charge a premium and towards budget-friendly foods, with the bean trend appealing to that. “I’m all for it,” Beckett enthuses. A teacher of culinary nutrition, her students note that social media is a font of easy inspiration when cooking feels overwhelming. So, seeing a trend that capitalises on the “easy factor” while also introducing a healthier ingredient is a win.



“This trend is about adding the beans to something people already want to eat. It’s not saying to get rid of anything, and it’s not saying beans are the silver bullet. It’s saying these kinds of dishes – that you already like – will be better for you if you do them with beans. There’s not much of a downside to that,” she says. Related Article Seven inexpensive sources of fibre to add to your grocery list “I like to say ‘use the delicious to access the nutritious’,” she adds, with a laugh, “and I think this trend is exactly that. If you just say ‘eat more beans’, how boring! But if you say: ‘Did you know you can add some beans to this satay-style dish?’ – well that’s a really great way in. It’s meeting people where they are.” The short answer is, yes, this trend helps with health goals, as long as we’re mindful about what else we’re adding to the sauces. And while the beans are a win on the fibre front, Beckett recommends checking salt content or rinsing your tinned beans first, if necessary. Jessica Brook’s creamy braised beans with lamb meatballs. James Moffatt



Does it taste any good? If you like creamy sauces, yes, these recipes win. You can’t really go wrong with a creamy sauce served over tender beans. “When we’re talking about flavours like satay and chilli oil, it’s sort of a twist on the condiments we add to silken tofu as a snack,” says Lisa Liu, creator of Saucy Wench condiments, whose satay sauce and chilli oil have won gold at Melbourne Royal and Sydney Royal shows respectively. “Tinned beans have that same kind of effect. That kind of rich, beany flavour with a soft texture that goes very well with these two things. So it makes sense and definitely makes beans more approachable,” Liu says. The real trick is to find the beans you like because there are plenty of varieties with different flavours and textures to play around with. Right now, though, it’s butter beans and white cannellini beans that are lending their milder flavour to this trend.



No-cook creamy satay-style butter beans Jane de Graaff Jane de Graaff’s no-cook creamy satay-style butter beans You can swap out the butter beans in this recipe for any cooked or tinned beans of your choice, and while this is a no-cook recipe, you can also warm the sauce gently in a pan for a comforting twist, just don’t reduce the sauce too much. Perfect with a soft-boiled egg on the side and some hot buttered sourdough, but also an ideal bowl on its own. INGREDIENTS



1 x 400g tin of butter beans + 2 tbsp reserved bean brine

2 tbsp crunchy peanut butter

½ tbsp chilli crisp oil

½ tsp tamari

2 spring onions, white and green parts, finely sliced

pinch of brown sugar (optional)

2 tbsp coconut cream, divided

juice of 1 lime Toppings ½ tbsp toasted sesame seeds

sprigs of fresh coriander

½ a small red chilli, finely sliced (remove the seeds for a milder result)

1 x soft-boiled egg

Hot buttered sourdough, to serve METHOD Reserve 2 tbsp of the bean brine and then drain the beans and rinse them. Soft boil and peel your egg and set aside. Toast and butter your sourdough. In a bowl, mix together the peanut butter, chilli crisp oil, tamari, sliced spring onion, brown sugar (if using), ½ the coconut cream and ½ the lime juice to make a sauce. Thin with a little bean brine if necessary for a loose consistency. Add the drained and rinsed beans to the sauce and toss through to coat. Spoon the beans into a dish, drizzle with the remaining coconut cream and lime juice, and top with toasted sesame seeds, fresh coriander, and chopped fresh chilli. Serve with a side of hot buttered sourdough toast and a soft-boiled egg.

World.title: Two children die, six injured in school pick-up tragedy near Bacchus Marsh
World.content:
A 34-year-old mother had just picked up children from school when her 4WD ran off the road and rolled at Melbourne’s western fringe on Tuesday afternoon, leaving two children dead and six people injured. A car containing seven children was travelling west on Nerowie Road in Parwan before it “inexplicably” rolled onto a nature strip about 4.28pm on Tuesday, police said. Major Collision Investigation Unit detectives are investigating a fatal single-vehicle rollover in Parwan which occurred on Tuesday afternoon. Nine News A seven-year-old girl died at the scene. An 11-year-old boy died overnight in hospital, police said early on Wednesday. The scale of the crash required a huge response from emergency services. Two air ambulances and nine paramedic crews were dispatched to the area, transporting seven people to hospital.



Three boys were taken to the Royal Children’s Hospital, two of them in the air ambulances with upper- and lower-body injuries, with one of the two in a critical condition. The third boy was taken in an ambulance with upper-body injuries in a stable condition. The scene of the fatal crash near the intersection of Parwan-Exford Road and Exford Road. Eddie Jim A further three children – a female toddler with minor injuries, and a teenage boy and primary school-aged boy with upper-body injuries – were taken to Sunshine Hospital, all in a stable condition. On Wednesday morning, the children’s hospital said the patients being treated there were stable. The driver was taken by ambulance to the Royal Melbourne Hospital in a stable condition. That hospital has been contacted for comment.



Loading On Wednesday morning, shattered windscreen glass remained on the roadside. A single black sneaker, belonging to a child, lay nearby. Local farmer John Bibby, whose fence was cut by responders to try to reach the children, said the nearby road was in good condition compared with other parts in the area. “It’s just horrible – especially when kids are involved,” he said. The scene on Wednesday morning. Eddie Jim



Detective Sergeant Tony Gentile said police were still investigating the circumstances of the crash. “From my understanding, the scene was quite hectic, people everywhere. Witnesses who witnessed it, they stopped and rendered assistance,” he said. “Obviously, with seven children, they were distressed, and they were cared for by paramedics, members of the public and police.” “This is just a really sad set of circumstances. Really very sad.”



Police said it was not apparent that drugs or alcohol were involved and have urged anyone who witnessed the crash or has dashcam footage to contact police. Intensive paramedic crews and advanced life support crews were at the scene. Nine News In May 2023, 13 children were taken to hospital after a truck hit a school bus carrying 45 primary school students on the same road. Seven children were left with serious injuries, including a 10-year-old who lost her arm. Be the first to know when major news happens.

World.title: ‘Where’s Karl?’ Podcast falls silent as advertising deal ends
World.content:
BusinessCompaniesMedia & marketing ‘Where’s Karl?’ Podcast falls silent as advertising deal ends Calum Jaspan Updated September 9, 2026 — 10:23am ,first published September 8, 2026 — 6:52pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Karl Stefanovic’s independent podcast has not uploaded new content in more than two weeks, raising questions about the program’s future as his main advertiser ended its contract with the former Today host. The Karl Stefanovic Show has not posted new podcast episodes or social media content across all social channels since August 24, leaving Stefanovic’s subscribers asking whether the former TV star will be returning at all. Karl Stefanovic’s independent podcast has not uploaded any new content in more than two weeks. YouTube The former TV host was sacked by Nine after he interviewed British far-right figure Tommy Robinson just over two months ago. After he was forced from his multimillion-dollar contract, Stefanovic said he was finally “free” and “truly independent”, allowing him to properly pursue his podcast. Country clothing brand Ringers Western confirmed its sponsorship deal with the independent show has ended, with no plans to renew the deal, when approached by this masthead over the show’s inactivity. A spokesperson from the brand said the deal was planned to end in September.



Stefanovic’s video content heavily promoted Ringers Western, with Stefanovic often appearing in videos in its clothing, including during an interview with One Nation leader Pauline Hanson in August. Related Article Opinion

On Background Billionaire brings former Gold Walkley winner back from the cold Calum Jaspan Media Writer The Karl Stefanovic Show has not posted any content since its last episode was published, featuring an interview with men’s surgeon Dr Buck Parker, discussing whether humans can de-age through “reprogramming ageing cells”, peptides and wellness treatments. In the week prior, Stefanovic uploaded five full episodes and often uploaded episodes several times per week to his YouTube channel, including almost daily posts on his Instagram and TikTok pages. Both Stefanovic and his business partner and producer Keshnee Kemp did not respond to requests for comment when asked to explain the absence on Tuesday afternoon. Kemp did also not respond to questions regarding the show’s ongoing funding after its partnership with Ringers Western came to an end.



Stefanovic posted a video on his personal Instagram page on August 29 showing him attending Griffith’s Taste of Italy Festival. Related Article Radio Stefanovic takes aim at TV’s ‘beige’ hosts after Nine departure Brand partnerships and sponsorships are key to Stefanovic’s funding model, which also relies on ad revenue from different social media platforms, largely YouTube. A company linked to Kemp’s digital marketing company August One owns 45 per cent of Stefanovic’s new venture, while Stefanovic owns 45 per cent himself. The final 10 per cent is owned by celebrity accountant Anthony Bell, as reported by the Financial Review in June. Some recent episodes published in August appeared without a brand partner, with Ringers Western the only partner listed on most videos on Stefanovic’s YouTube page. Some interviews were also sponsored by payroll platform Tanda. Stefanovic conducted the interview with Hanson in Mount Isa wearing Ringers Western clothing, while the One Nation leader appeared in a custom orange S Kidman hat, the clothing brand owned by party donor Gina Rinehart.



Pauline Hanson wearing what appears to be a custom-made hat made by Gina Rinehart’s Kidman Clothing company. A wellness supplement company Revive5 publicly backed Stefanovic in June after his sacking, but has not appeared on any recent episodes. Related Article Opinion

On Background Karl Stefanovic’s love affair with the British far right blooms Kishor Napier-Raman Senior Business Writer Stefanovic launched the new podcast at the start of this year, agreeing to a deal with Nine which allowed him to launch his own show while continuing to present the Today program. It quickly became clear that the podcast, pitched as an unscripted and uncensored platform for him to uncover “bloody good stories”, was instead an attempt to capture the growing chunk of Australians moving toward far-right, populist politics alongside the rise of One Nation in the polls.



One Nation politicians including Hanson and Barnaby Joyce became regular fixtures, as did Family First senator Gerard Rennick, who is a regular guest alongside conspiracy theorists and foreign far-right figures such as British MP Rupert Lowe. Related Article Updated

Media & marketing Today show host Karl Stefanovic to leave Nine after Tommy Robinson podcast fallout Stefanovic’s followers have begun leaving comments on his various social media accounts, asking if the show will be returning at all. “Karl we miss you mate hope you’re ok!“; “wheres karl??“; “Where’s the podcast gone?!” commenters wrote on his social media pages. Stefanovic’s interview with Robinson, who is a fascist and convicted criminal, was the final straw for Nine, despite Stefanovic removing the interview shortly after it was uploaded.



“Here’s what I believe in: the public deserve to hear perspectives,” Stefanovic said in a statement published online shortly after he was dismissed by Nine. “On my show, I have spoken to people who have different perspectives; I know that winds some people up. Sometimes I agree with everything a guest says, sometimes I don’t. But importantly, you get to make up your own mind.” During the interview, Stefanovic took a deferential tone with Robinson, at one point telling him “god, I love ya”. World.title: Hospitality businesses paying too many fees and struggling with red tape, review finds
World.content:
A government review into the hospitality sector has found some businesses are paying too many fees and decisions around licensing are murky and take too long.

The review was launched last year and looked how at restaurants, bars, clubs (like an RSA or sports club), cafés, food stalls at markets, food trucks, catering businesses and hotels interact with regulators like councils.

It found a number of inefficiencies, including:

Businesses give the same information multiple times, often to the same regulator.

Some decisions take too long, leaving businesses uncertain about timeframes

Alcohol licensing and renewal processes can be inefficient, disproportionate to risk, and ineffective in some cases

Fees for licensing and registration are too high for some hospitality businesses, not always transparent, and are not covering the costs for regulators

Food safety requirements are not always effective, efficient, or proportionate to risk

Food safety checks and compliance practices may not be effective, efficient, nor proportionate

Disproportionate regulatory barriers affect the provision of transport services

Building consent and planning requirements can create unnecessary costs and delays for temporary structures like marquees.

In total, the review contains 24 recommendations, including moving some businesses to a "lower-risk" category, scrapping annual or bi-annual renewals and introducing a nationally standardised application form, appointing a new steward for the alcohol regulatory system, and reviewing building consent exemption conditions for temporary marquees.

It also recommends removing the current alcohol licence types and replacing them with one "coherent risk framework", as well as repealing the Hotel Association of New Zealand Act 1969.

Minister for Tourism and Hospitality Louise Upston said the sector played a "vital role" in the economy, providing jobs all over the country.

"The hospitality sector is a $21.4 billion industry, employing more than 193,000 people across the country. We're backing Kiwi businesses and supporting a stronger visitor economy.

Regulation Minister David Seymour and Minister for Tourism and Hospitality Louise Upston announce the review in 2025. RNZ / Russell Palmer

"As several of the recommendations highlight, hospitality issues often span multiple portfolios and agencies. That is why I will develop a Hospitality Action Plan to provide a coordinated framework for priority hospitality initiatives across government," she said.

Regulation Minister David Seymour said everybody had a favourite café, bar or restaurant they wished was still open.

"The sector was hit hard by Covid. Red tape and dumb rules made it hard for the sector to bounce back.

"The rules and regulations are imposed by so many departments that they're difficult to fix. That's why we set up a ministry with a mandate for cutting red tape; to fix the problems no one else can," he said.

World.title: Victim of Blockhouse Bay stabbing named as Star Fetu Peretiso Sami
World.content:
The man who was fatally stabbed on an Auckland street in broad daylight can now be named for the first time.

Police say Star Fetu Peretiso Sami was on Holbrook Street in Blockhouse Bay on 22 August when there was what police described as a "violent altercation" and he was stabbed.

He got into a car and was driven a short distance to a bus stop where an ambulance was called but died the following day in hospital.

Police went to the Coroner and applied for Sami's name and gang affiliation to be suppressed.

That application was supported and continued by Sami's family who sought privacy after receiving abuse on social media.

Coroner Rachael Schmidt-McCleave, acting as the national duty coroner, granted an interim non-publication order prohibiting publication of the man's identity as well as the gang they were associated with.

Media were not informed of the application, which was granted on 25 August in chambers on the papers, or given an opportunity to oppose the non-publication order.

However, after allowing various media organisations including RNZ to respond, Coroner Janet Anderson found the case did not meet the threshold to continue suppression.

The Coroner heard an impassioned plea from Sami's family for the suppression orders to continue. They pointed to receiving abuse on social media platforms and stressed that Sami was much more than a gang member.

"No one should receive unpleasant or offensive messages through social media," Coroner Anderson said in her decision released on Wednesday.

"However, generally speaking it has been recognised that, 'the court is not the arbiter of social media standards'."

Dr Saleimoa Bill Sami, an uncle of Star Sami, issued a response to the Coroner following her decision to lift the suppression order.

"As the restrictions now come to an end, our hope is simply that those who choose to report on Star do so with accuracy, fairness, balance and appropriate consideration for those experiencing trauma and grief.

"We also hope that reporting does not create an implication that Star's death was gang-motivated when police have expressly advised that there is presently no evidence of that."

The family said Star Sami was much more than the circumstances of his death.

"He was our son, brother, grandson, nephew, cousin, father and friend. We will continue to uphold his mana and awhi the whānau he has left behind as best we can."

Sami was also a former student of Kelston Boys' High School and part of its First XV.

World.title: Donald Trump claims he was pulled from Ground Zero after 9/11 attack. But was he?
World.content:
President Donald Trump has for years told false or unproven stories about what he supposedly saw and did on 9/11 and soon after. As the 25th anniversary of the terror attack approaches, Trump told another story at the White House on Tuesday - in which he claimed to have been carried away by firefighters amid fears of an imminent building collapse at some point after the attack.

It's possible there are elements of truth in Trump's latest story, versions of which he has told before, but he hasn't provided any evidence for it. And some parts of his Tuesday account - which he delivered at an event honoring 9/11 first responders - are misleading at best. He was miles away from the World Trade Center on 9/11 and was not whisked out of any building near Ground Zero that day.

Asked for evidence for Trump's story or more details about what supposedly happened, the White House did not provide any.

The White House said in an unsigned Tuesday email, "He was a private citizen at the time, not everything he did was documented." Later in the day, spokesperson Davis Ingle pivoted to an attack on the media.

"President Trump spent the morning paying tribute to the heroic first responders who laid down their lives in service to others in the September 11th attacks and honoring their incredible families. The President was relaying his experience of a city reeling immediately after and in the days and weeks after the horrific attacks - and the fact that the failing legacy media is using this to try to attack him is a disgrace and yet another reason why Americans' trust in the media is at an all-time low," Ingle said.

Here's a look at what Trump said Tuesday and what the facts are.

What Trump said

Breaking down Trump's story

Trump wasn't close to the World Trade Center during the attack or later that day

Trump didn't specify when the firemen supposedly helped him, but by beginning the story by saying he went to Ground Zero "right after this happened," he at the least left open the impression that he was whisked to safety on the day of the attack. But that couldn't have happened because he was miles away, at Trump Tower in Midtown Manhattan, when the attack occurred. A former Trump Organization executive told Politico in 2016 that Trump did not do much out of the ordinary that day.

In a 2016 version of the story, Trump claimed the moment the firemen helped him happened "a couple of days" after the attack.

There's no public evidence Trump was in the 'US Steel building' soon after the attacks

With his comments about how he feared the US Steel building was "coming down on top of us" and about how a firefighter said "gotta get out of here," Trump left open the impression that he was inside an unstable building. But there is no public evidence he was actually in the building he was referring to (better known as One Liberty Plaza in 2001 and still today) in the days after the attacks. Two days after the attack, he was interviewed outdoors in the general vicinity of Ground Zero.

In Trump's 2016 telling of the story, he made clear he wasn't inside when the firemen supposedly lifted and moved him; he said the building that appeared on the verge of collapse was "not so far from us."

A man standing in the rubble, calling out asking if anyone needs help, after the collapse of the first World Trade Center Tower in New York City. AFP / Doug Kanter

There was indeed unfounded panic about One Liberty Plaza, though no proof Trump was swept up in it

In the days after the attack, there were fears that One Liberty Plaza would collapse even as city building officials said it was structurally sound; CNN reported that rescue workers and journalists were evacuated from the building on September 12, 2001, and The Washington Post reported that rescue workers were rushed away again on September 14, 2001.

Trump alluded to a similar situation when he was interviewed on September 13, 2001, telling NBC of workers at Ground Zero: "Every few minutes, a whistle would go off and everybody would just run, because you have all the buildings around it, which are in such a weakened state that people just don't know. And so they just have to take off, and then they come back, and they're working under 50-story buildings that you don't know if they're going to fall down. So it's a terrible thing for the workers and it's a terrible thing for the world, really."

It is possible Trump was personally swept up in one of these moments of panic, too. But there's no proof of that, and he didn't tell NBC that he was talking about himself running.

Donald Trump AFP / JIM WATSON

There's no public evidence Trump had a crew helping with the rescue effort

This time, Trump didn't explicitly say that he or his workers helped to clear rubble or otherwise assisted with rescue and recovery at Ground Zero. But he has made such explicit claims in the past, and this time he immediately thanked "my people" after mentioning the work of rescue and recovery crews. So it's worth noting that he has never presented evidence for his claims that he worked at Ground Zero or organized a group that worked at the site, let alone the 100-strong group of workers he has previously claimed.

"I spent many months there myself, and I never witnessed him," Richard Alles, a retired New York Fire Department official who was a battalion chief on 9/11 and who attended a Trump White House event in 2019, told The New York Times in 2019. Alles told PolitiFact in 2019 that if Trump had sent a crew of 100 workers, "there would be a record of it. Everybody worked under direct supervision of the police and fire department and the joint commander for emergency services."

The Associated Press reported in 2016, "News accounts from days just after 9/11 include references to Trump giving high-fives to police officers and volunteers on their way to the World Trade Center site."

No basis to say One Liberty Plaza 'still creaks'

Trump said, "The truth is it creaked a lot, it creaked. It still creaks." There is no basis for this claim. The One Liberty Plaza office building reopened in October 2001, less than two months after 9/11, and functions normally today.

World.title: Government acknowledges some pork labels may be misleading, refuses law change
World.content:
The Government is refusing to make any law changes surrounding pork branding but acknowledges some labels may be misleading.

This follows the pork industry calling for 'country of origin' information to be clearer as some shoppers think they are buying bacon or ham from New Zealand pigs - but it's not.

NZPork's chief executive said some supermarkets' pork products had extremely small labelling hidden on the back saying where the pig was bred overseas - but it's marketed as being local.

Brent Kleiss said it's infurating and he's not happy that no changes were being made.

He says a parliament committee recommended the government look at clearer labelling of pork products three years ago and has had no response since then.

However in a statement the Minister of Commerce and Consumer Affairs said the regulations ensured that information about the origin of regulated products - such as pork - was available to consumers in a way that was clear and informative.

Minister of Commerce and Consumer Affairs Cameron Brewer. VNP / Phil Smith

Cameron Brewer said the complaint upheld by the parliament committee related to how certain pork products were branded, rather than the origin information they were required to disclose.

"Although it might be possible for an imported meat product that complies with the regulations to be branded in a way that misleads consumers about the product's origin, I am not aware of evidence that this is occurring on a scale that would justify further regulatory change."

Brewer added that his Fair Trading Amendment Bill proposed to increase penalties for any misleading conduct that could affect consumers.

"I acknowledge your concern that some branding practices may give consumers a misleading impression about whether pork was raised in New Zealand."

He suggested PorkNZ complain to the Commerce Commission if it had issues with the way any pork products were labelled.

But Kleiss said farmers were not impressed - and they would be making a big noise about it. "Our fear is that the minister may have been mislead or made a desision to get it off his plate rather than actually tackle the issue head on."

Brent Kleiss, chief executive of NZ Pork. Supplied

He said an issue was animal welfare - some countries were breeding and killing pigs unethically and local consumers didn't realise how badly the pig had been treated before being made into bacon.

He was also frustrated with some supermarkets - saying he visited a Pak'nSave in Christchurch last week that didn't have any New Zealand bred and processed pork products - such as ham and bacon - at all.

In response, Foodstuffs said it supported customers having clear and accurate information about the products they bought, including country-of-origin information, in line with the labelling requirements.

In a statement it said availability of New Zealand pork could vary between stores depending on customer demand, supplier availability and the range of products stocked.

"When sourcing pork and other meat products, we consider a range of factors including food safety, quality, animal welfare, supply reliability and value for customers."

World.title: Children killed in Rotorua home were 11 months and 3 years old, police say
World.content:
The children involved in an alleged triple homicide in Rotorua were just 3 and 11 months old.

The investigation into the deaths of three people, the two children and a woman, at a home in Glenholme was continuing on Wednesday, Bay of Plenty acting district commander inspector Logan Marsh said.

"We can now release the age of the two deceased young children. They were an 11-month-old and a three-year-old.

"Police are continuing to support the family following this traumatic incident."

Emergency services arrived at the home on High Street in Glenholme shortly before 10.30pm on Monday, where they found the bodies of two young children along with a critically injured woman who died at the scene.

Police began a homicide investigation and a man in his early 20s appeared in the Rotorua District Court on Tuesday, charged with assaulting a person in a family relationship.

The man and the victims were granted interim name suppression and he was remanded in custody until next month.

Marsh said police and other specialist teams remain at the scene on High Street - with a forensic examination ongoing.

"Our team are working tirelessly and meticulously through a complex scene, so we can provide answers for those impacted.

"An investigation of this nature will take some time and we thank the community for their patience.

"Staff will continue to conduct additional reassurance patrols in the Glenholme area and wider community over the coming days."

Police officers making inquiries into a serious incident in High St, Rotorua, 8 September 2026. NZME

On Wednesday morning, Rotorua mayor Tania Tapsell said the community was devastated by the news.

"We're really devastated about the triple homicide that's occurred here in Rotorua and especially in the Glenholme neighbourhood. Look, this is a very … nice families that live there for multiple generations, quite a lot of elderly people.

"This is a wonderful neighbourhood that we are just shaken to our core that this has happened in Rotorua and there continues to be a police presence as they complete their investigations.

"Unfortunately, we do know that there are two very young children involved in this incident, so our thoughts are with the victims and all those impacted."

Rotorua police at the scene of the triple homicide on High Street in Glenholme. RNZ / Rachel Moore

Tapsell said her message to the community was to stay strong, look after one another and report things to police if they had concerns.

"We need to support each other, not only through this incident but also as we continue to deal with increased uncertainty."

A 79-year-old man who had lived on the street his whole life said he was in shock since learning what had happened.

The people living in the house seemed to have recently moved in, he said, and he had seen new children around the street.

World.title: Labour promises to set up AI regulator, copyright rules if elected
World.content:
Labour is promising to set up an AI office, an online safety regulator, copyright rules that ensure creators are paid for their work, and impose rules on data centres.

The regulator would have a wider mandate than overseeing a social media ban for under-16s, and the public service would be given "clear expectations" around AI, human oversight, accountability, privacy and consumer and employment protections.

The party says it would also work with small and large businesses, community organisations, iwi, educators, and unions on how to safely use AI and ensure productivity gains are passed through to wages and conditions.

Leader Chris Hipkins and Technology and Innovation spokesperson Reuben Davidson announced the policy at the Victoria University of Wellington's tech hub, across from the capital's railway station, on Wednesday morning.

"Used well, AI has huge benefits. It can cut hospital paperwork so doctors and nurses have more time with patients. Workers and small businesses can be more productive. Certain services can be delivered more efficiently," Hipkins said.

"But we cannot leave it to big international tech companies to decide how it shapes our future."

Davidson said Labour would make sure New Zealand set AI rules on its own terms.

"That means protecting peoples' rights, safety and privacy, creative work, and ensuring that there is always human accountability."

National's social media ban has already proposed an online safety regulator, but Labour's policy said its mandate would be widened to help advise the government on emerging issues and help "seize the opportunities from AI while managing the risks".

"We could look to establish it as an independent regulator, outside of DIA, given the significance of the issues involved," the party's policy document said.

The separate Office of AI would be established within the Department of Prime Minister and Cabinet using existing resources, and would have responsibility for coordinating AI policy across government and developing standards, a long-term plan for the workforce.

A senior minister would also have responsibility for AI, with a whole-of-government work programme to be published "so New Zealanders can see what action is being taken".

World.content:
Police are seeking the public's help to find a missing 12-year-old girl in Auckland.

Pearly was last seen on West Harbour Drive in West Auckland's West Harbour at about 12.15am early Wednesday morning.

World.title: $600 million Southland wind farm officially opens
World.content:
The South Island's largest wind farm has officially opened with the ability to generate enough electricity to power 96,000 homes.

The Kaiwera Downs Wind Farm near Gore cost just over $600 million in total and was completed over two stages.

The $486m second stage was given a green light in 2024 after Mercury signed an agreement to support Tiwai smelter.

It added 36 additional turbines, bringing the total number to 46.

The second stage increased its annual generation from 146GWh to 675GWh - the equivalent of powering 21,000 homes to 96,000 homes based on an average home using 7000kWh a year.

Mercury chief executive Stew Hamilton said it was an important renewable energy project for the country.

RNZ / Tess Brunton

"New Zealand needs an energy system that is affordable, reliable and resilient. The best way to achieve that is to keep building renewable generation at scale," he said.

Mercury estimated work on stage two added $100m to the local and regional economy, saying stage two was built on time and on budget.

The Kaiwera Downs Wind Farm was not expected to hold onto the title as the South Island's largest wind farm with Contact Energy gaining approval for its 55 turbine Slopedown wind farm in eastern Southland.

Mercury was also preparing to expand its Mahinerangi Wind Farm in Otago with a $506m investment into stage two, known as Puke Kapo Hau, after it received fast track approval this year.

That would include 40 new turbines, which would generate enough energy to power the equivalent of 76,000 homes.

RNZ / Tess Brunton

Mercury said the decision to approve the expansion was supported by a power purchase option agreement with the developer of a large-scale data centre in Southland, Datagrid.

Over the past 12 months, Hamilton said Mercury had also started generating electricity from its Kaiwaikawe Wind Farm in Northland and Ngā Tamariki Geothermal Station expansion project near Taupō.

World.title: Returning Rams superstar to miss MCG NFL clash with 49ers
World.content:
Aaron Donald will not play in the Los Angeles Rams' season opener against the 49ers at the MCG, delaying the three-time defensive player of the year's return to the field after ending his retirement last month.

"I think he'll be ready to go sooner rather than later. But we're making a decision that we think is best for him and for our team," coach Sean McVay said.

The 35-year-old Donald rejoined the Rams in August after two seasons away from the team, and the eight-time-first team All-Pro has been working his way back into game shape.

But with a 16-hour flight on deck ahead of the game at 10:35am on Friday, McVay decided the prudent choice was to keep Donald at home and allow him to continue his preparations.

Everything you need to know about NFL Melbourne The San Francisco 49ers are taking on the Los Angeles Rams at the MCG, the first NFL regular-season game to be held in Australia. Here's everything you need to know.

"He's as great a competitor as there is," McVay said.

"Wants to be out there. Wants to influence and affect positive change for us. But I think he also understands there's a necessary ramp up."

The Rams are flying in just one day before the season opener in Melbourne, while the 49ers have been in Australia for the past week.

Donald was earlier coy on his playing status after a scheduled day off from practice to focus on his cardio, saying he has been pleased with how his body is responding to his return to football.

"I'm feeling good, knocking the rust off," Donald said.

"I thought I'd be a lot more rusty than I was, but taking it day by day."

The Rams have spent the previous seasons developing their defence for a future without Donald, including drafting Kobie Turner and Braden Fiske, signing Poona Ford in free agency, and trading for reigning defensive player of the year Myles Garrett.

McVay said his trust in that group to perform at a high level factored into the call to not rush Donald back onto the field immediately.

"Every single game is so important. We want him out there. But I do think what's great for our group is (I) feel great about the guys that are going to be playing in Australia," McVay said.

"Any good defensive line I've been a part of, there's a rotation where you got to have five, six guys that play and play meaningful snaps."

World.title: Sabalenka stays alive at US Open by telling herself 'the match is over'
World.content:
World number one Aryna Sabalenka has survived her toughest test of the tournament to beat Wimbledon champion Linda ​Noskova 7-6(7/1), 3-6, 7-6(10/7) and reach the US Open semifinals for a sixth consecutive year.

Two-time defending champion Sabalenka had not dropped a set before facing the Czech sixth seed, who fired ​18 aces and saved ‌seven of nine break points but faltered when leading by a break at 2-4 in the final set.

Sabalenka, chasing a third straight title at Flushing Meadows, next plays the winner of ‌an all-American clash between Jessica Pegula and Emma Navarro.

"What a battle. What ⁠an incredible player she is. I'm speechless right now because ‌I was pushing myself to ​the limit this match," ‌said Sabalenka, who has now won 21 of her past 22 matches at the year-end grand slam.

"In the third set I honestly thought, 'That's it, the match is over.' Probably that's what helped me to kind of feel loose and just go after my shots. Super happy to get this win."

By reaching the final four for a sixth straight time, Sabalenka matched the 2011-2016 run of Serena Williams, during which she won three of her six US Open crowns.

The Belarusian broke in the second game, whipping a forehand into the corner that Noskova did not even attempt to chase down, but the Czech broke back with a pair of powerful groundstrokes from the baseline in ​the ‌ninth.

Sabalenka, who reached a record 21 consecutive tiebreak wins at the slams earlier this year, was completely in her element in the opening-set breaker, ⁠where she sprinted through the first ‌six points.

But her firepower deserted ‌her in the second set and she struggled to contain Noskova's serve before handing the ‌Czech a 4-2 lead with a double fault.

After levelling the contest at one set all, Noskova set about pressing home her ‌advantage.

Sabalenka ​screamed in frustration when ⁠a pair of double faults midway through the third set helped her opponent secure another break.

Noskova seemed to be heading for an upset win before Sabalenka recovered her poise to level the contest in the ⁠eighth game.

And the Belarusian was right at home again in the decisive tiebreak, clinching it with an ace ‌before giving ‌credit to the fans for helping to propel her to ​the win.

The ABC of SPORT Sports content to make you think... or allow you not to. A newsletter delivered each Saturday.

World.title: Schumacher comparisons made as Antonelli continues historic F1 season
World.content:
There were plenty of tributes to the great Michael Schumacher in Monza last weekend.

Ferrari ran special liveries to honour the seven-time world champion.

Drivers Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton wore one-off racing suits with Schumacher's logo.

Meanwhile, former Ferrari driver Sebastian Vettel drove around the famous Monza circuit in Schumacher's 2002 world championship-winning car.

But perhaps the best tribute to Schumacher last Sunday was the performance by Mercedes gun Kimi Antonelli.

In a season of magical moments for the Formula 1 championship leader, Sunday's Italian Grand Prix victory was the stand-out performance.

At the start of the race, Antonelli lined up 19th on the grid due to a grid penalty and looked certain to have what was a 59-point lead in the championship reduced.

By the end of the race, he was standing on the top step of the podium, hoisting the winner's trophy as the first Italian to win the race in 60 years, and extending his gap to teammate George Russell in the drivers' championship to 66 points.

It was a monumental win, and one that has the 20-year-old in pole position to become the youngest F1 champion in history.

Kimi Antonelli was paraded by his fellow Italians after winning his home grand prix at Monza. (Getty Images: NurPhoto/Andrea Diodato)

But what made Antonelli's win so impressive was the manner in which he did it.

He made 26 overtakes during the race, first taking the lead on lap 18 of 53, then chasing again when he took a pit stop with 24 laps remaining.

He passed rivals with precision, race craft and sheer pace, and it drew comparisons to Schumacher from a man who once went wheel-to-wheel with the legend.

Juan Pablo Montoya, winner of seven F1 grands prix which all came during Schumacher's dominant years with Ferrari, says Antonelli is so quick that rivals are not bothering to battle him on track.

Juan Pablo Montoya (left) battled Michael Schumacher (right) for many years in F1. (Getty Images: Clive Rose)

Speaking on F1 TV's post-race program after Antonelli's win in Monza, Montoya specifically pointed out the difference between how Red Bull's Max Verstappen, who finished third, battled hard against Russell for the lead of the race but put up less of a fight with Antonelli.

"Something that was incredible was how easy he was passing people," Montoya said.

"It's a little bit [like] when I raced with Michael Schumacher. When Michael was coming through, people would get out of the way for Michael.

"And people are doing that [now]. They know Antonelli is going to get you, they're not even bother about fighting with him.

"He [Verstappen] ran Russell forever. When Kimi came it was completely different … and it was the right thing to do."

There are nine or 10 grand prix weekends left this season, depending on whether F1 will be able to race in the Middle East at the end of the year.

Antonelli's lead in the drivers' championship is a whopping 66 points, almost double the lead Oscar Piastri had over Lando Norris (37 points) with nine race weekends left in 2025.

Piastri would suffer a form slump at the end of 2025, finishing 13 points behind Norris, and 11 points behind Verstappen who was a staggering 104 points adrift of the Australian with nine weekends remaining.

Kiwi to continue racing for Red Bull

New Zealand driver Liam Lawson will race for Red Bull for a third consecutive weekend while Frenchman Isack Hadjar continues to recover from a fractured wrist.

Lawson, who was promoted to Red Bull from Racing Bull for the first two weekends of 2025 before being demoted back, will be Max Verstappen's teammate in Madrid for this weekend's Spanish Grand Prix.

Hadjar has missed the previous two races in the Netherlands and Italy after suffering a wrist injury during F1's mid-year break.

Lawson finished seventh in the Netherlands, and 14th in Italy after starting from the pit lane.

"After racing for the team in Zandvoort and Monza, Liam will continue to drive alongside Max at this week's Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid," a statement from Red Bull read.

"The decision has been taken as Isack's recovery continues to progress positively. While he is not yet ready to return to the cockpit, he will be in Madrid supporting the team."

Yuki Tsunoda, who replaced Lawson in 2025, will again fill the Kiwi's seat at Racing Bulls.

ABC Sport will have a live blog of the Formula 1 Spanish Grand Prix from 9pm AEST on Sunday, September 13.

World.title: Football league says Swans scandal comments 'clearly insensitive'
World.content:
A country football league has distanced itself from "insensitive" and "unacceptable" comments made at a recent awards event at which the master of ceremonies joked about the Sydney Swans scandal.

But the league also said that, "in his defence", the man was attempting "to show how certain events can galvanise a team's resolve".

In video posted online, the MC at the Whyalla Football League's event made light-hearted reference to the Swans scandal, citing it in the context of local club South Whyalla's upcoming match.

The man, Jock Sleep, suggested the local club draw inspiration from Sydney's win over Brisbane in Saturday's AFL qualifying final, linking that performance to the scandal engulfing the Swans.

"My advice to the Souths' coach … [is] maybe we can manufacture a good old-fashioned scandal just to get that team going," the MC said.

"It worked for the Sydney Swans. I'm just talking a scandal — not a real big one."

Last week, Victoria Police detectives spoke with four Sydney Swans players as part of their sexual assault investigation linked to the club.

A still from the video shared online. (Facebook)

The man's remarks at the Whyalla awards night were strongly condemned by Australian Femicide Watch's Sherele Moody, who shared video on her social media pages and described the comments as "terrible".

"The crowd at the awards night laughed along with him. There was no attempt to shut down the conversation by the organisers," she wrote.

In a statement, Whyalla Football League president Keith Sichler said Mr Sleep was a "well-known local identity" and local football historian.

"His comments and joke were clearly insensitive and not indicative of current attitudes. In his defence, it was merely an attempt to show how certain events can galvanise a team's resolve with the intent of improving their performance. Nothing more," Mr Sichler said.

"Nonetheless, references of this nature are unacceptable and inconsistent with the inclusive and respectful environment we expect across our League.

"The WFL has spoken with him, and he understands the impact of his remarks and has expressed regret for any harm caused."

The ABC has reached out directly to Mr Sleep for comment.

Last week, the Swans said five players would remain stood down for the remainder of the season for breaching the club's behavioural standards in a post-AFL match hotel party in August, regardless of how an ongoing police investigation unfolded.

Victoria Police has interviewed four Sydney men as part of an investigation into sexual assault allegations during a post-AFL match party at East Melbourne's Pullman Hotel.

World.title: Crook elbows and big dreams propel unheralded Knights for finals
World.content:
Newcastle forward Francis Manuleleua might be less than two weeks off dislocating his right elbow but at the end of an interview he'll still shake your hand and shake it hard.

"Nah, let's go for it G," Manuleleua said when offered the chance to forgo a handshake, just in case.

"It's gotta be strong."

The 22-year-old's right arm bent in a way that right arms are not supposed to bend in the Knights loss to the Warriors a fortnight back.

Manuleleua suffered a dislocated elbow against New Zealand two weeks ago. (Getty Images: Hannah Peters )

It looked gruesome — Manuleleua was straight on the green whistle and phrases like "bony deformity" were used in analysis of the video.

But with Newcastle already without key men Dylan Lucas, Trey Mooney and Jacob Saifiti due to injury and suspension ahead of Friday's sudden-death semifinal against South Sydney and after being cleared of a fracture, Manuleleua will push to play.

He was named on Tuesday for what would be his NRL finals debut and is one of an unheralded mix of youngsters and journeymen in the Knights forwards who will be tasked with taking down the Rabbitohs.

In terms of star power it's a no-contest. Every player in the South Sydney starting pack has played either Test or Origin football except for Tallis Duncan, who might not have to wait long to join them.

Duncan pushing for maiden World Cup berth Australia are facing a shortage of backrowers for this year's Rugby League World Cup but South Sydney tyro Tallis Duncan could prove to be the answer.

Manuleleua has a mere 11 NRL matches to his credit and fellow second rower Jermaine McEwen is wrapping up his first full season as an every week player.

The baby of the side is starting prop Cody Hopwood, still just 20, although at 196cm and 105kgs that's a damn big baby.

He's great mates with eight-gamer Lachlan Crouch, who received his first Knights cap from Paul Harragon himself upon his NRL debut earlier this year.

Both the rookies played their juniors in Maitland, as did the more seasoned Thomas Cant and Pasami Saulo who both fit the image of the honest toiler.

Cant has played almost 40 NRL matches since his debut in 2023 and is yet to score a try but that pales compared to Saulo — he's about to finish his ninth season in the league without a single four-pointer to show for it.

Injuries have ripped through the Knights pack in recent weeks. (Getty Images: Scott Gardiner )

Newcastle will lean heavily on the experience of 300-gamer Tyson Frizell and the underrated Matt Croker at lock as they match it with a South Sydney pack that is both fully loaded and battle-hardened.

Cameron Murray, Junior Tatola, David Fifita and Keaon Koloamatangi all have 150 NRL games or more to their credit and all but Fifita have been through multiple finals campaigns.

Even Duncan, by far their least experienced starting forward, has made more first grade appearances than Manuleleua, Crouch, Hopwood and McEwen combined.

Given he's marking up on the reborn Fifita, Manuleleua might be facing the biggest task of all and certainly the hardest test of an NRL career that began just a few months ago. He can't wait for it.

"He's a big, powerful boy and there's a job to do. But I'm keen for the challenge," said Manuleleua.

"They've got a lot of strengths on their edge with Fifita, Latrell Mitchell and Jack Wighton and a great ball-player in Cody Walker, so it's a good challenge for us edges.

"But that's the kind of footy we want to play anyway. We want to go after that challenge, go after them and see what happens."

Despite making his NRL debut in Round 3, a steady start is leading to a big finish for Manuleleua.

It wasn't until Round 20 that he became a regular starter following Lucas going down with an ankle injury.

But with six line breaks, two tries, five try assists and 23 tackle busts in the six games since, Manuleleua has proven to be one of the finds of the season.

He's a big, explosive man who can do big, explosive things and has it in him to be a wrecking machine but he's also fresh enough that so much of this is still new.

The match against the Warriors, for example, was the first time the Papatoetoe junior got to play back in New Zealand and over 25 family members and countless friends packed out the stands to see him.

Manuleleua scored a try on his return to New Zealand last week. (Getty Images: Hannah Peters )

"It's pretty surreal. I still can't believe it. I didn't think I'd be playing finals footy this early in my career," said Manuleleua.

"It was gun, that game against the Warriors. They (my family) were loud as hell, Warriors had 25,000 fans but I could still hear my family and it was the first time I played an NRL game in front of them at home.

"It was bittersweet because we couldn't win the game but they were just happy I scored a try."

Manuleleua's clash with Fifita might be the most difficult job but it's not the biggest — that belongs to Hopwood, who will start at prop.

He did the same in the club's most recent clash with South Sydney in Round 19, when Hopwood and Crouch got in the mix with the Rabbitohs amid a torrid physical battle.

The two Maitland boys are popular members of the Knights squad given they have a special brand of front-row charm, as Manuleleua explains.

"They're intentionally funny. They'll do something weird but it'll be funny," said Manuleleua.

"When it comes to the game they look like monsters but they're kind at heart, they're good people."

Hopwood doesn't have time to think about what Manuleleua is talking about given he's about to play the biggest game of his life.

Hopwood will start in the front row for an NRL final at just 20 years of age. (Getty Images: Scott Gardiner )

"I have no idea what that means. I don't think I want to know either," said Hopwood.

"Whenever you're out and about people are wishing you luck for Friday night, the town's flying and we're all excited.

"I'm really confident, I'm in a good spot mentally and physically. Attack it front on, that's probably the best way to go. Just go hard and try to go for longer."

Hopwood was a highly rated junior, representing New South Wales Under 19s twice, but despite making his NRL debut in the final round of last season he never thought he'd play as much first grade in 2026 as he has.

"Not at all, but I've had some really good people around me that have helped with the transition," said Hopwood.

"I thought I might only play two or three games this year, so it's all come pretty quick.

"I'm feeling really supported and I don't want to let anyone down, I want to repay that faith."

Hopwood did not expect to play more than one or two NRL games this year. (Getty Images: Ayush Kumar )

Hopwood's done a fine job with it so far, starting seven of his 14 games this season, and seems the type who never learned to take a backward step.

Whether that will be enough against players like Koloamatangi and Murray remains to be seen but Hopwood isn't thinking about the odds stacked against him or his side.

Like any good Novocastrian, he has dreamed of making a difference for the Knights his whole life and was there as a 17-year old in the crowd for their last finals win three years ago.

Dom Young roaring down the sideline for a length-of-the-field try is a memory that will never leave him and now all he wants is to give Knights fans another moment that lasts forever.

"I remember thinking how much I'd love to be a part of something like that and I get to live it on Friday night," said Hopwood.

"How good is that?"

World.title: Popovic knocked back four-year Socceroos contract extension
World.content:
Socceroos coach Tony Popovic has revealed he turned down a four-year contract offer from Football Australia (FA) to take the team through to the 2030 World Cup.

Popovic instead signed a six-month extension during the World Cup to take the team through to the Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia, which begins in January.

"It was my choice to go until the Asian Cup. Although I was offered a four-year deal, I decided to go to the Asian Cup," Popovic told journalists on Tuesday.

"And I think that is something that I think is good.

"It gives the FA the opportunity if they want to go in a different decision they can, and I'm very comfortable with the decision that's been made."

FIFA accuses UEFA of 'smear campaign' Football's major governing bodies continue to fight over the failed plan by FIFA president Gianni Infantino to sell off the rights for the World Cup, with the global governing body accusing European body UEFA of a "smear campaign" against the president.

Popovic led the Socceroos to the round of 32 knockout stage of the World Cup in the United States, where the team lost to Egypt in a penalty shoot-out heartbreaker.

His side won its opening match against Türkiye, lost to the United States and drew with Paraguay before the fateful match against Egypt ended the Socceroos' dream run.

He led the youngest side at the World Cup of all 48 nations with an average of 25 years and 155 days.

Some of the Socceroos stars of the tournament have since signed transfer contracts worth up to $33 million, including Lucas Herrington (Hull City), Nestory Irankunda (Sporting Lisbon), Alessandro Circati (Benfica), Patrick Beach (Troyes) and Paul Okon-Engstler (Köln).

When asked directly whether he wanted to continue coaching the Socceroos, Popovic declined to give a direct answer, instead elaborating on his focus on fostering young talent.

"I love coaching the Socceroos," he said.

"When we qualified there was obviously 12 months before the World Cup.

"I ended up signing [his six-month contract] the last week before the first [World Cup] match, and we started this evolution of the team for 12 months without knowing whether I'd be there or not.

"I've never shied away from the expectation of results.

"But I've always had an eye on the future, and I think that was reflected in the squad we chose, the players we played and how much the team changed in 12 months."

Socceroos' World Cup story ends in heartbreak The Socceroos exited the World Cup in the cruellest possible manner, on penalties to Egypt. But the roots of the defeat could be found in the 120 minutes of play, which clearly showed where Australia must improve.

He said he was happy to make those decisions without the security of a long-term contract.

"I had no concerns about whether I signed or not and if I hadn't signed I would have been happy with what I had done and what I have left behind," he said.

"The same will be after the Asian Cup.

"I know the legacy that I will leave behind.

"And if it's someone else that takes it forward, that's fine; if it's me, great, if we agree to do this together," he said.

Popovic's decision to not take up the four-year contract offer gives him the option of pursuing a club contract now that he's been able to shop his talents through the World Cup window.

In his first press conference since returning from the World Cup, Popovic reflected on the decisions he made at the tournament and said there was little he would change.

He drew criticism from commentators for the goalkeeper substitution minutes before the penalty shoot-out against Egypt, which the Socceroos ultimately lost 4-2 when Harry Souttar and Lucas Herrington missed penalties.

Popovic introduced captain Matt Ryan, who hadn't played a minute in the World Cup, for Patrick Beach, who had been outstanding, conceding just three goals in four matches.

He said he would make the same decision again.

"There are many reasons why Matty came in," he said.

"Matty has experience; Matty saved two penalties for us in the qualifiers; Matty saved penalties for [his Spanish club team] Levante.

"Patrick Beach has not saved one penalty in any shoot-out, pretty much.

"In that moment it was very clear to me that Matty should come in.

"And like I said the next day I would have done the same thing."

The Socceroos play their first Asian Cup match against Singapore on January 9, where Popovic said he would continue his youth policy.

There will be a lot of young players probably at the Asian Cup, and that will be done without losing any expectation that I believe that we should be challenging for the Asian Cup," he said.

"Once you're there, you want to win it.

"I think that should happen for Australia."

The team has two friendlies later this month against the might of five-time world champions Brazil in Townsville and Brisbane.

Popovic said the team would have a chance to play another round of matches during the November friendly window, most likely in the Middle East.

World.title: Cricket Australia agrees to bring private investment to Big Bash
World.content:
Cricket Australia has agreed to bring private investment into the Big Bash League, starting with the sale of the Melbourne Renegades.

The Cricket Australia (CA) board made the announcement on Tuesday, with the sale process of the Renegades to be the first venture into bringing private investment into the franchise T20 league.

Cricket Australia green lights BBL privatisation The Big Bash League is set to look like it never has before as Cricket Australia prepares to welcome private ownership to the competition.

CA is hoping the Renegades will play under new ownership for the 2027/28 Big Bash season.

Depending on the success of the Renegades sale, CA said in a statement on Tuesday that it would "consider taking other clubs to market under a self-determination model that gives each State member the ability to assess the optimal pathway for its own club and community".

CA chair Mike Baird said the decision was a major moment for cricket in Australia.

"Beginning the sales process for the Renegades allows us to take the first step in a self-determination model for our members and represents a defining moment for the game," he said.

"Importantly, CA and its members will maintain control over the most significant aspects of Australian Cricket operations, including international scheduling, player availability, the Big Bash Leagues' salary caps, branding proposals as well as the reserve price for a licence to operate that must be achieved, and approval of investors."

The move to bring private investment into the Big Bash Leagues has been debated for months.

CA chief executive Todd Greenberg said in May that private investment was "inevitable", and privatisation was thrust into the spotlight when Cricket Victoria made plans to sell the Renegades in June.

Baird said inviting private investment would allow cricket to grow at every level of the game.

"Cricket Australia and its state members are united in our commitment to investing in and growing the BBL and WBBL, and to advancing the interests of cricket at every level," he said.

"By opening the door to private investment in the Big Bash Leagues, Cricket Australia is taking a deliberate step to strengthen and secure the long-term future of the game, accelerate growth and ensuring we can keep investing in community cricket and grassroots participation, domestic and international pathways and the elite level.

"This is a significant decision that has involved an enormous amount of analysis, discussion and collaboration over many months. I'd like to thank all involved as we move to what we believe is the best way to secure cricket's future in this country, strengthen the Big Bash and protect our standing on the global stage."

World.title: Lion turns down monster offer, premiership Bulldog calls time
World.content:
Brisbane Lions premiership hero Zac Bailey has re-signed with the reigning premiers, ending a long-running saga about whether he would move to Adelaide.

In an added subplot to this Saturday night's semifinal between the Lions and the Crows at the Gabba, Bailey has turned down a monster offer from Adelaide.

The restricted free agent has penned a new eight-year deal to remain with the Lions until the end of 2034.

A two-time All-Australian, Bailey has enjoyed another outstanding season with 31 goals and averaged a career-high 21.7 disposals.
